description: Edit 7/14/2026** Now Also check out “Big Chap” in a huge, detailed print!: https://makerworld.com/en/models/3052357-big-chap-alien-detailed-xenomorph-statue#profileId-3433924 & the other newly added detailed sculpture! https://makerworld.com/en/models/3056011-internecivus-raptus-alien-detailed-sculpture#profileId-3438404 Xenomorph (Alien) Ultra Detailed Display This one is by far one of my largest, and definitely the most detailed model that I've worked on to date.. This is an Ultra Detailed Xenomorph statue that stands 19 inches (48cm) tall in the largest form! This statue pulls inspiration from the unbelievably awesome Sideshow Collectibles Vinyl model, which if you are familiar with their models, are next level in detail.. but next to impossible to get! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 19" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 19" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 19" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. I had 4 machines running test prints none stop. I promise though, it is worth it at the end. **Please also be aware that the model images you see are 100% real, with 0 use of AI, but they have been post-process colored using some Rub'n Buff waxes, along with some gloss clear coat layer application at the end. ASSEMBLY REQUIRED ** The 19" tall, multipiece print will require some glue. I have used both super glue, as well as hot glue. Hot glue was my preference. With all the parts printed, and supports cleaned up (TAKE YOUR TIME REMOVING THE SUPPORTS AS THE PARTS ARE HIGHLY DETAILED AND FRAGILE ) do a dry-fit of all the parts to ensure proper fitment. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. Assembly is very straightfoward, with the exception of the tail. DO NOT mount the tail to the model until the Xenomoprh is placed onto the base display. The tail loops around the display and needs to be installed afterwards. Install the tail by turning is 90 degrees and carefully looping the tip around the back of the base and then gently rotating it up into the reciever cutout on he back of the xenomorph (Yes, it looks like a butt ). With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process, you can assemble everything together, just leave the tail to the end. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting peg as well as some glue to the toes of the left foot (there is no peg here) and firmly place the model on to the base. Proceed with snaking the tail into position, and then apply some glue onto the peg of the base of the tail. There is a small mounting support for the tail at the back of the base that also requires a small application of glue to help it from bouncing around with the model fully assembled. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff Antique Gold wax for the Xenomorph, and Brass color for the base. Wear gloves and apply the wax to a towel and gently go over the details. Avoid pressing really hard so that the void remain black/dark, this helps with final contrast of the model. As you can tell from these two photos the difference between the plain model and the colored one is pretty phenomenal and I HIGHLY recommend going through the effort!

During testing, the Bambu filament consistently produced: Cleaner surface finish Better dimensional accuracy Less noticeable seams on glued joints More forgiving connector tolerances during assembly During testing, PLA KINGROON filament was printed using the standard textured build plate , while PLA Bambu filament was printed on the Bambu Grey Cool Plate . The Bambu filament provided a better balance of strength and fit, making assembly considerably easier and more reliable. I also printed these with a Bambu P2S and the heads using a H2C and X2D 🔧 Assembly Assembly is straightforward using the keyed connectors. description: In Book Five of the Odyssey , Odysseus is finally within sight of home when the sea itself turns against him. Poseidon, the Earth-Shaker, the dark-maned lord of the deep has not forgotten that this man blinded his son, the Cyclops Polyphemus. So he gathers the clouds, takes up his trident, and calls every wind down onto a single raft. This is that moment made solid. Not a calm sea-king on a throne, but the god rising out of his own storm: the wave curling into a fist beneath him, the trident already lifted, the grudge that will keep a hero wandering for ten more years. Homer never lets us forget that the sea has a memory, and a temper. I wanted the base to carry that: the water isn't scenery, it's Poseidon's will taking shape. Sculpted as a single figure rising from a sculptural mass of sea, so the wave does the storytelling instead of a second character competing for the eye.

description: Ethereon – Der Geist von Sparta Nicht jeder Krieger findet nach seinem Tod Frieden. Einst war Ethereon einer der mächtigsten Spartaner seiner Zeit. Unzählige Schlachten kämpfte er für sein Volk, bis er schließlich auf dem Schlachtfeld fiel. Doch sein Wille war stärker als der Tod selbst. Die Legende erzählt, dass seine Seele von den Göttern zurückgerufen wurde, um über die gefallenen Helden zu wachen. Seitdem wandert Ethereon zwischen den Welten – halb Krieger, halb Geist. Sein zerfetzter Umhang weht in einem Wind, den niemand spüren kann, während sein Schild die Seelen der Gerechten beschützt und sein Schwert jene bestraft, die die Ehre verraten. Man sagt, wer ihm in einer dunklen Nacht begegnet, hört das ferne Echo marschierender Soldaten und das Klirren alter Waffen. Doch bevor man ihn erkennen kann, ist er bereits wieder im Nebel verschwunden. Ethereon ist kein Held und kein Monster. Er ist die letzte Wache Spartas. Beschreibung Ethereon – Der Geist von Sparta ist eine detailreiche Fantasy-Figur für den 3D-Druck. Das Design verbindet die klassische Erscheinung eines spartanischen Kriegers mit einer geisterhaften, mystischen Form. Fließende Energien, dynamische Bewegungen und zahlreiche Details machen das Modell zu einem echten Blickfang für Sammler, Tabletop-Fans und Liebhaber epischer Fantasy-Figuren. Druckhinweise Druckbar mit FDM- und Resin-Druckern. description: “Big Chap” (Alien) Ultra Detailed Sculpture Staying on the recent Xenomorph Theme, here is another absoutley awesome, and highly detailed, “Big Chap” Xenomorph Sculpture! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 18" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 19" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 19" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. I had 4 machines running test prints none stop. I promise though, it is worth it at the end. **Please also be aware that the model images you see are 100% real, with 0 use of AI, but they have been post-process colored using some Rub'n Buff waxes, 2-part epoxy resin, and then some gloss clear coat layer application at the end. ASSEMBLY REQUIRED ** Discard the small round cylinder that prints on the 2nd plate with the arms and foot. It is an uneeded part that was a result of slicing the model in the studio* The 19" tall, multipiece print will require some glue. I have used both super glue, as well as hot glue. Hot glue was my preference. With all the parts printed, and supports cleaned up (TAKE YOUR TIME REMOVING THE SUPPORTS AS THE PARTS ARE HIGHLY DETAILED AND FRAGILE ) do a dry-fit of all the parts to ensure proper fitment. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting pegs and firmly place the model on to the base. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff Antique Gold wax for the Xenomorph, and Brass color for the base. Wear gloves and apply the wax to a towel and gently go over the details. Avoid pressing really hard so that the void remain black/dark, this helps with final contrast of the model. As you can tell from these two photos the difference between the plain model and the colored one is pretty phenomenal and I HIGHLY recommend going through the effort!

This project is a highly customizable 3D Car Profile Desk Sign. Create the perfect personalized gift for any car enthusiast by blending their name directly into the silhouette of a sleek car model. Fully parametric in OpenSCAD. ⚠️ BETA VERSION - COMMUNITY FEEDBACK NEEDED!⚠️ This is the beta release of our Car Sign generator. Due to the high level of customization, there are still several challenges regarding part positioning, support generation, and overall print optimization. We want to build this project together with the community and are actively looking for your feedback on: * Best printing orientation(laying flat vs standing up) * Support settings** (if needed for overhanging letters) * General optimizations to make printing easier Please leave a comment with your tips, pictures, and suggestions to help us improve the final version! --- CUSTOMIZATION --- Choose from 5 distinct car models and adjust sizes, thickness, and text spacing to create a completely unique desk piece. --- PARAMETER GUIDE --- 1. Size Selection - Médio (Medium): 97x20x35 mm - The perfect balanced size for shelves and desk displays. - Grande (Large): 145x30x50 mm - A striking centerpiece for a desk or garage. 2. Car Settings & Base - Car Model: Choose between Sedan, Hatchback (Default), Retro Muscle, Supercar, or Original Sports Car. - Solid Base (Use_Solid_Base): **Enabled by default!** Adds a solid backing plate behind the letters in the exact shape of the car profile. This greatly improves structural rigidity, prevents fragile letters from snapping, and makes the side-profile look stunning. You can adjust the base thickness. - Flip Car (Flip_Car_Horizontally): Mirrors the car horizontally so the front points the other way, ensuring it flows perfectly with your chosen name. 3. Text Customization - Name / Text: Type any name or word (Default: "TESLA"). - Font Style: Currently locked to a robust, bold font (*Courier New Bold*) that works exceptionally well for 3D printing and Boolean intersections. - Letter Spacing & Thickness: Adjust how close the letters sit (Default: 0.85) and add extra boldness (Default: 1.2) if needed for better fusion. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS --- - Flawless Geometry: The model uses an advanced OpenSCAD boolean intersection technique to guarantee a 100% solid, gap-free model (manifold) that imports perfectly into your slicer without errors. - Smooth Vector Curves: The car profiles have been algorithmically smoothed to completely eliminate jagged pixel-stepped edges. --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- Depending on your chosen car model and specific letter combination, you might need to adapt your slicing approach. Here are some potential strategies you can use to reduce supports and improve print quality: - Orientation: Rotate the part in the X and Y axes on your build plate. Finding the perfect angle depending on your specific car model and letter combination can drastically reduce overhangs! - Supports: Enable supports only for critical areas. - Layer Height: Use Variable Layer Height. This keeps print times low while creating perfectly smooth curves on the car's roof and hood. - Top Surface Pattern: Rectilinear. - Ironing: Test Enabled (Topmost surface only) for a perfectly smooth finish on the front face of the letters. - Wall Generator: Arachne (Crucial for sharp letter details). - Outer Wall Speed: Reduce the speed of the outer walls to ensure a flawless, premium surface finish. - Infill: 10% Gyroid.

Cookie Monster Godzilla "Cookie Blast" Edition "Cookie...zilla breathes cookies!" What happens when Cookie Monster Godzilla unleashes his ultimate attack? You get the Cookie Monster Godzilla "Cookie Blast" Edition! Instead of a traditional monster breath attack, this version features Cookie Monster Godzilla standing on a detailed base while blasting a stream of cookie dough from his mouth. Some might call it a cookie-powered attack... others might say it looks like he's having a bit of a cookie-related incident. Either way, it's a hilarious and unique addition to any monster, cookie, or 3D printing collection. The model includes a custom base designed to add stability, along with a detailed flowing "cookie flame" effect that gives this version a completely different look from the original Cookie Monster Godzilla Duck. Design Process This model was created using a hybrid workflow of AI-assisted generation and traditional 3D modeling. I began with an original mashup concept, then used AI-assisted tools to explore different forms and proportions. After selecting the strongest base design, I refined the model to improve the details, clean up geometry, and optimize it for reliable FDM printing. Print Settings Layer Height: 0.20 mm Infill: 15% Gyroid Supports: Tree Supports (required) AMS Required: Yes Base Modifier A modifier is included that increases part of the base to 30% infill . This adds extra weight to the bottom of the print and helps prevent the model from becoming top-heavy and tipping over. Color Changes This print uses 6 colors and requires two pauses for filament swaps . The pauses are already in the file, but be sure to check that after slicing. If you change the size for a larger or smaller printer, you'll need to change the pauses. Layer 350: Swap Gray for Light Brown Layer 949: Swap Black for Dark Brown Filaments Used Anycubic PLA+ Black Anycubic PLA+ White Kingroon Blue PLA Kingroon Light Brown PLA Elegoo PLA+ Gray Sunlu PLA+ Coffee Brown Post-Processing Notes Support removal on this model can be a little challenging. The area underneath the tail can be difficult to access when removing supports, so take your time and be careful. The cookie drips at the very top of the "cookie fire" effect are also extremely delicate and can break during cleanup. I broke a few of mine during testing, but thankfully they were fairly easy to repair. Small pieces can usually be reattached with glue or bonded back together by carefully heating the plastic. If one of the cookie drips breaks off and you don't want to repair it, remember... it's a melting cookie! You can carefully heat the broken end slightly to soften it and let it resolidify into a natural-looking melted edge. The entire cookie flame effect is fairly fragile, so handle it carefully after printing. Notes for Future Versions I may create a larger version of this model in the future that separates at least part of the cookie flame effect into an assembly piece. This would make the effect more durable while also allowing for an even larger and more detailed version. Print Testing I always print my models before releasing them so I can make sure they actually work and look good in real life. Most of the time, I start with a simple single-color test print first. That lets me check the overall geometry, supports, and printability without burning a ton of filament. If everything comes out clean, I'll move on to the full multicolor AMS version. My prototyping and testing setup includes two Bambu Lab P1S printers and two Snapmaker U1 printers , which lets me quickly iterate between test prints and full-color versions depending on what I'm working on. That said, if I'm already confident in the design—usually from similar prints or earlier versions—I might skip straight to the multicolor print. “The Odyssey - Achilles” I have wanted to recreate and color my take on Achilles from The Odyssey for quite some time.. and figured what better time than when the contest is ongoing? This is a 20" tall, highly detailed, multi-piece print. Please note that the print profile is SINGLE COLOR ONLY. The coloring of the model was achieved in post-process application of coloring wax, as well as acrylic paints applied via air brush. This is not your typical AI colored model, this is truly what this could look like! I only spent 30 minutes on mine! The model prints in several pieces in order to maximize the build volumes of the P and X series machines. Some gluing is required. ASSEMBLY Assembly of the model is very straightfoward - first glue the upper torso to the lower body, and then test fit the arms. The arms stay in place pretty good, and I highly recommend waiting to glue the arms/shield on until after you're doing with painting just so you can have better access. Once the modle is painted, just add a drop of glue on each joing and press them into place. Wait to glue the arrows into their respective holes until the end of the process. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff waxes - Antique Gold, Copper, Brass, etc. Below is an example of this application process on my Alien model I posted earlier. I simply use a microfiber towel, wear gloves, dab a bit of the Rub'n Buff (I buy mine on amazon) and lightly spread it on the model. For this particular model I could have stopped at the first Bronze look.. but I decided to try out some acrylic paints and see what I can do to really bring it to life. After about 20 minutes of spraying this was the end result! I use really cheap, hobby store acrylic paints that are water based. I dilute them with distilled water to make them sprayable. Clean up is a breeze, and so far I have been loving the color effects. As a finishing step, I applied to Matte Clear Coat to the model. The Before and After really give you a good idea of just a little added effort can REALLY make for an awesome print!

description: Stormwing – Windswept Owl Sculpture The idea behind Stormwing came from my fascination with driftwood sculptures and how nature and time shape everything they touch. I wanted a model that looks like raw power and motion, which lead to this windswept owl—an animal pushing forward while almost getting torn apart. The current height of the sculpture is ~ 16 cm (~6.3 in) in height. I would not print it smaller as the thin edges would become rather thin and increase the risk of not forming as it should. For the easiest support removal, keep the model in the provided vertical position. This helps reduce the amount of support required and makes the supports as manageable as possible to remove. Printing Use a clean print plate with some glue (unless you are using a super tack plate) Use dried out filament (Different filament and printers impacts the print differently, please adjust your settings accordingly.) Keep the model in the provided vertical position Support Removal Instructions Allow the print to cool completely before removing it from the build plate. Use small flush cutters, needle-nose pliers, and tweezers to remove the support branches in smaller pieces. Support removal will take a little bit of time. Patience and careful handling are important for protecting the thin driftwood details. Be especially careful around the talons of the owl. Start by removing the larger support sections around the base and outside edges. Break the smaller branches into smaller sections and alternate around each supported section as needed. I needed to alternate between the front and backside as some of the support was built up from both sides for the same section. After removing the supports, clean up potential rough contact points with a precision knife, small file, or fine-grit sandpaper if needed. Light sanding and gentle, controlled heat may be needed to clean up areas where the supports were attached. I used a handheld mini torch, but apply heat carefully to avoid warping or damaging the print. Wood PLA is very sensitive to heat! description: Carved Walnut Parlor Suite VEF-SUITE-0053 1:12 How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model To Change the Scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊 [End]

description: Rococo Chair & Setee VEF-CHR-0035 1:12 Dollhouse How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Download it Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊

description: Victorian Cottage 6 Drawer Dress VEF-DRS-0036 1:12 How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model For those of you who want the model but in a different scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊 [End]

description: Chinese Rosewood-inspired Storage Chest – 1:12 Scale A detailed 1:12 scale Chinese rosewood-inspired storage chest designed as a functional miniature furniture piece. This ornate chest features an opening lid with a working captured hinge and two separate functional sliding drawers. It is well suited for dollhouse interiors, historical room scenes, miniature displays, and collector showcases. The model is supplied as three separate STL files: One chest frame with its integrated captured hinged lid Two individual sliding drawers Printing Notes The chest frame and lid print together as a permanently captured assembly. The hinge components capture one another during printing; the lid cannot—and should not—be separated from the chest afterward. Before attempting to open the lid fully, carefully inspect the hinge area. A small amount of adjoining filament may need to be cut away from between the male and female hinge surfaces. Use the tip of a sharp hobby or X-Acto knife carefully, removing only the unwanted filament. Once cleared, gently work the lid through small movements until the hinge operates freely. Do not force the lid open, as excessive pressure may damage the printed hinge. The original model measures: 60 mm W × 65 mm D × 100 mm H Reducing the model size will also reduce the hinge clearances. Smaller prints will require more careful hinge cleanup and release before the lid can move freely. With its decorative detailing, functional drawers, and opening upper compartment, this chest makes an attractive feature piece for miniature bedrooms, studies, period-inspired interiors, and display collections. How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model For those of you who want the model but in a different scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊

description: F1 - Redbull Racing RB20 - 1/12 Scale model! Next on my list is this my take on Redbull's RB20 F1 Car done in 1/12 scale! The main idea behind this model was to try and (finally) make a model with some spinning wheels. I had a bunch of 608 bearings from an old project and models this size/wheels around it. The car body is split into 3 pieces to fit the X/P series machines. The wheels and wheel covers print separately. Gluing is required. Size This is a 1/12th scale model Assembly Assembly is straightfoward. The body of the car has hex pegs and needs to be glued. I use Contact Adhesive but any glue will work. The only thing to watchout for is to make sure that your body is perfectly aligned, or your wheels won't sit square across all 4 corners. While the body is drying, take your 608 bearings and press them into the wheel/tire. With that done, install the wheels onto the body (paying attention to which is the front and rear) by pressing the bearing onto the stub shaft. The fit should be somewhat snug, but not too tight. If you are having issues sliding the wheel on, I recommed sanding the wheel stud around just a bit to smooth it out. With the wheels pressed onto the body, proceed to install the retainer washer by pressing it onto the shaft. Don't press it too tight against the wheel or it will prevent free wheel spin. If you want added assurance that this stays in place, you can add a dab of glue to the washer/stubshaft, but it will make it impossible to remove later. With the wheel retainers installed, proceed to press in the covers (again paying attention to the front/rear as they are different). You're done! Only thing left is to paint it you want to go an extra step!

model_name: The Nostos Compass: Homer's Epic Secret Box
description: The Nostos Compass: Homer's Epic Secret Box Un omaggio stampabile in 3D al viaggio epico di Ulisse. Un tempo concepita come una bussola concettuale per trovare la via di casa, questa complessa scultura architettonica nasconde al suo interno un vano segreto. Perfetta come stash box da scrivania o come pezzo da collezione per gli amanti della mitologia e del design classico. La Storia dietro il Design L'Odissea di Omero non è solo una storia di mostri e divinità, ma il racconto della più grande forza umana: il desiderio di tornare a casa ( Nostos ). Questa bussola scultorea è stata progettata per incarnare quel lungo viaggio. Il corpo esagonale della bussola è un susseguirsi di pannelli architettonici separati da colonne classiche, su cui sono incise in altorilievo le iconografie delle tappe fondamentali del viaggio di Ulisse. La corona superiore, finemente decorata con un pattern a onde che richiama le sfide di Poseidone, è ispirata alle complesse geometrie concentriche dei rosoni dell'architettura barocca del Sud Italia (Rosone della basilica di Santa Croce, Lecce, Puglia). Non è solo un oggetto da esposizione: sollevando il coperchio superiore a incastro, la bussola rivela uno scompartimento vuoto, ideale per custodire dadi per giochi di ruolo, gioielli, chiavi o piccoli oggetti preziosi. Caratteristiche Principali Design Modulare e Funzionale: Il modello è composto da un corpo principale e da un coperchio (il rosone della bussola). L'assemblaggio avviene in maniera fluida grazie a tre spine di centraggio interne progettate con tolleranze perfette per l'incastro. Nessun Supporto Necessario: Grazie a uno studio accurato in fase di Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) , tutti gli sbalzi e le geometrie complesse (inclusi i dettagli in altorilievo) si stampano in modo impeccabile senza l'ausilio di alcun supporto. Dettagli ad Alta Risoluzione: La rosa dei venti e le texture laterali sono studiate per risaltare al massimo sia con i classici PLA opachi, sia con filamenti materici (come PLA caricato legno o pietra), che donano all'oggetto un aspetto da vero reperto archeologico. Istruzioni di Stampa Il modello è stato ottimizzato per garantire una stampa semplice, pulita e alla portata di tutti, senza sprechi di materiale. Risoluzione Consigliata: Altezza layer 0.16 mm (profilo high quality ) per un ottimo bilanciamento tra velocità e resa dei dettagli (è possibile utilizzare anche il profilo standard con altezza layer 0.20 mm). Riempimento: 15% - 20% (pattern a griglia o giroide). Supporti: Disabilitati. Il design è 100% print-in-place / support-free . Adesione al piatto: Nessun brim richiesto. Assemblaggio: Stampa il corpo, il coperchio superiore e le 3 spine di centraggio. Inserisci le spine negli appositi fori sul corpo esagonale per creare le guide di incastro per il coperchio. Per i tasselli, incollare al corpo della bussola i 6 blocchetti di centraggio e successivamente, incollare a loro volta i 6 tasselli nelle loro sedi.

Originally introduced as an oversized piñata that players break open with a pickaxe to claim massive caches of ammo, materials, and healing items, it has become one of the most recognizable icons in modern gaming culture. About the process and Print Profile : There are 3 plates depending on your needs and 3d printer set up: AMS facing up : this is the Logo with the text facing up ("looking" at the top of the printer). You need to use this with 2 colors on the AMS. AMS facing down : this is the Logo with the text facing down on your build plate if you want to get the plate texture. You need to use 2 colors on the AMS. No AMS : if you are just like me, and you don't have an AMS yet, you have to use this plate. The process is simple but a bit manual, you have to: chose the position of all objects and never change it again during the process (make sure that you choose a position where the nozzle does not touch the build plate during the start up process), for each of the colors that you want to use, you're going to have to do a “new” print, without removing the previously printed objects: enable each of the same color objects to print (eg all the parts that you want to be gold) and disable the rest of the colors (Process > objects > No AMS Plate > check/uncheck given the color). Print that, when that print ends, manually set up the build plate temperature to prevent the print from ungluing from the plate, remove everything that got printed on the startup process except the actual Logo objects (eg: skirt, nozzle cleaning line, etc), enable a new set of objects of the same colors (and disable the one you just printed) and change the external spool in your 3d printer to that new color you're going to print, eg red repeat the process with all the colors, make sure that the last one is the background one, in this printed example the last one would be white background . NEVER EVER THINK ABOUT TOUCHING OR REMOVING THE BUILD PLATE UNTIL YOU PRINT ALL COLORS!!! Enjoy your multi-color print without AMS! In this particular case, I recommend the following order for the colors: gold > red. I found out that if I did white first, then the blue would unglue the white parts, so this is the order that worked for me. If any of the small parts get unglued, don't get discouraged! you can choose only that object in a new print and re print just that, without needing to start over! I know it's a pretty laborious process and seems hard at first, but feel free to reach out if you have any questions! Once you get the hang of it, it becomes easier and makes your prints more versatile! If you liked this print and process, follow my profile to find out more about my designs. Proceed with extreme patience and follow this exact extraction sequence to prevent accidental breakage. 🚫 Golden Rule: Always snip contact tips with fine flush cutters and pull support branches DOWNWARD , never outward or toward yourself, to avoid applying snapping leverage against the thin bone connections. 🌾 Step 1 - The Scythe & Blade: Begin by freeing the top rune-engraved scythe blade and the upper hand grip. description: 2" Virgin Mary Concrete Casting Mold Create a beautiful, 12-inch tall statue of the Virgin Mary with this custom-designed, multi-part 3D printable mold. This project is designed for those who enjoy the challenge of high-quality concrete casting and want to produce professional-looking results at home. Project Overview This mold is comprised of 8 distinct parts, engineered to lock together to create a seamless casting cavity. The intricate details on the inner faces are designed to capture the delicate features and flowing fabric textures of the statue perfectly. Instructions for Casting The process for using this mold requires patience and attention to detail: Printing: Print all 8 segments of the mold. For the best results, I recommend using SUNLU PLA+ Filament , which provides the durability and surface finish needed for intricate molds. Assembly: Connect the printed parts using clips and rubber bands to ensure they are held tightly in place during the pour. No glue is required for this assembly. Concrete Preparation: Select a high-quality concrete mix. Crucially, you must sift out ALL large rocks from the mix to ensure a smooth, detailed surface. Pouring: Add water according to the manufacturer’s instructions and carefully fill the assembled mold. Setting: Allow the concrete to set for the full recommended time specified by the manufacturer. Removal: Once set, place the mold in an oven at a low temperature to slowly and carefully melt the 3D-printed pieces away, revealing your finished statue. Remixing and Applications This design can be adapted for various purposes beyond religious decor: Garden Art: Scale up or down for custom garden accents. Custom Plaster Casting: Use the same mold with plaster of Paris for indoor display pieces. Abstract Sculpture: The modular nature of the 8-part system allows for creative re-orientation to produce abstract, geometric concrete art. description: 用 AI 做了一个透光浮雕折扇生成器～✨ 上传图片，简单调整位置和浮雕参数，就可以一键生成适合 3D 打印的透光浮雕折扇模型。 打印完成后，普通状态下可以看到扇面上的浮雕纹理；放到灯光前，图片会通过不同厚度呈现出丰富的明暗层次，形成漂亮的透光浮雕效果。 现在支持 三种折扇形状 ，整图铺满模式还支持 一次上传多张图片 ，可以自由调整每张图片的位置、大小、旋转角度和图层顺序，并自动适配折扇展开后的扇形结构，让制作更加简单、自由。 不需要自己建立浮雕，也不用手动把图片拆分成十几片扇页，更适合第一次制作透光浮雕折扇的新手使用。 📥 下载链接 （可以私信我获得，看到就会给。目前因为格式问题无法上传，MakerWorld 后续可能会更新。可以的话，不妨送我一张助力券💖） ⚡ 三步上手 1️⃣ 选择图片上传方式（单页上传 / 整图铺满） 2️⃣ 调整图片位置、缩放、图层及透光浮雕参数 3️⃣ 导出模型，放入 Bambu Studio 切片打印 第一次使用建议先生成并打印一片扇页，确认透光效果后，再打印完整折扇。 推荐耗材： 玉石白 PLA 🎨 单页上传 单页上传适合给某一片扇页单独添加图片。 可以分别选择扇页，并为每一片设置不同的图案，例如： 每片扇页放置不同文字 制作连续排列的小图案 单独调整某一片扇页 测试图片的透光浮雕效果 制作不同内容组合的折扇 上传图片后，可以调整图案在当前扇页中的位置、大小和旋转角度。 这种方式自由度更高，更适合想单独设计每一片扇页的用户。 🖼️ 整图铺满 整图铺满适合制作一张横跨整把折扇的完整画面。 新版支持一次上传 一张或多张图片 。 导入多张图片后，每张图片都会作为独立图层，可以分别调整： 图片位置 图片大小 图片旋转 图层前后顺序 多张图片上传 单张图片上传 图层调整 人物、文字、Logo、贴纸等素材都可以自由组合，轻松完成属于自己的折扇设计。 折扇完全展开后，多片扇页会共同组成一幅完整图案。 适合制作： 人物照片 动漫图片 风景图片 国风画面 插画 线稿 多人物拼图 Logo 与文字组合 无需自己裁切十几张图片，也不用逐片计算位置，生成器会自动完成图片分配。 🪄 图片自动适应扇形 普通图片都是矩形，而折扇展开后属于放射状结构。 如果直接平均切开图片，容易出现： 图片左右衔接不上 人物和图案发生变形 扇页之间出现明显断层 中间画面正常，两侧画面被拉伸 折扇展开后整体构图不自然 因此生成器加入了 图片自动适应扇形 功能。 上传图片后，程序会自动根据折扇展开结构，对画面进行适配，再分配到不同扇页。 整个流程可以理解为： 上传图片 → 自动适应折扇形状 → 自动分配到各扇页 这样折扇打开以后，画面能够更加自然地围绕中心展开，人物、建筑和风景也能保持更好的整体效果。 图片自动适应扇形 🪭 三种折扇形状 生成器目前提供三种不同风格的折扇形状。 不同形状适合不同类型的图片，可以根据人物、动漫、风景或国风作品自由选择，更容易获得理想的排版效果。 切换扇形后，所有图片都会自动重新适配对应的折扇结构，无需重新排版。 扇子甲 扇子乙 扇子丙 ✨ 透光浮雕效果 生成器会根据图片的明暗关系，自动生成不同厚度的浮雕结构。 打印完成后： 较薄的位置透光更多 较厚的位置透光更少 普通光线下可以看到浮雕纹理 放到灯光前可以显示图片明暗层次 建议选择主体清晰、明暗对比明显的图片，最终的透光浮雕效果会更加明显。 人物照片可以提前适当提高对比度，避免面部层次过于平淡 🙏 模型来源说明 本工具内置的所有扇子骨架，使用了开源大佬 @安迪圣剑 分享的折扇骨架模型。 我在原有骨架模型的基础上，增加了： 图片上传与处理 单页图片设置 整页图片分配 横向图片弯折 扇页自动分割 透光浮雕生成 模型导出功能 感谢 @安迪圣剑 的开源分享与创作。 工具仍在持续优化中，欢迎大家在 MakerWorld 上传自己的打印作品，也欢迎在评论区反馈使用过程中遇到的问题。 觉得工具有用的话，可以帮忙点赞、收藏或送上一张助力券。大家的支持可以让我继续维护生成器，也能继续开发更多适合3D打印的小工具～💖

Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: Hey guys! :) Are you looking for a cool print to level up your Victorian/Steampunk costumes? Do you wish to bring a little bit of your “Maker” personality to your RP character for DnDs, renfaires, and festivals? Well, then this one is especially for you! :D This model is very close to my heart. :)) Not only did I LOVE creating it and fusing every aesthetic I enjoy into one model, but now I can cosplay as like.. myself? But like a cooler version of myself in a fantasy setting? YES. 💅🏼✨ 📌What do you need to know? (Before printing) This is a multipart design, with two separate frame looks that you can choose between. One of the frames has a clean/industrial steampunk look, and the other has a more ornate Victorian look with foliage patterns. Both frames are included in the design profile on separate plates. I designed the assembly first for compatibility with laser-cut 3 mm PMMA (acrylic) lenses, but then I decided to make it more accessible to everyone by including an FDM-printable version of the lenses. So you can print this full design even without laser cutting. Just keep in mind that the FDM version is mostly a prop for wearing overhead, since I personally couldn't see anything behind the printed lenses. :D Also, these goggles are gigantic by design. :D Please don't scale them up or down, by doing that the assembly won't be possible anymore. 📌What about additional components? I put the DXF file for the laser-cut acrylic lenses in this model if you'd like to cut your own see-through lenses. You can find them under the “Download STL/CAD files” section. For the forehead lights, I used mini battery-powered LEDs of 10x15 mm (Dxh). You can see an example here . Although I didn't include them yet in my versions, the movable mechanical assembly on the side is there to integrate a magnifying lens with a diameter of 20 mm into your glasses if you want. You can see an example here . 📌Print notes: Since this design has several print plates and objects with various settings, I suggest you open the 3MF directly in Bambu Studio and check out the requirements for each group of objects. 📌Post-printing and assembly: This design requires only minimal support, and most of the clean-up is for the brims (since there are quite a few small and separate components). However, there is a small “bridge” that you'll need to clean up before the assembly. Push it open with a hot or sharp tool to have access to the back of your LED and printed insert, so you can push them out from behind if needed. After cleaning, assembling the goggles is quite straightforward. You won't need any glue or additional joining components. Here are some additional guides. I really like that you enjoy this design as much as I did, and happy printing! :) 🥂✨

description: This is my original concept and design. Personal use only unless purchased from my website: www.themakerseditco.com OR subscribing on MakerWorld. This interchangeable badge reel system was designed so you could easily swap out badge reel toppers by simply attaching a new lid with a glued on topper. The lid is thin and prints very quickly. Note: Make sure to align topper on lid properly. Glue-On Versions: I have designed 2 versions: The twist & lock version is best for PETG or ASA . PLA will fail with this design because the part that keeps it locked in will wear down quickly. This design requires a bit of force to lock the topper in place. Because of this, you will most likely need to glue the badge reel topper design on the lid before trying to twist it on the base. This design has been extensively tested. It 100% works, but it is a tight fit. If it does not “click” into place, you have not gotten it all the way on. I have inlcuded a looser fit base for anyone having issues with the original base. This was my first design, but it can be difficult to use for some people. To make this interchangeable system easy to use for everyone, I created the threaded, screw on version. The threaded, screw-on versions works with PLA. I personally use Bambu Lab Basic PLA. There are alignment slots on this design. I recommend .12mm (High Quality) layer height and 4 wall loops. I cannot guarantee that the slots will align properly if you use different settings. Due to different printers and filament, there is a possibility that your slots won't line up perfectly, even with using my settings. I have included an option with no alignment slots. This design allows you to easily twist the lid on the base and then glue your topper on if that is easier for you. Badge Reel Cover: It fits standard badge reels that are no more than 33mm in diameter. This was intentionally designed to cover the entire badge reel and to not use magnets. This badge reel holder is 43.5mm in diameter and is better suited for jumbo badge reel toppers. Due to the diameter of this design, it works exceptionally well for jumbo badge reel toppers by helping it to sit flatter and not flop over as much.

Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: 🛍️ Trash Bag – L'eleganza nasce dove nessuno se l'aspetta Chi ha detto che il lusso debba seguire sempre le stesse regole? Trash Bag nasce proprio da questa provocazione: prendere qualcosa di estremamente semplice e quotidiano e trasformarlo in un accessorio capace di attirare ogni sguardo. È una borsa che gioca con i contrasti, mescolando ironia, design contemporaneo e raffinatezza in un oggetto unico. Le sue superfici sfaccettate ricordano un tessuto morbido che si è cristallizzato nel tempo, creando una geometria elegante e dinamica che cambia aspetto a seconda della luce. Il grande fiocco che funge da manico non è solo un dettaglio decorativo, ma il simbolo della sua personalità: romantica, femminile e audace allo stesso tempo. L'ispirazione arriva dalle linee sinuose del Liberty e dell' Art Nouveau , reinterpretate in chiave moderna attraverso la stampa 3D. Il risultato è una borsa dal carattere deciso, capace di sembrare una piccola opera d'arte più che un semplice accessorio. Che venga stampata in colori pastello delicati, in finiture opache, seta o perlati, Trash Bag cambia completamente personalità, diventando ogni volta un pezzo esclusivo. È perfetta per chi ama il design, la moda alternativa e gli oggetti che raccontano una storia. ✨ Design originale e fuori dagli schemi 🎀 Grande manico a forma di fiocco, elegante e scenografico ✨ Superficie geometrica ispirata agli origami e ai drappeggi della stoffa 💎 Perfetta come accessorio fashion, pezzo da collezione o elemento d'arredo moderno 🖨️ Progettata per valorizzare al massimo la stampa 3D con dettagli puliti e una finitura impeccabile Divertiti a personalizzarla con i tuoi filamenti preferiti: ogni colore le regalerà un'anima diversa. Dal rosa cipria al nero satinato, dal bianco perlato ai colori più vivaci... ogni Trash Bag sarà davvero unica. 📸 Hai stampato la tua versione? Pubblicala su MakerWorld ! Sono curioso di vedere le vostre combinazioni di colori, finiture e interpretazioni personali. 📖 La storia di Trash Bag La leggenda racconta che il primo prototipo nacque quasi per gioco. Un designer osservava un semplice sacchetto appoggiato sul tavolo del suo studio. Era stropicciato, imperfetto, destinato a essere buttato. Eppure, tra quelle pieghe casuali, vide qualcosa che nessun altro aveva notato: eleganza. Da quell'idea nacque una sfida. E se ciò che normalmente viene considerato banale potesse diventare qualcosa di prezioso? Così, piega dopo piega, curva dopo curva, quel concetto prese forma fino a trasformarsi in una borsa dal carattere inconfondibile. Il grande fiocco rappresenta il gesto finale: il momento in cui l'ordinario si veste di straordinario. Per questo Trash Bag non è solo una borsa. È un piccolo manifesto di creatività, un invito a guardare il mondo con occhi diversi e a trovare bellezza dove gli altri vedono soltanto normalità.

description: 水果主题便携折扇 安装说明视频： 配色说明： 创作灵感：复刻童年折扇回忆 作品取材于儿时经典层叠圆形纸折扇，依托3D打印技术重塑怀旧物件，赋予老折扇现代设计形态。 以水果横截面作为扇面核心视觉，结合扇子消暑的使用属性，借助热带水果清新甜美的气质，强化清爽氛围感，兼具实用性与创意趣味。 系列包含八款独立水果造型，自带专属图案，色彩搭配丰富，可匹配不同家居风格。 无AMS多色打印机也能制作单色版本 ，仅外观存在差异，功能性能完全相同。 手柄依照对应 水果特质定制专属纹理 ，每款握持手感各不相同； 指尖大小的开关按钮也采用水果造型 ，细节设计呼应整体主题。 机身尺寸适配大人与孩童握持，体积迷你可收纳进裤袋、包包。成品重量约50g，耗材仅60g，长时间手持不易疲惫。 扇体坚固耐用，开合手感顺滑，打印精度出众，参数经过优化，操作简单易上手。 整体全卡扣结构拼装，不用胶水与额外配件。 设计过程分享： 一开始做这把折扇，我以为弄懂结构就很容易成型，结果实操处处碰壁。 想要做出童年那种超小巧的扇子，可 FDM 机器精度有限，没法一味缩小尺寸。只能反复改模型，兼顾小巧体积、免胶卡扣组装和结构牢固度。 受打印平台限制放弃了方形扇面，改用圆形设计。加上水果图案后，打印纹路复杂，折叠很容易开裂，放射纹理的款式更是改了好几版才修好。 原本计划只做三款水果样式，越设计越觉得多款切面都很好看，一路追加到八款。全部利用下班业余时间，整整花了一个月才做完，难度远超预想。 期间还试了很多配色、不同品牌耗材，材质差异带来不少突发打印问题，都逐一调试解决。 这把小扇子耗费了不少心血反复打磨，喜欢的朋友不妨自行打印支持一下。谢谢！

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: One customizable OpenSCAD generator for everyday personalized tags: keychains, luggage tags, fridge magnets, screw plates, bin labels, door signs, and desk nameplates. Universal Personalized Tag Generator Pro expands a simple winning keychain label into a broader personal-label generator. Choose a mode, type your text, and generate a practical tag for keys, bags, storage bins, fridge notes, tool panels, doors, desks, and workshop organization. The first build includes seven fast MakerWorld-ready modes: `keychain` , `luggage_tag` , `fridge_magnet` , `screw_plate` , `bin_label` , `door_sign` , and `desk_nameplate` . Each mode has sensible default size, shape, text layout, and mounting, while manual overrides let you tune the width, height, thickness, shape, mount type, and text style. Mounting options include single ring hole, double ring holes, strap slot, blind magnet pockets, screw holes with counterbores, adhesive tape recess, and no-mount plates. The default text style uses raised lettering so color changes near the top layers are easy on a standard FDM printer. Optional text styles include engraved, recessed, and inlay-ready lettering for paint, resin, or filament-fill workflows. The desk nameplate mode prints as a simple support-free wedge with text on the sloped face. Customization Notes - Use `tag_mode` first, then leave `size_preset` , `mount_type` , `text_layout` , and `shape_style` on `mode_default` for a quick printable result. - Leave `color_style` on `raised` for the easiest two-color print with a filament swap near the top layers. - Use `inlay_ready` for deeper lettering pockets that can be filled after printing. - Use `fridge_magnet` or `magnet_pockets` for blind underside magnet pockets; glue magnets in after printing. - Use `screw_plate` or `door_sign` for screw holes with counterbores. - Use `back_side` for simple underside ID text such as phone number, serial number, property label, or emergency info. - Keep very long labels short or reduce the font size for narrow tags.

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: Create a whole custom bracelet bead set in one download. Enter up to 12 bead labels, choose cube, coin, or barrel beads, set the size and hole diameter, then pick raised or recessed lettering. Make personalized letter beads for friendship bracelets, craft projects, classroom name strings, zipper pulls, gift tags, and keychain accents. This parametric OpenSCAD generator creates a full batch of matching beads with adjustable size, thickness, stringing hole, and per-bead face lettering, so you can generate a complete name/word bracelet instead of downloading each letter as a separate file. Features: - Cube, coin, and barrel bead styles. - Adjustable bead size, thickness, bead count, and spacing. - Up to 12 separate label fields, one per bead. - Horizontal side-stringing hole by default for classic bracelet-bead layouts. - Optional vertical hole mode, offset below the letter, for name-string or tag layouts. - Raised or recessed label text. - Optional back-side label. - Rounded cube corners and optional barrel rib detail. - Cutaway preview mode for checking hole and label depth. The default prints a small `FRIEND` bracelet-bead set with horizontal side-stringing holes. The default 3 mm holes bridge cleanly on normal tuned printers, so it can print without supports while looking more like classic bracelet beads. For bracelet stringing, test your cord/elastic against `hole_diameter` ; different filaments and printers can make small holes tighter than expected. Safety note: these are small parts. Not for children under 3, and not for any use where broken or loose beads could become a choking hazard. Customization Notes - `bead_style` : choose cube, coin, or barrel. - `bead_count` : number of beads in the batch, up to 12. - `bead_size` / `bead_thickness` : bead face size and height. - `hole_diameter` : string/elastic hole size. Increase for fuzzy cord or printers that close small holes. - `hole_orientation` : horizontal is the default for classic side-stringing; vertical is available for top/bottom stringing or tag-style use. - `hole_y_offset` : moves the vertical hole away from the label when vertical mode is selected. - `label_1` through `label_12` : text for each bead. One letter per bead works best; short symbols or numbers also work. - `label_style` : raised lettering is easiest to see; recessed lettering gives a cleaner engraved look. - `show_back_label` : duplicates the label on the back face.

It features a delicate, lace-like pattern inspired by the beautiful silhouettes of orchids, making it a perfect accessory or a unique gift. 💡 The Concept & Credit This model is designed to be printed completely flat on your print bed and then shaped using hot water. While this is an original design made from scratch, the brilliant concept of using flat-printed patterns to thermoform bracelets was inspired by the work of @ G-ODA and their excellent Organic Wave Bracelet . I highly recommend checking out their work, which taught me this wonderful technique! 🛠️ How to Make It (Post-Processing Guide) Shaping the bracelet is incredibly easy and takes less than 2 minutes. Follow these simple steps: Print the file completely flat. Prepare hot water: Fill a mug or container with hot water. It doesn't need to be boiling, just hot enough to soften the plastic. Shape it: Carefully wrap the bracelet around the outside of the mug. 🖨️ Recommended Print Settings Material: PLA works perfectly for this technique as it softens at accessible temperatures. (The one in the photos is printed in Matte Olive Green). Layer Height: 0.16mm or 0.20mm for clean details. Bed Adhesion: A clean bed is recommended due to the detailed first layer. No brim needed. *** Images are actual photographed Prints. This is a fully 3D-printable eyewear design that you can print, finish, and assemble entirely at home. It requires no screws, hinges, or extra hardware—all you need is some super glue and a bit of post-processing to get a clean, functional pair of glasses. This model is designed to support standard and prescription lenses, making it both a stylish accessory and a practical daily wear option. For ordering lenses in the EU: I found Lens4Glasses to be an affordable option that ships across the EU. Important: Please ask your optician not to heat the frame when fitting the lenses. The frame is designed to fit the lenses without heating—and yes, they will deform your eyewear and send it back! 🙂 Key Features Two Sizes Included: Comes in two different sizes to help ensure a proper fit for different face shapes. Lens-Ready: Designed to accommodate both standard non-prescription lenses and prescription lenses. 100% Hardware-Free: No need to source tiny screws or specialized hinges. Easy Assembly: Simple joint design secured with a small amount of super glue. Recommended Print Settings To ensure the best surface finish and structural strength, the following settings are recommended: Layer Height: 0.10mm to 0.15mm (highly recommended for smoother curves and easier sanding) Infill: 40% – 50% Supports: Required. You will need to enable supports for the curved sections of the temples (the arms that go behind the ears). Material Compatibility This model has been tested with several filaments, and you can print it using almost any standard material: Bambu PLA-CF: Highly recommended. The carbon fiber texture provides a premium matte finish and excellent structural rigidity. Wood PLA: Gives a unique, organic aesthetic. It looks great but will require extra sanding and finishing to get a smooth feel. Standard PLA/PETG: Works well and offers a wide range of color choices. Assembly & Post-Processing Sanding: To achieve a comfortable fit and clean look, thoroughly sand the frames and temples. Start with a coarser grit (like 220) to smooth out print lines, and finish with a wet sand (400 to 1000 grit) for a smooth surface. Dry Fit: Test-fit the temples into the frame joints before applying any glue to ensure they align properly. Gluing: Apply a very small drop of super glue (cyanoacrylate) to the connection points. Hold the pieces firmly in place Lens Installation How to install: Standard scanned or custom-cut lenses can be snapped directly into the frame from the inside. Important Note: Do not apply heat (such as hot water or a hairdryer) to the frame during installation. Heating the plastic can cause the printed frame to warp or lose its shape. The lenses are designed to snap into place easily at room temperature.

Since this filament is tougher to melt, it requires a specific technique combining high heat and immediate pressure: Setup: Lay the t-shirt perfectly flat on a smooth, heat-resistant surface (like floor tiles). Placement: Position the main Haaland design, then carefully place the 2 or 3 small detached pieces that aren't connected to the rest. Protection: Cover the entire design with tightly stretched baking paper. Heating: Use a heat gun to melt the filament onto the fabric through the baking paper. Pressing (The key step): Immediately after heating, firmly press a wooden cutting board directly onto the hot baking paper to force the melted filament into the fabric mesh for a solid bond. ⚠️ Warning: Do not stay in one spot for too long with the heat gun! Heat evenly and keep moving, then press immediately to avoid deforming the plastic. 💡 Pro Tip: Which filament should you use? Standard PLA with a household iron (Possible, but not recommended): You can technically try using regular PLA with a standard iron (no steam) and baking paper, but the result isn't great. The plastic doesn't bond well to the fabric and tends to peel off easily. TPU Filament (The absolute best option): For the best results, we highly recommend using TPU (flexible filament) instead. It works beautifully with a regular household iron (no steam) . When heated, the TPU melts right into the fabric mesh, blending with the textile. This gives you maximum flexibility, a softer feel, and incredible longevity. 🧼 Care Instructions: To ensure your design lasts as long as possible, always wash the t-shirt at a low temperature and inside out .

This project is a premium parametric Cotton Pad Dispenser (Porta Algodão Dispensador) with a vertical U-shaped front slot. It allows you to load a stack of circular cotton pads from the top and easily pull pads out one-by-one from the bottom. Fully parametric in OpenSCAD, it features three standard capacities, optional screw-on lid configuration, and deep aesthetic customization. --- UNLIMITED CUSTOMIZATION --- With over 30 texture patterns and adjustable scales, this project offers hundreds of unique combinations for you to create an exclusive dispenser. --- PARAMETER GUIDE --- 1. Size & Capacity - Size Selection: Choose between three height capacities: - Small (P): Height 80mm (Holds approx. 20 cotton pads) - Medium (M): Height 120mm (Holds approx. 35 cotton pads) - Large (G): Height 160mm (Holds approx. 50 cotton pads) - Has_Lid: Option to include a screw-on lid. - Enabled (Yes): Adds a top thread to the base and exports the lid. - Disabled (No): Removes threads entirely, leaving a clean open-top dispenser with a smooth, rounded upper rim. 2. Dispenser Slot Settings - Cutout Width: Controls the width of the vertical dispensing slot (Default: 35mm). It is optimized to be wide enough for your fingers to easily pull a pad out, but narrow enough to keep the pads stacked securely inside. - Bottom Lip: Height of the bottom retaining wall that supports the stack (Default: 8mm). 3. Aesthetics and Texture - Surface Pattern: Applies geometric textures in high/low relief to the outer face (Default: Grid Diagonal). - Pattern Depth: Controls how pronounced the texture is (recommended: 0.6mm). - Pattern Scale: Adjusts the size of the texture tiles. Small variations in this scale dramatically transform the visual effect, essentially creating entirely new textures from a single base pattern. You can fine-tune the look from bold geometric shapes to fine, intricate details. Scale effects on the same pattern - Text Bands: Show customized text at the top (Default: "COTTON"). - Logo Patch: Creates a smooth, centralized area on the base for logos or custom labeling. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & PRINTING --- - Support-Free Design: Both the dispenser base and the lid print completely without supports. The bottom of the U-slot is a semi-circle that prints cleanly in mid-air, and the inside has straight 62.0mm cylinder walls to prevent soft cotton pads from catching or tearing. - Smart Lidless Finishes: When printing without a lid, the top edge of the dispenser is automatically detailed with a smooth, 1.0mm double-rounded rim (both inner and outer lips). This ensures that cotton pads don't snag when loading and the top is completely safe and pleasant to touch. - Perfect Thread Synchronization: When the lid is enabled, the metric threading system includes a hardcoded thread phase (angular offset). This guarantees that when you fully tighten the lid, the texture patterns on the lid and the base align flawlessly, even with the vertical slot cutout. --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- - Layer Height: 0.16mm (Optimal) - Wall Generator: Arachne (Required for sharp texture details) - Line Width: 0.6mm (Outer & Inner walls) - Infill: 10 Gyroid or Cross Hatch - Speed: 100 mm/s (Outer & Inner walls for premium finish) - Supports: No supports needed! description: A functional, aesthetic charging and display stand based around the Pebble Time 2! Includes an indent for the heart rate sensor and a non-slip TPU 95A foot. HARDWARE This project requires a couple things: Your Pebble magnetic charger. If you don't want to use the one that came with your watch, I have had luck with this one from Amazon . There are a few like this, but if you buy one without the USB C port make sure it has a thin (preferably flat), flexible cable. Right-angle USB-C adapter. If you don't use a charger with an attached cable, you will need one of these. Make sure it is slim. The fitment was modeled after one similar to these from Ugreen . USB-C cable, if you aren't using a charger with one attached. Just use one of the hundreds you have laying around at this point! 4x M3x25mm self-tapping screws. Mine came from this set . These are optional, but I like the look of screws instead of using glue and it's easier to take apart. PRINTING TIPS I have carefully painted supports, infill & walls on the included print profiles. There should be no need to tweak them. Ironing is enabled on the Pebble logo to look nice and smooth. This can be tweaked or disabled to your preference. If printing from the step files, note the following: The stand is best printed on its side so that the curves are smooth and the inset on the bottom is accurate. Ensure that your bridging is calibrated and well-tuned Ensure that the widest part of the stand at least is supported; tree supports can angle into the cavity about 10mm while remaining on the build plate and I found that to be sufficient Ensure that the inset at the bottom of the stand for the foot is supported; I had to paint on supports manually since the slicer kept wanting to print that as an overhang. The inlay side (pebble logo) of the watch holder should be printed face down and should not need supports - they're hard to remove. However, the cantilever for the heart rate sensor does need support. Print the stand and foot at 100% infill (or 1000 walls, your preference). This is to ensure they are weighty enough to offset the high weight when the watch is on the stand. Print the foot on a textured PEI plate if using TPU. I recommend 95A TPU or SEBS. The texture on the plate, when applied to the foot, greatly enhances grip. Assembly Print and Gather your parts Insert the charger (with right angle connector if applicable) into the cavity. There is an indent for the lanyard if you do not want to remove it. The lanyard can also be used to add some friction by sliding it underneath the magnetic charger. Plug the cord in and feed it through the cavity in the stand. Slide the stand onto the watch holder. Fitment is tight, so a small amount of force may be necessary. It may be easiest to slide the watch holder onto the stand, feeding the charger into the cavity as you do so. Secure 4x M3x25mm self-tapping screws into the four holes on the side of the stand. Screw them all the way in so their heads are flush to ensure that they have secured the holder to the stand. Click the logo inlay into place. It should not require glue, but a little dab does not hurt. Insert the foot into the inset in the bottom. The small peg should align to the small hole next to the cord cutout. Do not glue this in or the cord will be impossible to remove later. Fill your coffee!

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively.
