Powerful printable foam dart sniper pistol blaster capable of up to 250FPS These are alternative cosmetic parts for the Zinc .50, with a more aggressive, tactical design. This listing contains all parts needed for the Zinc .50, including unchanged ones. This listing includes new parts for the following Zinc .50 configurations: 160mm barrel compact front, 160mm barrel BCAR front, and 205mm barrel BCAR front. These parts require no hardware changes and so use the original hardware kit for the Zinc .50. See here for the original Zinc .50 model listing (check out all the amazing makes from everyone!). About the Zinc .50 blaster: Technically all standard Nerf darts are ‘50 caliber’ as the darts have a diameter of half an inch, though the Zinc .50 brings the essence of 50 caliber into foam dart hand-cannon format. The Zinc .50 is a high-powered, mag fed (7-13 dart capacity) foam dart springer pistol blaster capable of up to 250 feet-per-second muzzle velocity for 205mm barrel configurations, and up to 230 FPS for 160mm barrel configurations. If you have no reference for those velocities - don't hit your tv or it may break. It may also leave divots in your drywall. Everything You Need To Build Your Own Purchase a hardware kit: Hardware Kits can be found here. Discounted 'Duel Bundle' (2x Hardware Kits) for this blaster can be found here. Discounted 3-Blaster Hardware kit Bundle pack (Zc Aus, Znc Aus, Zinc .50) can be found here. The hardware kit can make any blaster configuration, just choose your barrel length! Affordable international shipping available, fast and tracked! Please note: Hardware kit sales support me in developing upcoming designs. They include several custom-machined parts, not just off-the-shelf parts. They are priced for an order frequency that I can keep fast dispatch times up with while also remaining competitive with similar kits. Download the print files, or Bambu Studio 3MF with all parts and preset settings (contains one of every part, remove unused parts for your configuration, duplicate parts as desired), from this model listing. Download the print and assembly guide here . Buy some half-length darts if you don't already own any, here are some links: US - Frontline Foam , OutOfDarts EU - Blaster Time AU - Blaster Tech Although the files include some printable tools to make assembly easier, you will also need some basic common tools for assembly, see the assembly guide linked above. Lubricant is included in the hardware kit. Demo Video Warning Note This blaster has a large spring with a somewhat heavy prime weight. Said spring may present danger if the blaster is not assembled, used, or cared for correctly. This is your responsibility. Information on correct assembly, use and care is provided in the assembly guide linked above. If you are looking for a blaster with a lighter prime and less powerful spring: check out the more compact Znc Aus / Znc Aus Cosmetic Part Variants , or even the ultra-compact Zc Aus . IMPORTANT NOTE - PRINT IN BRIGHT COLOURS Due to it's design this blaster must be printed in bright colours and with an orange tip so it is clearly visible as a toy, for your safety and other's. Use responsibly and in responsible settings. Details Textured Grip Note The textured grip shown on the frame part in the images is done with fuzzy skin fill-painting in the slicer. The grip sections are bordered by a small deboss which allows them to be easily fill-painted with the fuzzy skin fill-painting tool. The settings used for fuzzy skin in the blasters in the images are 0.18 thickness and 0.25 point distance. The Bambu Studio 3MF file already has the fuzzy skin set up with these settings. Variants A bearing scar (BCAR) uses rings of flanged bearings with each at a slight angle to impart spin on the dart as it exits the barrel, vastly increasing accuracy with little effect on fps. These new cosmetic parts for the Zinc .50 can make 3 total configurations (all shown in the cover image), two of which include a 9-bearing (3 rings) BCAR. The hardware kit can make any configuration, just choose your desired barrel length (all hardware kits come with 9x BCAR pins and bearings): 160mm barrel with a compact front (no BCAR) Up to 230FPS Not very accurate due to lack of BCAR but fun in that it's super powerful for it's size 160mm barrel with a 9 bearing BCAR Up to 230FPS Good balance of size and accuracy/power 205mm barrel with a 9 bearing BCAR Up to 250FPS Proper sniper pistol configuration, longer barrel for maximum FPS and BCAR for accuracy Zinc .50 Additions and Changes vs Ziiiinc and Zinc The Zinc .50 is based on the Ziiiinc by Misplaced Moose, and is modified and sold with his permission, though it includes many changes and upgrades including a slightly larger diameter plunger tube, a longer barrel, many customisable part options allowing for many different configurations, revised hardware, and modified/remodeled part designs and tolerances in the interest of performance, ease of assembly, and aesthetics. Hardware changes include a tighter-toleranced aluminum plunger tube over the original polycarbonate one, refined closed-end springs for all springs to fix issues of the original Zinc such as the stiff catch and weak mag release, double O-rings on all seals, lubricant oil included, tapping screws replacing machine screws with nuts (caused part splitting or the nuts would turn in place, making removal impossible), and more. See images for further details. Assembly Assembly is relatively straightforward. The assembly guide is detailed and includes troubleshooting steps for common issues. Unlike the original Zinc 2.0, no excessive sanding is required to get parts to fit and function. A dimensionally accurate printer such as a Prusa or Bambu model is recommended for easy assembly. See the print guide for printing tips. Care and Safety Print in bright colours and use in responsible locations/settings. Do not leave the blaster outside under sunlight or in a car that may get hot when not in use. Do not leave the blaster primed when not in use as this will fatigue the main spring and other parts. Use responsibly. Do not aim at eyes or face. Eye protection for skirmishing is essential. Not recommended for use by young children. Note Like the Ziiiinc, the Zinc .50 is an unofficial descendant of the Zinc 2.0 blaster by 118 Design.

model_name: Fractal magnetic base for the Insta360 Luna Ultra
description: Let's Make It! Think bold. FRACTAL BASE Insta360 Luna Ultra meets INNOVATION Behold, the most versatile base solution for the Luna Ultra! Design ready for injection molding process for scale up manufacturing. Sits on any surface thanks to its fractal Ball joint linkages. Artificial Leather (PU) lower+upper surfaces for maximum grip . Sticks to metal objects thanks to the built in magnets. How does it actually work? Clip the Luna Ultra on the tiltable upper base. Magnetically snap the upper base on the lower base and adjust the tilting angle manually. Place the assembly on the desired platform and apply gentle pressure to engulf the platform's surface geometry. The third and second level magnetic hemispheres rotate freely in the ball joint and get displaced due to the forces applied by the platform's surface geometry on them. As soon as all third level hemispheres contact the platform's surface, stop pressing down and perform manual adjustments to keep the Luna Ultra vertical and stable. References: This project was first inspired by the widely spread 3D printed 2 DOF (degrees of freedom) fractal vises using rotating hemispheres (attached with sliders). Moving to the 3rd dimension, a simpler solution was required. To simplify the task, magnets were used to attract and “attach” the hemispheres to their pods. The following research paper: The Fractal Hand-II: Reviving a Classic Mechanism for Contemporary Grasping Challenges . presents a similar idea but the model mentioned featured no ball joint mechanism and relied heavily on screws for rotation unlike the present uploaded model that uses magnets and spherical pods for attachment and rotation! This project is therefore far from a direct copy; rather, it represents a new vision that is “allegedly” a new invention. Membership For exclusive access to CAD models Components: Magnets arrangement in the base: Mounting guide: Install the 3rd level hemisphere magnets and glue the PU circles on top. Install the 2nd level hemisphere lower magnet and screw the bracket with 2 M2x4 self tapping screws into the lower 2nd level hemisphere half. Put the 3rd level hemispheres in the 2nd level pods to facilitate the placement of the 4 2x2 2nd level hemisphere magnets. Screw in top 2nd hemisphere half on the lower half. Apply all previous steps to the duplicates. Put the 2rd level hemispheres in the 1st level pods to facilitate the placement of the 2 12x2 1st level hemisphere magnets. Screw in top 1st hemisphere half on the lower half. Install the 1st level hemisphere's 12x2 magnet and hemisphere block. Screw the bottom 1st hemisphere half on the upper half. Screw the square block on the hemisphere adapter with 1 12x2 magnet. Finally assemble all magnetic parts together. Inspiration: The fractal magnetic ball joint contraption was further tested by installing it on a vise to prove the flexibility and versatility of the design! model_name: Tempest Putter - Low-Torque / Modular / High MOI
description: Tempest - A Modular 3D Printed Putter with Everything You Need Looking for a customizable putter without the price tag of today's premium designs? This project combines the flexibility of 3D printing with design features inspired by modern high-performance putters. The putter head is designed to incorporate removable weights, allowing the majority of the mass to be positioned around the perimeter. This increases the moment of inertia (MOI), helping improve stability on off-center strikes while reducing twisting through impact. One of the key features of this design is its modular construction. The shaft insert is a separate component that bolts into the main putter head, allowing different putter head designs to be swapped without needing to remove or reinstall the shaft. Simply remove a few screws, install a new head, and you're ready to go. The shaft insert has a lie angle of 74 degrees and a static loft angle of 3 degrees to match the feel of many center-shafted putters. The design of the head of the putter has been carefully made to ensure that the center of mass is aligned with the center of the face. It sits slightly in front of the center of the shaft, providing little torque when swinging. Therefore, the design of this putter naturally eliminates the majority of the torque that can open or close the face while putting. This can make it significantly easier to keep the face square at impact. To improve feel, the striking face is printed from TPU, providing a soft but responsive impact that closely resembles the insert faces found on many premium putters. Including the printed parts, added weights, screws, and epoxy, the total mass of the head of the putter is right around 320g. Features Large integrated putting alignment aids High-MOI perimeter-weighted design Center of Mass positioned to produce Low Torque when swinging Modular construction with interchangeable putter heads TPU face insert for a soft, responsive feel Removable shaft adapter secured with screws Designed for commonly available hardware and weights Inexpensive and creative alternative to traditional putters Hope you can have as much fun with this project as I did and get to give it a try out on course! For instructions, materials, and a list of parts to purchase/use, see the information below! Happy printing! Modular Design: Find other compatible putter heads here! Eclipse Putter - Low Torque / Modular / High MOI Striker Putter - A Center-Shafted Modular Putter Material Selection Body / Shaft Insert - PETG is recommended for outdoor use and to withstand higher temperatures while being relatively easy to print. Face Insert - TPU provides a soft yet confident feel when striking the ball. Assembly Be sure to read all the following steps before beginning assembly of your putter! The order in which some of these steps are taken is very important! Print all required components in your favorite colors. Be sure to print each component in its recommended material. Support removal. This step can be rather difficult due to the way the model must be printed, so my recommendation is to work from the outside inwards. I've used normal supports for the flat-bottomed sections to allow for each of the gaps for the weights to be cleared in a singular piece. Press the TPU face into the putter body. Secure it by using super glue or epoxy. Install the weights. All weights should sit flat within the head of the putter when installed correctly. A total of 30 individual 0.25oz weights are to be inserted, with 4 stacked near the face and 2 stacked in all other locations. While removing the film on the weights (making them stick) is recommended, it is not required for the putter to work great. Doing so may reduce noises heard when making contact with the ball slightly but will make it more difficult to remove the weights if interchanging putter heads. Prior to installing the bottom plate, it can be helpful to lay a layer of tape over the bottom plate and cut to size. This will reduce some noise made when putting. Install the bottom plate to the putter head at the 5 holes around the perimeter. Ensure that the side which features cutouts matching the position of the weights is facing the inserted weights. Use 5x M3 x 3/8" wood screws (link provided below for the ones used). Screws should only be hand tight, and do not over-tighten them! Cut down the putter shaft to your desired length (I cut mine down to 36in for my height). For a great step-by-step process to complete this, check out this YouTube video: How to Shorten a Putter with a Steel Shaft . Install the grip to your putter shaft. I recommend completing this step before installing the shaft adapter and putter head as there is less time to work and straighten out the grip in comparison. For a great guide to doing this, check out this other YouTube tutorial: How to Install a Putter Grip (jump to 3:00 in the video). Bolt the shaft adapter/insert into the putter head after sliding the shaft adapter into place from the top. Using 3x M3 x 3/8" wood screws, secure the bottom plate, main body, and adapter together through the bottom in the three central holes. Then, complete the installation by using one more screw in the hole near the top of the putter towards the back. Screws should only be hand tight, and do not over-tighten them! Epoxy the shaft into the adapter by applying epoxy to the shaft and sliding it in from the top. The epoxy which is suggested has a long working time which allows you to rotate the putter shaft so the the grip precisely lines up with its correct orientation. My recommendation for alignment of the grip is as follows: look down the shaft and line up the flat part of the grip with the line on top of the putter which is parallel to the direction of your stroke. Once aligned properly, wipe away any excess epoxy from the top of the putter. Let the putter sit overnight so that the epoxy can fully cure. Next step, rolling putts! Hardware & Non-Printed Parts Required Purchased Components: I've added direct links here so you can source everything needed. Shaft: 0.370in Tip Diameter Straight Stepless Putter Shaft ( Amazon Link ) - $29.95 Grip: Any putter grip should do, but the one seen in all images here is a SuperStroke Zenergy Tour 3.0 ( Amazon Link ) - $34.39 Weights: Important to uses these weights due to their exact size and 1/4oz weight ( Amazon Link ) - $6.99 Screws: M3 x 3/8" Wood Screws ( Amazon Link ) - $6.79 Required Tools/Adhesives: Links are provided in case you may need to get these. If you don't already have some of these, they are also great to have in general for a variety of projects. Epoxy: Simple JB Weld 2-Part Epoxy ( Amazon Link ) - $5.93 Steel Tube Cutter: I used a copper pipe cutter (although it worked, not recommended), but using a proper steel pipe cutter is advised if possible ( Amazon Link ) - $13.99 Total (For Required Components and Printed Parts): ~$80 USD Future Plans This modular platform was designed with expansion in mind. I plan to release additional interchangeable putter head designs that will all use the same shaft adapter, allowing you to experiment with different shapes and weight distributions without building an entirely new putter. If you build one, I'd love to see your make! Feel free to leave feedback or suggestions for future head designs. Happy printing, and good luck on the greens!

Here is my version of a DIY Loadcell handbrake. I see some bought handbrakes and diy brakes put the lever farther away from the hand and some placing the loadcell at an angle, needing additional parts for leverage. I wanted it to be a simple direct connection with the lever closest to me since I put it next to my wheelbase. The cost is around $25 depending on if you have somethings stuff already. The most expensive part is the loadcell that I found for $16. Printed parts 1 - Lever - 6 walls and 10% gyroid infill and it has held up well. 2 - Base - 6 walls and 10% gyroid infill and it has held up well. 3 - Lever Spacers - 4 walls and 10% gyroid infill. 4 - 8mm pin - 6 walls 5 - Arduino box - 3 walls 6 - Bushings - TPU - 4 walls and 10% infill 7 - 5mm rod guides (if you use springs larger than the spring I used then the rod can move around and touch the spring while in movement, I added example rod centering spacers (16mm and 20mm) to keep the rod centered. I used PLA plus filament except for the bushings that are TPU. If you are unsure, or you shift like the hulk or are using a filament at is not that strong you can increase the walls to 8, 10, 12 or just print at 100% infill. The bushings I printed with TPU, 4 walls 15% grid infill. You can play with this to change the feel of the last stage of the pull. BOM (purchased parts) 1 - 200kg Loadcell (Qty 1) . It's needs to be this one or have the same the dimensions and hole patterns as this one due to the center hole for the spring guide rod/screw. NA151 60kg 100kg 200kg Commitment To 15Days To Arrive, New ($16) 2 - M5 x 100mm screw (Spring guide rod) (Qty 1) - This is what I had lying around and the length worked out fine adjusting the TPU bushings size to make it fit together. If you use a longer or shorter screw you will need to adjust the bushings accordingly. 3 - 5mm Rod end ball joint - Right Thread SI5 5mm (Qty 1) 5mm6mm8mm10mm12mm Rod End Male/Female SA SI T/K POSA8 PHSA8 Ball Joint Metric Threaded Rod End Bearing - AliExpress 13 4 - M4 screw 25mm or longer (and M4 Nut) (Qty 1) - To connect Rod end to the lever. 5 - Springs (Qty 1)- I used a 40mm x 12mm x 10mm Red spring that I had lying around. You can change the spring to whatever you have available or play with different spring setups. You can use to two smaller springs with different strengths. Wider springs, softer, stiffer, wider bushings and print different TPU bushings (elastomers). You will need to adjust the lengths of the bushings accordingly as you change the length. 6 - Washers (Qty 4) - I used 5mm x 12mm since I had them. If you use wider (larger diameter springs then use wider washers/bushings to match). 7 - M6 x 45mm screws (full thread) (Qty 2) - to bolt the loadcell to the base. They can also be 35mm but 45mm is best to pass through the sensor completely. 8 - Arduino pro micro - New Pro Micro for arduino ATmega32U4 Module with 2 row pin header For Leonardo in stock . best quality - AliExpress 502 9 - HX711 board - I would use this one. 1-10pcs HX711 Weighing Sensor 24-bit A/D Conversion Adapter Load Cell Amplifier Board Weight Sensors - AliExpress 502 There are different hx711 board versions. I recommend this one. It is larger, so it is easier to work with also with the HX711 you need to change read frequency (rate) from 10hz to 80hzx (10hz is too slow to read the data we need). This particular purple board version has an area on the back you just slice the connection between two pads with a razor and it changes it to 80hz. 10 - M8 x 45mm screw and nut (Qty 1) (optional) - You can either print the 8mm pin I made for the lever or use a M8x45mm screw. The 3d pin has worked fine. Print the base as it is oriented in in the file, on the side face. That is to maximize the strength due the layer lines. Printing it standing up will make it weak and prone to break due to layer lines. Here is the Arduino code to upload: #include #include // HX711 pins #define LOADCELL_DOUT_PIN 3 #define LOADCELL_SCK_PIN 2 HX711 scale; // Change this after calibration - - I left this as is. float calibration_factor = -9000.0; // Adjustable max force (kg) to reach 100% float maxForce = 120.0; // You can change this but would leave it at 120. If set to 200 it requires a lot of force to reach max pull. // Non-linear curve strength (1.0 = linear, 2.0 = strong curve) - You can play with this to change the “feel” of the end range of pull. float curve = 1.8; // HID Joystick object Joystick_ Joystick(JOYSTICK_DEFAULT_REPORT_ID, JOYSTICK_TYPE_GAMEPAD, 0, 0, false, false, true, // Z-axis only false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false); void setup() { Serial.begin(9600); scale.begin(LOADCELL_DOUT_PIN, LOADCELL_SCK_PIN); scale.set_scale(calibration_factor); scale.tare(); Joystick.begin(); } void loop() { if (scale.is_ready()) { float weight = scale.get_units(5); if (weight < 0) weight = 0; // Limit to maxForce if (weight > maxForce) weight = maxForce; // Normalize 0–1 float normalized = weight / maxForce; // Apply non-linear curve float curved = pow(normalized, curve); // Convert to HID 0–1023 int joyValue = curved * 1023.0; if (joyValue < 0) joyValue = 0; if (joyValue > 1023) joyValue = 1023; Joystick.setZAxis(joyValue); Serial.print("Raw kg: "); Serial.print(weight); Serial.print(" | Normalized: "); Serial.print(normalized); Serial.print(" | Curved: "); Serial.print(curved); Serial.print(" | HID: "); Serial.println(joyValue); } delay(5); } Assembly: Insert loadcell from the bottom upwards into the base (it will be a snug fit). Make sure the arrow on the loadcell is pointing towards the rear. I made the hole placement randomly with no meaningful spacing for a particular rig. I just drilled new holes into the plate. Place the lever base on the area want it and bolt it down. I recommend using all 3 holes in the front since that is where it receives the most force. Then place the two M6x45mm screws to secure the load cell to the base. They can be M6x35mm minimum. I like 45mm so they enter the other end of the base for added distribution of force/support. Place a spacer, insert the pin, then the lever, push the pin, then place the other spacer and push the pin through. I made the spacers a tight fit very tight to keep the lever from wiggling. You could print the spacers 0.5 shorter to make it easier. insert with the 3d printed M8 pin or M8 screw. Place the 4mm M4 rod end into the lever and secure it with the M4 x 40mm screw and nut. Take the M5x100 screw and place: washer > spring > washer > bushing > washer. Then insert that into the into the loadcell in the direction of the arrow. Then on the other end place a washer > bushing > washer and screw it into the rod end that's in the lever already. Program the Arduino (I will not cover this as there is a ton of info/videos on this) Just make sure your Arduino IDE Software you add the library for : 1 - joystick.h 2 - hx711.h Arduino + HX711 wiring The hx711 5 pins that are color coded go to the same colors on the loadcell sensor wire. The loadcell sensor silver/clear wire goes the yellow (for ground/noise) hx711 - VCC to Pro micro pin 2 hx711 - CLk to Pro micro pin 3 hx711 - GND to Pro micro pin GND hx711 - DAT to Pro micro pin 3 (goes to pin 3 or others on this side at the loadcell is a digital not analog). Cut between the two pads marked as RATE on the rear of the HX711 to convert it to 80hz Take the soldered boards insert them into the box/housing. In case you want to remove the boards there are holes at the bottom if the box to push the boards up with a thin object. To remove the adrunio you will need to pull the small lip back that locks into place and push it up from the bottom. Connect it to your PC and start racing and braking. description: Soft Plastic Dice Bait Mold Make your own custom soft plastic dice baits with this mold! Dice baits have become a popular finesse choice because their compact shape and flowing skirt. This mold allows you to pour your own dice-style baits using recycled soft plastics. Instructions 1. Prepare the mold Apply a very light coat of petroleum jelly to the mold cavities and the top of the mold. Use only a small amount because too much can affect the finish of your bait. 2. Melt your soft plastics Cut old soft plastics into small pieces and place them in a heat-safe glass measuring cup. Heat until the plastic becomes completely smooth and runny. Using a larger amount of plastic helps it stay warm longer and makes pouring easier. 3. Clamp and pour Clamp the mold halves together securely. Slowly pour the melted plastic into the sprue until the cavity is completely filled. 4. Let it cool Allow the bait to cool for several minutes. As the plastic shrinks during cooling, you may need to add a bit more melted plastic to the sprue. 5. Trim the bait Once fully cooled, remove the bait from the mold and cut away any excess plastic with scissors. 6. install the skirt Using either a bobbin threader or a leather needle, carefully push through the center of the dice bait. Feed your silicone skirt material through the loop of the bobbin threader or the eye of the leather needle, then pull it back through the bait gentaly until the skirt is centered. Repeat on all sides and trim the strands to your desired length. If you enjoy this model, please consider boosting, and sharing photos of the fish you catch with your custom dice baits.

Installation requires almost no permanent modifications to the caravan. The adapter simply fits into the original ventilation grille and can easily be removed again if required. description: Modular Baseball Pickup Tube *ASSEMBLY AT BOTTOM* This modular baseball pickup tube lets you collect baseballs quickly without repeatedly bending down. Simply press the bottom of the tool over a baseball. The ball pushes past the eight movable flaps and enters the tube, while the flaps return to their starting position to prevent the ball from falling back out. The entire design uses built-in threaded connections , so every section twists directly together. No separate screws, bolts, or connectors are needed. Modular Design Each storage capsule holds approximately four baseballs . You can add more capsule sections to increase the total capacity or use fewer sections for a shorter, lighter collector. Because every part twists together, the tool is easy to: Assemble Disassemble Transport Customize Repair Expand The bottom flap assembly only needs to be printed once. Additional threaded capsule sections can then be added above it as needed, and the handle twists onto the top. How It Works The bottom contains eight one-way flaps . These flaps can move upward when the tool is pressed over a baseball, allowing the ball to enter the tube. Built-in stops prevent the flaps from moving below their original position, which keeps the collected baseballs trapped inside. Assembly Assemble the eight flaps inside the bottom flap holder. (MORE ABOUT THIS AT THE BOTTOM.) Twist the bottom section and flap holder together using the built-in threads. Twist one storage capsule onto the bottom assembly. Add additional capsules by twisting each section together. Twist the handle onto the top capsule. No separate hardware is required for the main assembly. The threads are built directly into the printed parts. Capacity Each capsule holds about four baseballs Add more capsules for greater capacity Remove capsules for a shorter and more portable setup This design is useful for baseball practice, batting drills, coaching, field cleanup, and anyone who wants a simple way to collect balls without constantly bending over. ASSEMBLLY IMPORTANT: For the flaps, you want to either print the flaps first. If you do this, then make sure to cool the print plate down 10 Degrees because trying to take them off will cause the PLA to warp. Continue with the regular bed temp after inserting. , or while using the pause I put into the slicer. After you obtain the 8 flaps, you want to pause the flap holder at 8MM (I have already done this in the slicer) and the insert the flaps sideways, as the gif shows. I also recommend putting the bottom part of the flaps (the part that was facing down when printing) toward the bottom. (If you're on the phone, click on it to play it.) IMPORTANT: Make sure to watch a few layers after you insert them, as they wiggle due to the cooling fan, which can cause stepper loss. It has not happened when you pause at this layer height; however, it is prone to happen when you pause at lower layer heights. While After making the pause point higher in the slicer, it hasn't happened. If you want to completely avoid this, then I recommend putting the hotend cooler down a little bit for the next couple of layers. After that, you can print normally. description: 缩小到一米四尺寸的大疆EV50航模。 大疆EV50是大疆近期（2026年七月）发布的一款垂起固定翼无人机，采用了8+3动力布局，我这款是尺寸缩小到1.4米的缩比航模简化为4+1动力配置，空机大约1.1kg(PETG)建议起飞重量≤2.5kg. 说是缩比EV50但其实翼型用的NACA4412并没有和实机一样用那种超厚的看起来像超临界翼型的方案，并且稍微加大了一些机翼弦长以确保刚好的飞行性能。得益于参考机型巨大的机身尺寸，座头鲸同样也获得了巨大的机身空间，即便是6S2P电池放进去也显得非常宽敞，尽管并不建议用难么大的电池。而为什么要做一米四这个尺寸，很大的原因是为了给打印一整架飞机的耗材量刚好能控制在一卷以内或者多出来也不会太多，另外就是考虑到P1S大打印行程，这个巨大的机身确实是太巨大了。 由于参考资料仅仅是DJI官网的几个图片和一段视频所以也有少量额外的比例失真。 这次我开源了整机基础版的STP实体文件，大家可以根据自己的喜好二次编辑，并且可以直接使用Bambu Studio右上角的整体试图参考装配 490*10的碳管一根，主翼梁 500*8的碳管两根 460*2 400*2 120*2 320*1 140*2 这是3毫米碳棒 机臂是两根12*450的碳管 升力电机座可以直接用这种CNC的 如图 尾推电机座孔位和朗宇2814或者2810是一样的 当然其他电机的孔位也是这个，比如我手头刚好有一个兴耀华2820 当然我建议是2814电机就足够了 升力电机建议使用2801或者3110之类能带9到10寸桨的电机，不建议使用四合一电调，散热不好容易宕机，虽然丑一点我还是推荐用4个分体电调。 舵机需要六个，银燕ES08或者PTK7452的尺寸都是可以的 区域的电设诸如飞控之类看自己预算和喜好了，后舱盖的GPS舱可以容纳280尺寸的GPS模块。 因为现在的飞行报备流程太麻烦，所以暂时我也没打算装机试飞，先打出来看看，也只能期待条件比较方便的模友尝试一下了。

The design focuses on: Full compatibility with the A1 Mini build volume Reduced print time Lower filament consumption Simple assembly with minimal hardware requirements Good airflow for media and light gaming workloads Fan grills are not included. The photos show PC Fan Cover with Grille, Filter 60/80/92/120 by Gorilla Labs, but any standard 120mm fan grill can be used or printed according to your preference. Current Status This design is still a work in progress and should be considered a beta release. I have personally been running this case continuously just over a week for: 4K movie streaming General desktop use Light gaming During this testing, temperatures have remained in the low to mid 60°C range, even under peak loads. However, I have not yet subjected the system to extended heavy gaming or stress testing. As additional testing and revisions are completed, updates and improvements will be released. Assembly Notes Assembly is fairly straightforward overall. The only challenging portion is installing the four internal heat-set inserts and screws that secure both the BC-250 board and the case structure together. Access is somewhat limited, along with your soldering iron a small pair of pliers or tweezers are recommended to make installation "easier". Printing Recommendations This model was designed and tested on a Bambu Lab A1 Mini using PETG-CF . For best results: Clean the build plate thoroughly before printing large parts. Apply a thin layer of glue stick to the build plate before printing. PETG can bond very aggressively to PEI surfaces, and the glue acts as both an adhesion promoter and a release layer. Dry your filament before printing. PETG-CF prints significantly better when dry and will produce stronger parts with cleaner surfaces. Run bed leveling and vibration calibration if the printer has recently been moved or serviced. Allow parts to cool completely before removing them from the build plate. Avoid touching the print area of the build plate with your fingers immediately before printing. Alrighty, PLEASE READ this all if you would like to print this. I was a little hesitant on posting this model. I am really proud of it, but I am hesitant on posting… let me explain my concerns. Firstly, the model works and prints well. It does take about 5 hours on my P2S (sorry, it won't work on an A1 Mini). Once the model is finished, a little work is required from the user to get the pegs to spin. You need to turn the model around and push down on each peg to loosen it from the model. Since these pegs are in there tightly and I didn't want them to pop out, there is some light bonding to the rest of the board when first printed, but once you put some pressure on EACH peg, the peg will loosen for turning and will be good to use for the future. Please take a look at the gif in the sample pics above as I show myself loosening some of the pegs. You will feel a snap when loosening each peg. Second, I didn't want to make this model too big and wanted it to work nicely with the MLB plates, so my concern is that the numbers may be a bit too close, but that could just be my perspective. When the numbers are displayed, I would recommend looking at this model from at least 5 feet away because anything closer than that, the number arrangement may look a little "weird' but again, that may be just me. Third, this is mainly a desk/table item and not meant to be mount to be mounted on a wall. I left the screws on the model if you wanted to mess around with it, but I couldn't really add any holes to the right side of it. I added a desk mount to the model that is printed separately so the model can sit nicely in it. I also feel like it would be harder to turn the pegs if this was wall mounted. Lastly, changing each peg every day to update the standings can get tedious. Especially since the pegs are small it is very easy to hit other pegs while adjusting others and getting pegs misaligned. Alright, as you can see, I am not a salesman, at all lol. I just wanted to be open and forward to everyone before printing this. I am really proud of this project but I do see some of the limitations that it does bring, so I wanted to be as open as possible to everyone. This model contains three versions, one that says “standings”, one with a blank sign and one with no sign. If you want to make your own text on the blank sign, but like the font I use, it is called Jersey M54 and can be found here to download for free. In the end, I really wanted to post this model because I worked really hard on it and I don't see another model like this anywhere on makerworld, so figured I'd give it a go. I don't plan on making other models of this version for NFL, NBA, NHL and so on as this did take a lot of work (and test filament prints) on my end. If you are looking for my MLB plates, they can be found here in this collection (contains each team, standings, etc for all my baseball plate stuff). Thanks!!

With this model you are going to need: 11 - Ruthex (12.7mm Long) ¼-20 Inserts -OR- Ruthex (12.7mm Long) m6 inserts. 9 - ½" long flat head socket cap stainless steel bolts. Snap tiles together to build a display of any size — from a single card to a full grid wall — with zero glue, screws, or loose hardware. NOTE: Load each One Touch case into its tile BEFORE snapping the tile above it on the wall — once tiles are stacked, the ones below are covered. Plan your layout first! Recommend 3M Command tape to stick them to the wall. 🔗 HOW THE SYSTEM WORKS Every tile is a single printed piece with built-in interlocking connectors — no clips, extra magnets, glue, or screws required in the print itself. The magnets are already inside the One Touch case. Tiles lock together in every direction (side-to-side and stacked vertically) to form a grid of any width and height. To add a tile: hook it over the pegs of the tile beside or below it and slide straight down — it locks in place. To remove or rearrange: lift straight up. Edge caps finish the outer edges so the assembled grid looks like one clean framed piece. 🧩 THE PARTS (Mix and Match Freely) Tiles — available in 1-wide, 2-wide, and 3-wide. Multi-wide tiles print as one solid piece for added strength and faster printing. All widths line up exactly with single tiles, so any combination fits together (e.g. a 3-wide tile sits perfectly above three singles). Top Caps (1/2/3-wide) — clip onto the top row to cover connectors and give a clean top edge. Side Caps — clip onto the right edge for a finished side; they also stack vertically for tall displays. Corner Piece — caps the top-right corner and locks the top and side caps together. Don't have a printer? Buy physical tiles here: https://hitprints.com The design focuses on clean, modular construction, easy expansion, and reliable printability, making it ideal for personal-use prints. Notes: I've kept infill at 15% which keeps tiles sturdy while saving filament. If you experience corner lift, adding an 8mm brim and slowing the first layer to 20mm/s is recommended. No supports needed. 🔧 DESIGN FEATURES Fully modular — start with one tile, expand to any size No hardware required — integrated snap-together design (magnets are already in the One Touch case) Removable & rearrangeable — pull any tile to swap cards or restyle 1-wide, 2-wide, and 3-wide tile options included Top caps, side caps, and corner piece for a clean framed look Designed for standard 35pt One Touch magnetic cases Cross-compatible with the top loader and PSA graded Infinity Wall Tile systems — mix grids freely Damage-free wall mounting with 3M Command strips Clean, modern design optimized for 3D printing 🖨️ PRINTING NOTES Designed for standard FDM printers No supports required Light layer lines are normal and expected Works great in PLA and PETG HF 🖼️ MOUNTING Recommend 3M Command tape to stick them to the wall. Designed for use with 3M Command picture-hanging strips for damage-free wall mounting. No drilling, no holes, no permanent damage. Strips are not included. 💬 HAVE A REQUEST? model_name: Trotec PAC 2020 E – Dual Hose Adapter
description: Overview This project converts the Trotec PAC 2020 E from a single-hose to a dual-hose portable air conditioner. The original unit uses conditioned indoor air to cool the condenser and exhausts this air outside. This creates a slight negative pressure inside the room, causing warm outside air to enter through doors, windows and other leaks. With this modification the condenser is supplied with fresh outdoor air , while the hot exhaust air is still discharged outdoors. This greatly reduces the negative pressure inside the room and improves the overall cooling efficiency. Features ✅ Dual-hose conversion for the Trotec PAC 2020 E ✅ Designed for 16 mm twin-wall polycarbonate (multiwall) sheets ✅ Secure hose connection with integrated retaining bead (hose won't slip off) ✅ Tool-free installation into the air conditioner ✅ Tight fit without additional adapters ✅ Perfect for removable summer window inserts Required Parts In addition to the printed parts you will need: 16 mm twin-wall polycarbonate sheet 150 mm aluminium flexible duct (inside diameter) for the fresh air intake Original Trotec exhaust hose Fly screen (recommended) Suitable adhesive for bonding the inner and outer window rings The hose connector is specifically designed for 150 mm inner diameter aluminium ducting . The integrated retaining bead keeps the hose securely attached during operation without requiring hose clamps. Window Insert The window insert is designed for a 16 mm polycarbonate twin-wall sheet . Simply cut two circular openings into the sheet and install the printed adapters. The insert can easily be removed after the summer season without modifying the window. Hose Connection The hose connectors include an integrated retaining bead . This prevents the flexible air hoses from slipping off during operation while still allowing easy installation without hose clamps. Outdoor Air Intake Installing a fly screen on the outside air intake is highly recommended. This prevents insects, leaves and larger debris from entering the air conditioner while having almost no impact on airflow. Assembly Print all parts. Cut two openings into the 16 mm polycarbonate twin-wall sheet . Use the inner ring as a template to mark the cutout. Cut the openings as accurately as possible to ensure a snug fit. Place the fresh air intake below the exhaust opening. Position the exhaust opening above the fresh air intake. Place the outer window ring on the outside of the polycarbonate sheet. Lay the fly screen over the outer ring. Apply adhesive to the inner retaining ring. Press the inner ring into the outer ring, clamping the fly screen securely between the outer ring and the polycarbonate sheet. Allow the adhesive to cure completely. Connect the original Trotec exhaust hose and the 150 mm aluminium intake duct . Important For the best cooling performance, always install the exhaust opening above the fresh air intake . Since warm air naturally rises, placing the exhaust above the intake minimizes the risk of recirculating hot exhaust air. Material Recommendation I printed all parts in ASA because it offers: excellent heat resistance UV resistance high mechanical strength good dimensional stability PETG should also work well if the parts are not exposed to direct sunlight for long periods. Print Settings Layer Height: 0.30 mm Nozzle: 0.6 mm 3-4 Walls 20–30 % Gyroid Infill Material: ASA (recommended) Supports ✅ Trotec Adapter: No supports required ✅ Outer Window Ring: No supports required ⚠️ Inner Window Ring: Supports required Only the inner ring contains overhangs that require support material. The remaining parts have been designed to print support-free. Results After installing the dual-hose conversion I measured the following performance: Outdoor temperature: ~30 °C Supply air temperature: ~12 °C Exhaust air temperature: ~40 °C One children's room cooled from 25 °C to below 20 °C With both bedroom doors open, the complete upper floor stabilized at approximately 23 °C , even in full sunshine. These results were measured using Home Assistant temperature sensors and represent real-world performance in my home. Notes This model was designed specifically for the Trotec PAC 2020 E . It may fit other models with a similar rear housing, but this has not been tested. If you build one, I'd love to see your make! A split version of the Trotec adapter is included for printers with a 256 × 256 mm build volume (e.g. Bambu Lab P1, X1 and A1 series). Simply bond the three printed parts together before installation.

description: 3D printed TPU inserts are great! They are waterproof, so no need to worry in the trail. They are highly modular (especially this model). Extreme side hill capability, yet conformative. Fit 1.9 wheels 4.19 tires from Pro Line! Probably even Jconcepts 4.19 tires. This model is meant to be adjusted in the slicer. I have placed modifiers on the model. If you want ex. a harder inner core, set the modifier infill higher. If you want the outmost layer to be softer or harder. Adjust the infill in the global global section. Also you will find modifiers on top and bottom. These control the amount of walls on the sidewalls. I set it to 2 walls for easier print and more stable side hill. Everything is set to make for a good print with soft feel for lighter trucks. Again, just change the infill to suit your needs. Please use the process presets included as a starting point. The project is set for Bambu Labs TPU 85A on 0.4 nozzle. Of course you can print these in harder TPUs aswell. IMPORTANT! Bambu states that you cannot print 85A with anything smaller than a 0.6 nozzle. You can, but it takes some thinking. 1: Make sure you use a spool holder with NO drag. It needs to move super smooth and preferably feed the extruder from the top. You can find that kind of spool holders here on makerworld. 2: Bambu 85A Filament profile. Bambu studio wont let you choose Bambus 85A profile while using a 0.4 nozzle. So choose the Bambu 90A profile. Change volumetric flow to 2.2 and up the temp to 235. Save as new profile. This works great! All settings in the project are there for a reason. A lot of time went in to this, so if you want to change something you should proceed with care. If you get a bad prints from making other settings, please dont blame me!

description: GoPro Visor Mount – Various Angles (155° / 160° / 165°) A GoPro mount designed to sit under the peak/visor of a full-face mountain bike helmet, anchoring to the ridge angle formed by the underside of the peak. Since visor peak angles vary between helmet brands and models, this design is available in three ridge-angle variants — 155°, 160°, and 165° — to suit different helmets. A test fit template is included and should be printed first: it's a quick, low-material print of just the mounting interface, letting you check which of the three angles best matches your helmet before committing to a full print of the mount itself. How to use: Print the test template (fast, minimal material). Hold it against the underside of your helmet's visor peak and compare the fit against the ridge angle. Print the full mount version (155° / 160° / 165°) that matches best (note the important print settings/ orientation further down) Glue in a M5x.08 Cap Nut, don’t get glue on the threads (commonly available from amazon/ Aliexpress etc) Designed and tested on a Troy Lee Designs D3 (160°), but the provided angle options should cover most full-face MTB helmets with a peaked visor (Fox, Bell, POC, Leatt, O'Neal, etc.). The 1-2mm 3M tape can take up a few degrees slack on each side. Let me know which angle fits your helmet in the comments and I will build up a database to save everyone printing the templates. Happy to add more angles if needed just let me know if bigger or smaller angle needed. ### ⚠️ CRITICAL SAFETY & INSTALLATION GUIDE ⚠️ An under-visor mount is only as strong as the tape holding it on. To prevent your camera from flying off on rough trails or heavy jumps, you **MUST** follow these surface preparation steps. Plastic visors are often coated in factory release agents or silicone-based cleaners that will cause tape to fail instantly. #### 🛠️ What You Need: * **Genuine 3M VHB Tape** (1-2mm thickness is highly recommended to absorb visor flex). * **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** (70% or higher) or disk brake cleaner. * A clean microfiber cloth or lint-free wipe. * A heat gun or hairdryer (highly recommended for cold workshops). #### 🧽 Step-by-Step Installation: 1. **Scrub the Visor:** Soak your cloth in Isopropyl Alcohol and vigorously clean the underside crease of your helmet visor. Do NOT use soapy water, window cleaner, or WD-40, as they leave a greasy film. 2. **Clean the Mount:** Wipe down the vertical side faces of your 3D-printed mount with alcohol to remove any skin oils from your fingers. 3. **Apply Tape to Mount:** Apply the VHB tape to the mount first. Press down with heavy thumb pressure for 30 seconds to activate the pressure-sensitive adhesive. 4. **Warm the Plastic (Pro-Tip):** If your room is under 20°C (68°F), use a hairdryer to slightly warm both the helmet visor and the mount. VHB tape needs warmth to flow into the microscopic ridges of the plastic. 5. **The Final Bond:** Press the mount firmly into the visor crease. Apply heavy pressure for a full 60 seconds. 6. **⏳ THE MOST IMPORTANT STEP:** **Wait 24 Hours.** VHB tape takes 24 hours to reach 90% bond strength, and a full 72 hours to reach 100%. If you ride immediately, the mount will fall off. 🚨 RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS 🚨 • Material: PETG (Highly recommended over PLA for impact resistance) • Perimeters: 5 to 6 Walls (This makes the tiny part structurally solid) • Infill: 99% Gyroid (Do NOT use 100% to avoid warping) • Top/Bottom Layers: 5 layers • Print orientation: Print front face down to ensure the mounting tabs do not have layer lines creating weakness in the horizontal axis when installed, note this will require minimal support enabled • Supports: enabled "tree minimal" ### 🛑 Disclaimer This is a DIY 3D-printed accessory where print quality and material is variable. Ride at your own risk. The designer is not responsible for any damaged cameras, lost equipment, or broken helmet visors resulting from the use or incorrect installation of this model. Always use a camera tether (fishing line or cord) in the provided tether hole and attached to your helmet as a secondary safety backup!

description: The Ultimate Ball Generator Create fully customizable decorative, sensory, toy, or hanging balls directly in MakerWorld. Adjust the ball dimensions, surface pattern, hole spacing, wall thickness, colors, custom text, and hanging ring without using external CAD software. One generator. Endless possibilities. Create personalized balls with names or logos, Christmas ornaments, keychains, sensory and fidget toys, bouncing balls, decorative spheres, party favors, and unique gifts. Mix patterns, colors, text styles and accessories to generate thousands of completely different designs — all in just a few clicks. Main Features Ball diameter from 20 to 150 mm (larger also possible per request) Adjustable wall thickness from 1 to 5 mm Airless or solid spheres Multiple pattern styles: Circle Hexagon Diamond Rectangle Triangle Teardrop Heart Flower Star Four pattern effects: None – smooth ball Hole – openings through the shell Emboss – recessed pattern Raised – pattern raised above the surface Adjustable pattern size, spacing, rotation and marking depth Optional rounded pattern edges Optional Seam decorations (basketball, tennis ball, soccer ball, …) Custom text with multiple fonts Two text background styles: Text Outline – background follows the actual letter shapes Plaque – rounded rectangular nameplate Flat, embossed or raised text Adjustable text margin and nameplate curvature Optional reinforced hanging ring Custom colors for the ball, text background and lettering Adjustable sphere resolution for better quality or prototyping How to Customize Ball Dimensions Use Diameter to select the overall size of the ball. Wall Thickness determines the shell thickness when the Hole effect is selected. A value of 2–3 mm is a good starting point for most prints. Sphere Resolution controls surface smoothness: Draft – fastest preview Standard – quick testing Smooth – good balance Fine – recommended default Great or Ultra – smoother result, but longer generation time Pattern Choose the desired shape using Pattern Type . Use: Pattern Size to control the size of each element Pattern Spacing to control the visible gap between elements Pattern Angle to rotate the pattern on the ball Pattern Marking to control emboss depth or raised height Add Fillet on Pattern to round the pattern edges Small patterns combined with very small spacing can create a large number of elements and significantly increase generation and slicing time. Seams (decoration) Use this predefined seam decorations that adds a final touch to your ball. Available now: Basketball Basketball retro Tennis Baseball Soccer ball (football) Custom Text Set Custom Text to On , then enter your message. Choose between: Text Outline for a compact background following the letters Plaque for a traditional rounded rectangular label Text Margin controls the space or outline around the lettering. Plaque Curve Correction allows fine adjustment of how tightly the background follows the ball: Negative values create a flatter curve Positive values wrap the background more tightly The default value is tuned for most ball and text sizes Text effects: Flat – flush multicolor lettering Emboss – recessed lettering Raised – lettering above the surface For multicolor models, download the generated 3MF to preserve the separate ball, background and text colors. Hanging Ring Enable Hanging Ring to add a reinforced loop at the top. Adjust: Ring Hole Size for the string or ribbon opening Ring Thickness for the strength of the loop This option is useful for ornaments, decorations and hanging sensory toys. The color of the ring can be customized in Color section. Best Practices / Tips At first lower Ball resolution to Draft. When done designing try making it higher (only if needed). Please note that dense patterns actually are very good at Draft and there is no need to set higher resolution. Pattern Fillet can be quite heavy to process on the servers but in most of the cases is not needed. If you expirience server timeouts or errors consider turning it off. When you expirience server timeout or errors it most likely means that your set-up is to heavy to process on MakerWorld's servers. Try larger patter or higher spacing, lower resolution. Everything that will make it less complicated will work and try again. Consider the position of the ball when you will be printing it. For example when using heart pattern - the middle part of heart can not face down as you will need to support every patter like this. Thy setting an angle and face it up. The larger the ball is the more render power it requires on MM servers. If you plan going large try less details. Printing Tips Printing spheres is quite challenging and it is important to choose the right options in the slicer. Here are some tips to achieve the best results: Use the generated 3MF when printing in multiple colors. A layer height of 0.16–0.20 mm works well. Enable option “Don't support bridges” Add “Support Blocker” modifier to block supporting areas inside the ball. Rise the blocker a little bit so the base can be supported Tune your “Top Z distance” value for supports Use at least three wall loops for hollow balls. Enable supports when required by the selected pattern and orientation. Build-plate-only supports are usually easier to remove. For small holes, verify the preview before printing. Reduce print speed on the outer wall for a smoother spherical surface. Larger balls, dense patterns and Ultra resolution require more processing time. To achieve optimal bounce, use a suitable filament (TPU, PEBA, other flexible filaments). Important Notes Hole produces a hollow ball using the selected wall thickness. None , Emboss and Raised produce a solid ball. Very thin walls or extremely small gaps may not print reliably with every nozzle size. This generator creates geometry dynamically, so complex configurations can take longer to generate in MakerWorld. Make sure to follow my profile on Maker World for updates and ready to use examples. Have fun printing!

description: 🚴♂️ Garmin Fenix (51mm) Lenkerhalterung mit integrierter Frontlicht-Halterung (Garmin Quarter-Turn) | Ø 31,8 mm (Optimiert für Fenix 8, 7X, 6X & Zubehör wie Frontlichter z.B. Towild FR500 / Gaciron) Bringe deine Garmin Fenix sicher an dein Fahrrad und halte gleichzeitig dein Cockpit clean! Diese robuste, 3D-druckbare Lenkerhalterung wurde speziell für die 51 mm Garmin-Modelle (mit 26 mm Stegbreite) und Standard-Fahrradlenker mit Ø 31,8 mm entwickelt. Das Highlight dieser Version: Das Modell wurde strategisch verstärkt und an der Unterseite mit einer Garmin-Vierteldrehung-Aufnahme (Quarter-Turn Mount) erweitert. Dadurch kannst du direkt unter deiner Fenix ein kompatibles Frontlicht (z. B. FR500) oder eine Action-Cam mit passendem Adapter bombenfest und platzsparend montieren! Die Montage ist denkbar einfach und extrem sauber gelöst: Die Klemme wird mit einer M3-Senkkopfschraube und Mutter festgezogen. Durch die Senkung schließt der Schraubenkopf perfekt bündig ab. Das smarte Scharnier nutzt ein einfaches Stück Filament als robusten Scharnierstift – kein Spezialwerkzeug oder zusätzliche Hardware für das Gelenk nötig! ⚙️ Technische Details & benötigte Hardware Lenkerdurchmesser: Ø 31,8 mm (Standard für Rennräder & Mountainbikes) Zubehör-Kompatibilität: Untere Aufnahme passend für Garmin Quarter-Turn (speziell für Frontlichter oder Action-Cams mit entsprechendem Adapter) Hardware benötigt: 1x M3 Senkkopfschraube (Länge ca. 12-16mm) & 1x M3 Mutter Scharnierstift: Ein kurzes Stück Filament (1,75 mm, idealerweise aus dem gleichen Material geschnitten) Material-Empfehlung: PETG, PETG HF oder ASA/ABS . Bitte kein normales PLA verwenden! Durch das zusätzliche Gewicht des Frontlichts und die Vibrationen beim Fahren ist ein zähes, witterungsbeständiges Material wie PETG HF absolut notwendig. 🔍 Umfassende Kompatibilitätsliste (Uhr) Die Halterung ist kompatibel mit allen Garmin-Modellen, die für die großen 26-mm-QuickFit-Armbänder ausgelegt sind. Fenix-Serie (51 mm): Fenix 8 (c / Solar & AMOLED), Fenix 7X / 7X Pro (alle Varianten: Solar, Sapphire), Fenix 6X (Pro, Sapphire, Solar), Fenix 5X / 5X Plus, Fenix 3 / 3 HR Epix-Serie: Epix Pro (Gen 2) – 51 mm Tactix- & Enduro-Serie: Tactix 8 (51 mm), Tactix 7, Tactix Delta, Tactix Charlie, Enduro, Enduro 2, Enduro 3 Instinct-Serie (Große Modelle): Instinct 2X Solar, Instinct 3 (50 mm Varianten) Descent- & Quatix-Serie (Tauchen/Marine): Descent Mk3i (51 mm), Descent Mk2 / Mk2i, Descent Mk1, Quatix 8 (51 mm), Quatix 7X, Quatix 6X, Quatix 3 🖨️ Empfohlene Druckeinstellungen (Print Settings) Aufgrund der zusätzlichen Belastung durch das untere Frontlicht wurden die Wände verstärkt. Für maximale Stabilität empfehle ich: Material: PETG HF (Hohe Festigkeit, witterungsbeständig, ideal für Outdoor) Schichthöhe (Layer Height): 0,20 mm Wandlinien / Perimeter (Wall Loops): 4 – 5 (Sehr wichtig für die Stabilität der Zubehör-Aufnahme!) Infill: 40% – 50% (Gyroid für gleichmäßige Stabilität in alle Richtungen) Strukturen / Support: Ja, Support für die untere Garmin-Halterung und die Scharnier-Überhänge wird empfohlen. 🛠️ Montageanleitung 1. Drucke das Modell aus einem witterungsbeständigen und stabilen Material (z.B. PETG HF). 2. Setze die beiden Hälften am Gelenk zusammen und schiebe ein passend gekürztes Stück 1,75 mm Filament durch den Scharnierkanal. Fixiere die Enden optional mit einem Tropfen Sekundenkleber oder verschmelze sie ganz leicht. 3. Klemme die Halterung um deinen Lenker (drucke einen dünnen Steifen TPU, darunter schützt vor Kratzern und verhindert Verrutschen). 4. Setze die M3-Mutter ein und ziehe die M3-Senkkopfschraube handfest an, bis sie bündig im Gehäuse sitzt. 5. Klicke deine Garmin Fenix oben per QuickFit ein. 6. Drehe dein Frontlicht (z.B. FR500) mit einer Vierteldrehung in die untere Halterung ein – fertig ist dein super aufgeräumtes Cockpit! Gefällt dir das erweiterte Design? Ich würde mich riesig über ein Like, ein Abo und vor allem über ein Foto deines Makes inkl. montiertem Frontlicht in den Kommentaren freuen! Allzeit gute und sichere Fahrt bei jeder Tageszeit! 🚴♂️💨

Dented my trunk a while ago and thought that it is a great opportunity to do something new. FILE FORMAT: STEP HOW IT IS DESIGNED: First I made high quality scan of the trunk(availale on my official account in CULTS3D.COM - https://cults3d.com/en/users/Booster316/3d-models for free). Imported it into my CAD software and started designing around it ensuring it fits perfectly so it could be mounted without any problem whatsoever. HOW I PRINTED IT: The Ducktail is cut manualy in the slicer (5 individual parts, no allignment pins, bed capacity:256x256x256mm, Printer: Bambu Lab X1C), aplied a 6mm brim to every piece to avoid warping which appeared in a test print I did. The parts are put together with a two component glue (the parts were preped with sandpaper beforehand for better adhesion). MATERIAL: PETG Prep for paint: Sand down with sandpaper so the bodyfiller sticks (clean the surface with a degreeser before applying the filler). I used elastic bodyfiller. Sand till smooth and add and sand more until you are satisfied with the result. Apply primer and you are ready to paint it. Paint: For this part I used spray paint the same color as my car, however you can use a paint gun if you wish for a better result. Used a 2k clear coat in a spray can. It is beter if you use 2 component clear coat, it's way better (the one i used was not). The Ducktail in the pictures is holding onto the car with double sided tape in case it looks odd to you. I would really appreciate any feedback you have! Do not holdback in the comments! I would love to hear what is on your mind! Thank You!

This is a tool tube for the CFMoto (Ibex) 450MT. It has been customized to store the Icon mini ratchet & extension, Harbor Freight 1/4" 8/10/12/13mm sockets, and up to 10 hex bits. Inspiration came from the design on Uncle Wang's Shop. Fusion file is included in case you want a starting point to make a tube of your own. Uploaded as zip file as it wouldn't allow f3d upload here? I've put the initial tube generation into the first grouping, so you can just roll back to there and have at it. This model leaves about 80mm to work with on the other side. This should only be printed in flexible filaments (I used foaming TPU). Use auto alignment or specify to print on the plug face, forcing it to print at an angle. Printing using .16mm layer heights makes supports unnecessary. Supports were avoided because foaming TPU is nasty when moving between objects. Having supports wasn't a big deal with traditional TPU while I was prototyping. There is a parameter "gripAmount" in the fusion file, which may need to be relaxed if printing in TPU harder than 75A.

Diseño de Cubierta para PS5: "Vice City Legacy Edition" (Inspirado en GTA VI) Este diseño de cubierta personalizada para PS5, creado mediante impresión 3D, fusiona la estética icónica de Vice City con los logotipos oficiales que se esperan para el próximo Grand Theft Auto VI. El diseño se presenta en dos paneles (izquierdo y derecho) que reemplazan las cubiertas originales de la consola. Características Visuales: Lado Izquierdo (Panel de Logotipos): Este panel presenta una composición vertical y estructurada. Área de Logotipo Principal: En la parte superior, se muestra el logotipo completo de "Grand Theft Auto VI", exactamente como se ve en la imagen "GTA 6.png". El logotipo cuenta con el gran número romano 'VI', relleno con un patrón de palmeras en color magenta brillante y un borde azul eléctrico. El texto "Grand Theft Auto" está superpuesto en color blanco limpio con un contorno negro. Estructura del Logotipo: El logotipo principal está suspendido dentro de un marco de estructura de acero estilizado de color negro mate (como las vigas de soporte que se ven en la imagen "GTA 6.png"), que se extiende verticalmente. Insignia de Rockstar: En la parte inferior de la estructura de soporte, se encuentra una insignia de Rockstar Games separada. Esta presenta el icónico logotipo de "R*" en blanco, centrado en un cuadrado azul eléctrico con un borde magenta brillante, similar al que se muestra en "GTA 6.png". Superficie de Textura: El fondo de la cubierta izquierda es negro mate con sutiles patrones hexagonales grabados que imitan una textura de fibra de carbono ligera, dando un aspecto tecnológico y premium. Lado Derecho (Panel de Arte): Este panel presenta una composición artística expansiva que contrasta con la estructura del panel izquierdo. Escena de Fondo: Un paisaje urbano de Vice City al atardecer, renderizado en tonos neón (azul, magenta, cian, rosa). El sol se pone sobre el agua, con las siluetas de los rascacielos de la ciudad y más palmeras. Arte de Personaje Silueteado: Un primer plano estilizado de los dos presuntos protagonistas (Lucia y Jason) caminando por un paseo marítimo, silueteados contra el sol poniente, en tonos neón. Detalles Adicionales: Sutiles grafitis en neón "VICE" y "GTA VI" integrados en la arquitectura de la ciudad. El fondo es negro mate texturizado, permitiendo que los elementos neón resalten. Estilo de Impresión 3D y Materiales: Técnica: Impresión 3D por deposición de material fundido (FDM) multicapa de alta precisión. Ajuste y Acabado: Tolerancias precisas para encajar perfectamente en los soportes originales de la PS5 Digital Edition. Estética: Una combinación de superficies mate texturizadas y acabados brillantes en los logotipos, lograda mediante cambios de filamento precisos. Material: PLA de alto rendimiento. (yo utilice PETG) Descripción del Producto y Guía de Impresión Título del Producto: Cubiertas Personalizadas "Vice City Legacy Edition" para PS5 (Digital Edition) - Diseño GTA VI Descripción Corta: Dale a tu PS5 un cambio de imagen radical de Vice City con estas cubiertas personalizadas impresas en 3D. Con los logotipos oficiales de GTA VI y una impresionante escena artística de neón, este diseño fusiona la nostalgia con el futuro del gaming. 🛠️ Guía de Impresión Multi-Color (SIN AMS) - Instrucciones de Cambio de Filamento Este diseño ha sido optimizado para impresoras FDM estándar sin sistema automático de filamento. Debes realizar cambios de filamento manuales en capas específicas para lograr el efecto multicolor en los logotipos. Parámetros de Impresión Recomendados: Altura de capa: 0.16mm o 0.20mm (para mejores detalles de logotipo). Relleno: 15% o 20% . Paredes: 3 o más. Soportes: Si (Arbol Sobre Placa) Secuencia de Cambio de Filamento: A continuación, introduce el orden de tus cambios de color según las capas de tu laminador. Negro - Azul - Negro - Azul - Negro - Azul - Negro - Blanco - Morado - Blanco - Negro - Blanco - Morado - Blanco - Negro - Blanco - Morado - Negro - Blanco - Negro - Blanco - Negro - Blanco Asegúrate de configurar pausas en tu laminador o "Cambio de Filamento" (G-Code M600) en las alturas de capa indicadas. description: Prevent your window from accidentally slamming shut due to wind or drafts. Unlike other window stops, this design features an eccentric clamp mechanism. Secure eccentric clamping The eccentric clamp mechanism securely locks the stop to the windowsill with a simple flip of the lever. No screws, adhesives, or permanent installation required. Low-profile design Only 24 mm high when folded. Most windows can be closed without removing the stop. Leave it installed on the windowsill and simply flip the lever up whenever you want to limit the window opening. Fully parametric Adjust the height to match your desired window opening. Customize the dimensions to fit your windowsill perfectly. Print in place design Ready to use right away Dimensions Dimension A : Windowsill thickness ( For maximum holding power, the window stopper should fit onto the windowsill with as little play as possible ) Dimension B : Lower depth (Reduce only when space is limited) Dimension C : Lower frame thickness (Reduce only when space is limited) Dimension D : Window height (Adjust it so that the flap extends slightly beyond the window seal. description: I know the configurator can be a bit tricky; if the guide isn’t clear enough, please do feel free to message me. I’m currently putting together some more comprehensive example profiles featuring all the patterns and various options TESSERA — Modular Parametric Wall Tiles (22 pattern engines) Turn your wall into a generative artwork. TESSERA is a fully parametric system of decorative 3D-printed wall tiles: pick a pattern engine, pick a seed, and build a wall where every tile is unique — yet every joint matches perfectly. No two TESSERA walls in the world need to look the same. Yours won't. 🆕 What's new in v2.0 Relief modulation — the headline feature. Every 2D pattern can now be sculpted in height while keeping its exact design: the top of the relief follows a 3D field of your choice — waves (egg-crate), radial splash (one giant drop centered anywhere on the wall), organic (seed-driven noise), ridges , stepped terraces (contour bands crossing the design) or random plateaus (a block grid where every cell gets its own height — align the grid to the pattern cell and each element rises to its own level). A height floor keeps the design always readable, and a minimum-width guard drops unprintably thin slivers to the level below automatically. Three new sculpted engines (22 total): Crosswave (interfering sine waves — domes and saddles), Droplet (a water drop frozen mid-splash, rings fading with distance) and Topo (organic noise quantized into flat terraces — a contour-line terrain model, gorgeous with one filament color per level). Functional tiles, upgraded : the hook tile now takes 1 to 3 evenly spaced prongs (hook_count), and shelf/hook add-ons ship as a separate third object in their own color — assign three filaments, or print just the add-on in PETG for extra strength. Customizer polish : parameter groups reorganized in the order you actually use them (Pattern and Dimensions right after Part, backlight options at the bottom); curve resolution is now an exposed parameter (curve_res — the Quality section is no longer empty!); and sculpt_res moved next to it as the smoothness control for all sculpted engines, now up to 160. ✨ Why it's different Most tile models repeat one identical piece. TESSERA doesn't: the pattern lives on an infinite virtual canvas , and each tile is just a window on it. Give every tile its position (tile_x, tile_y), keep the same seed, and the design flows across the joints — curves, mazes and dunes continue from one tile to the next as if the wall were printed in one piece. Bonus: if a tile ever breaks, reprint it. Same seed, same position, identical tile. Write your seed on the back of the wall! 🧩 22 pattern engines, 4 families Global random field — every tile unique, always matching: Truchet arcs, Diagonal maze, True labyrinth, Voronoi web, Bubbles Global deterministic field — one continuous lattice across the wall: Hexagon honeycomb, Flowing waves, Fish scales/Seigaiha, Interlace lattice, Isometric cubes, Diamond plate, Celtic plait Per-tile motif — identical tiles, infinite repetition: Concentric ripples, Sunflower, Star lattice, Girih strapwork, Basket weave Sculpted heightmap — continuous 3D surfaces, plaster-panel style: Silk, Dunes, Crosswave, Droplet, Topo Two engines deserve a special mention. The True labyrinth is a genuine perfect maze (binary-tree algorithm): every corridor connects, no dead zones, and it continues across tiles — yes, you can solve your wall with a finger. 🌀 And the Sunflower is pure mathematics made visible: seeds placed at the golden angle (360°/φ²), exactly like a real sunflower — and its arms style draws the spiral arms themselves. The arm count is a Fibonacci number by theorem (8/13/21/34 — nothing else produces clean spirals). Switch 21 → 34 and watch the next term of the sequence appear on your wall. 🌻 🔧 The system Two tile formats : square 1×1 and wide 2:1 , freely mixed — sockets share the same pitch, so brick-style running bond layouts just work Relief modulation 🌊: sculpt the height of any 2D pattern with waves, splashes, noise, terraces or random plateaus — same design, new depth Backlight mode 💡: switch to cutout and the tile becomes a pierced light panel with a smart support web (no floating pieces, with any engine). The included LED spacer frame mounts on the wall, hosts the strip, and the tile snaps into its front rebate Hidden bowtie connectors join tiles from the back — clean joints, nothing visible from the front Blind keyhole pockets (0/1/2 per tile) hang the wall on ordinary screws, invisible from the front Multi-color by design : base plate and relief are separate meshes, and functional add-ons are a third — use your AMS, or simply add a filament change at the base layer on any single-nozzle printer (on sculpted tiles this paints gorgeous topographic contour lines) Functional tiles : a shelf tile with ribbed ledge and a hook tile with a 45° lip — same footprint, same connectors, they click into any TESSERA wall Calibration part included: dial in the connector fit for your printer before committing to full tiles NxN preview (2×2 to 5×5): see your exact wall before printing a single gram 🖨️ Printing Everything prints flat, no supports require . Tiles: base on the plate, 2 walls, 10–15% infill. Connectors: 4+ walls or 100% infill. PLA is perfect; PETG for humid rooms. Layer 0.16–0.20 mm (adaptive/0.12 mm recommended for the sculpted engines). 📖 A full illustrated PDF guide is attached — quick start, seamless-tiling explanation, per-engine reference, parameter tables, mounting steps and FAQ. ⚠️ For shelf/hook tiles: set keyholes = 2, put at least one screw in a stud or proper anchor, and load-test gradually. Connectors align tiles — they don't carry shelves. 🚀 Quick start Print the calibration part, tune conn_clearance Play with preview until you love a pattern + seed Export one tile per wall position (same seed, different tile_x/tile_y) Print, connect, hang. Done. Show me your walls in the comments — pattern + seed, so others can remix your design! ❤️ Designed by Xeyos Design. Fully parametric — hit Customize and make it yours. NOTE. The uploaded profile contains just a few examples to illustrate some good print settings, but TESSERA offers a huge number of combinations – find the one you like best.

A modern 3-tier organizer for perfumes, jewelry, cosmetics, candles or decorative accessories. Inspired by Japandi and minimalist interior design, this display stand combines elegant aesthetics with practical storage while remaining easy to print and assemble. The sturdy screw-together construction with brass heat inserts provides excellent stability and allows the organizer to be disassembled if needed. Printing Print the following parts: 1× Bottom Base 1× Middle Shelf 1× Top Shelf 1× Large Pillar 1× Small Pillar 2× Top Caps Print Settings Layer height: 0.20 mm Material: PLA Supports: Not required Brim: Not required Infill: 15–20% Gyroid or Grid Hardware Required 4× M5 × 9.5 mm brass heat inserts 4× M5 × 16 mm socket head cap screws (Allen) Note: The printed caps are specifically designed to fit over counter head screws. Assembly Install one M5 × 9.5 mm heat insert into each end of both pillars (4 total). Attach both pillars to the bottom base using two M5 × 16 mm socket head cap screws from the underside. Attach the middle shelf to the shorter pillar using one M5 × 16 mm socket head cap screw . Attach the top shelf to the taller pillar using one M5 × 16 mm socket head cap screw . Press the two printed caps into the top openings to conceal the screw heads for a clean finish. Assembly takes approximately 2 minutes . description: A modular picture frame system that fits any canvas size. Print the corners and connectors once, then generate custom rail segments to match your artwork dimensions. Canvas clips lock the artwork in place from the back without glue. A small drop of CA glue on the connector pins is recommended for a permanent frame joint. Works with canvas depth of 10mm or more. Four plate types included in default print profile Corners are fixed parts that connect the frame at 90 degrees. Each corner takes up 65mm on each side it connects to. Print 4 for any frame. Connectors are the printed pins that join rails to corners. Print one connector per part, corners and rails combined. For example, 4 corners and 6 rails need 10 connectors total. Canvas clips are retaining pins that hold the artwork securely in the frame recess from the back. Each corner has 2 clip holes and each rail has 1. Print one clip per hole for maximum hold. Note: one hole on the top rail is reserved for wall hanging. Frame rails are the straight segments generated to your dimensions. Two generators are included Frame Side Generator: enter your canvas side length and it automatically accounts for the space the corners take, then splits the rest into equal rail segments. Use this to build a full frame. Single Frame Rail Generator: outputs a rail at exactly the length you enter, with no corner adjustment. Use this for replacement parts or custom segments when you already know the exact length. How to use Frame Side Generator You enter your canvas side length. The generator subtracts the space the two corners take, 130mm total or 65mm per corner, and divides the rest into equal rail segments, so you do not need to calculate anything yourself. Steps: Enter your canvas side length in mm. Minimum 170mm. Enter the number of rail segments for that side. Aim for at least 40mm per segment, otherwise the connector pins won't fit. The generator calculates the segment length: (canvas length - 130) / number of segments. Click a generated part in the preview to confirm its exact length before printing. Repeat for the other side if your frame is not square. How to use Single Frame Rail Generator Enter the exact rail length you need. Minimum 40mm. The length you enter is exactly what you get, with no corner space subtracted. Use this for replacement parts or when you already know the dimensions. Material notes PLA works well for most sizes. For larger frames (above approximately 400mm per side) consider PETG or a stronger material for better rigidity. Assembly Apply a small drop of CA glue to each connector pin before pressing into the corner sockets and rail ends. Slide the rails and corners together and let the glue set. Place your canvas in the recess and insert the canvas clips to lock it in place. If you print it, please leave a rating - it helps a lot.
