🌐 Internet Connection Monitor 24H The project that finally proved my Internet provider was wrong. Have you ever had random Internet dropouts that magically disappeared every time the technician arrived? I did. For almost three weeks my Internet connection kept randomly disconnecting. Video calls froze, downloads stopped, smart home devices went offline... but every time I called my ISP the answer was always the same: "Everything looks perfect from our side." And of course... When the technician came to my house... The connection was perfect. So I decided to build something that could monitor my Internet connection 24 hours a day , collect real data, and prove what was really happening. That is how this project was born. After a few days of continuous monitoring, the graphs clearly showed that the connection randomly died for short periods before automatically recovering. Those historical logs finally convinced the provider to investigate further. The real culprit? A faulty modem/router that randomly crashed and reconnected. Three weeks of frustration... Solved thanks to a tiny ESP32. What does it do? This standalone monitor continuously checks your Internet connection without requiring a PC. It periodically performs: ✅ HTTP connectivity tests ✅ Ping / Latency measurements ✅ Wi-Fi RSSI monitoring ✅ Connection Health calculation ✅ 24-hour historical logging Everything is displayed on a beautiful touchscreen interface. HOME Screen The main page always shows: Internet status (UP / UNSTABLE / DOWN) Connection Health (%) HTTP Connectivity Network Latency (Ping) Wi-Fi Signal Strength (RSSI) IP Address Immediate RGB status indication 24-Hour History Touch the display to open the historical graphs. You can instantly see: Internet quality over the last 24 hours Ping history Connection stability Drops and recovery events Sometimes a connection that "looks fine" at the exact moment you're checking it tells a completely different story over an entire day. And that's exactly the purpose of this project. RGB Status LED The rear RGB LED lets you understand the connection status from across the room. 🟢 Green → Stable connection 🟡 Yellow → Unstable connection 🔴 Red → Internet unavailable No need to look at the display. Hardware ESP32 Cheap Yellow Display (ESP32-2432S028R) 2.8" ILI9341 Touch Display XPT2046 Touch Controller Integrated RGB Status LED Why I decided to share it Someone else is probably experiencing the exact same problem I had. Instead of arguing with your provider... collect the data. Numbers and graphs are much harder to ignore than words. If this project helps even one person solve an "impossible" Internet problem, then it has already achieved its purpose. Printing Tips For the best visual result: Print the front panel vertically . This produces a much smoother curved surface below the display. PETG is recommended for better temperature resistance, although PLA also works well indoors. Source Code The complete Arduino (.ino) project is included. You are welcome to study, modify and build this project for: Personal use Educational purposes Learning and experimentation Commercial use is not permitted. If you wish to manufacture, sell, or integrate this project into a commercial product, please contact me first. ⭐ If this project helped you troubleshoot your Internet connection, please consider leaving a Like, Download, Boost or Make. It really helps support future open-source ESP32 projects! 🛠 Required Components To build this project you will need: 1× ESP32-2432S028R (Cheap Yellow Display - 2.8" TFT Touch Display) 1× TP4056 Li-Ion Battery Charging Module (USB-C or Micro-USB version) 1× 18650 Li-Ion Battery 1× 18650 Battery Holder 5× M3 × 6 mm Screws 1× JST 2-Pin Mini Connector (usually included with the ESP32 Cheap Yellow Display board) 🧰 Assembly The enclosure has been designed with snap-fit joints , so no screws are required to assemble the case itself . The only screws needed are the five M3×6 mm screws used to secure the electronic components inside the enclosure. Only basic soldering skills are required to complete the project. 📦 What's Included Printable enclosure (3MF / STL) Arduino source code (rename the .txt in .ino) Complete assembly-ready design Educational documentation The template you downloaded is free; if you encountered any difficulties, please let me know and I will try to resolve them. Printing Recommendations This bottle opener is not just a decorative print—it is a functional tool that has to withstand significant force during use. To ensure the best performance and durability, please keep the following recommendations in mind. Filament Choice Choosing the right filament is essential. Filaments with additives such as silk, matte, wood, or similar effects are generally more brittle and less durable than standard materials, making the opener more likely to fail under load. For the most reliable results, standard PLA is highly recommended. Recommended Material The opener base performs best when printed in regular PLA . It is stiff, resists bending, and provides the precise fit needed to open bottles reliably. PETG is also suitable, but keep in mind that it is significantly more flexible and will bend more under load. If you choose to use more advanced materials, I assume you're already familiar with their properties and printing requirements. Please only use profiles uloaded by Designer. Make sure the opener hooks securely under the ridges of the bottle cap. Hold the opener firmly in place with your thumb . Press the lever with your index finger . The faster the bottle cap is ejected, the louder the gas will escape from the bottle. A Few Final Notes Many factors can influence how well the opener performs, including the filament brand, bottle manufacturer, beverage temperature, print quality, printer calibration, and even the way the opener is used . model_name: Midea PortaSplit Dual Hose Adapter - Full Set
description: I wanted the cold air from my PortaSplit in a different room than the unit itself. This adapter sits on the indoor unit and routes the air into up to two 200 mm flex hoses, so the AC can stand in the hallway while the bedroom gets the cold air. Nothing on the unit is modified. No screws swapped, nothing drilled. The adapter rests on the housing, two printed clips hold it. The flap keeps its full range of motion. Every mode still works, Breeze Away and Swing included, and no flap position is blocked. The hoses dock magnetically (optional) . Each outlet is a 226 mm flange with 11 magnets, the coupler carries 12 and snaps on centered. Cable-tie your hose to the coupler once, then dock and undock it as one piece. Printed clamps lock the joint if you want it permanent. Couplers for 200 mm and 150 mm hoses. A cover plate closes the second outlet in single-hose use. The air path is smooth all the way through and noise is massively reduced . 8 plates: adapter in 4 parts (fits a 256 mm bed, labyrinth joints - no glue needed) · 2 clips + 4 clamps · cover plate · coupler 200 mm · coupler 150 mm Magnets: neodymium 8 x 3-4 mm, at least 1.6 kg pull, pockets are 8.5 x 4 mm. Full kit needs 60 (adapter 2 x 11, each coupler 12, cover 12, clips 2 x 1). Single-hose setup: 48. In my setup, i only use half the magnets for the adapter and coupler and there is still enough pull force. Maybe 4 is even enough with proper magnets. 🧲 IMPORTANT: Polarity matters, read this before gluing: these magnets hold against other magnets, not against steel. Glue the flange magnets first, all with the same pole facing out. Then let each counterpart snap onto a flange magnet, mark the face you can see, and glue it exactly that way round. Dry-test every pair before the glue comes out. Also needed: the hose (I run two 200 mm PVC hoses, 6 m each), one long cable tie per hose (around 700 mm, or chain shorter ones), glue for the magnets (epoxy, CA or smartphone screen glue). Assembly Glue in the magnets: 11 per adapter outlet (the innermost pocket at the bottom of the V stays empty, you can't reach it anyway), 12 per coupler, 12 in the cover, 1 per clip. Plug the four adapter parts together, epoxy the joints if you want. Without glue it still holds and stays easy to take apart. Set the adapter on the air outlet. Slide the two side clips onto the flap edge. Cable-tie the hose onto the coupler, dock the coupler on an outlet, add clamps if you want it fixed. Close the unused outlet with the cover plate. If you print it, post a make. And if it solved a problem for you, a Boost helps me a lot.

Esta es mi interpretación de cómo pudo haber sido realmente el Caballo de Troya. Al modelarlo, intenté considerar aspectos que suelen pasarse por alto: la resistencia estructural necesaria para soportar su propio peso y el de los guerreros que ocultaba, así como una postura sólida y convincente. También imaginé que, al presentarse como una ofrenda o tributo, su apariencia debía transmitir solemnidad y respeto, más que la de una simple estructura de madera. Otro aspecto importante fue pensar en los recursos disponibles de la época. Asumí que fue construido principalmente por guerreros, con conocimientos prácticos, y no por artesanos especializados. Por eso busqué un diseño robusto, funcional y factible de construir con las herramientas y materiales que probablemente tenían a su alcance. Esta no pretende ser una reconstrucción histórica definitiva, sino una interpretación basada en criterios estructurales, funcionales e históricos.

What happens when my most successful design meets one of my newest design series? My firefighting pen holders have become a huge part of my MakerWorld journey – and my Fog Nozzle Pen Holder is still my most successful design ever . At the same time, MPAS has grown into a complete modular pool accessory system, now including its own series of pool fountains. So... it was probably only a matter of time before these two worlds collided. 😄 The result is the MPAS Pool Fountain “FireHero” . 🚒💦 Based on the design language of my popular Fog Nozzle Pen Holder and combined with the MPAS Pool Fountain “Pure” , FireHero turns your pool fountain into a firefighting-themed highlight. And yes – this time, the nozzle actually sprays water. 😄 Important – “Pure” is required FireHero is not a standalone MPAS Pool Fountain. It is an extension for my MPAS Pool Fountain “Pure” and requires Pure as its base. The complete FireHero assembly is attached to the front of Pure and should be glued in place as securely and watertight as possible. The water supply is connected externally to Pure via its 1" thread . Please keep in mind that FDM printed parts are not automatically watertight. Before use, I strongly recommend sealing all water-carrying printed parts with clear coat, Dichtol or another suitable sealing product. All connections should also be glued as watertight as possible. Use a sufficient amount of suitable adhesive – in this case, a little too much glue is better than too little. 😄 Even small gaps between the parts may cause water to leak. Assembly The connector part installed inside the coupling and glued to the neck of Pure has an “UP” marking on one side. This marking must face upwards during assembly! The orientation of this part determines the final position of the complete nozzle assembly and ensures that the fog nozzle is positioned the right way up. So before applying glue: Find “UP”, check the orientation, then glue. 😄The red lever on top of the nozzle is purely decorative and has no function . It does not start, stop or regulate the water flow. Water Pattern The spray pattern and range shown in the photos were created with my own pool setup. The actual result may vary depending on pump performance, water flow and the complete hose setup. About the MPAS - Modular Pool Accessory System The MPAS aims to provide a simple solution for attaching a range of accessories to different pools. The installation is done through standardized brackets, to which various modules can be attached. you will find all available MPAS Modules in my Maker World MPAS Collection . Note: The models in the pictures were printed from PLA. For outdoor use, ASA filament should be used due to its UV resistance. You can also use PETG for more strength.

description: A parametric pet bowl riser designed to give your pet better posture while eating. Raising the bowl to the right height can make a real difference, especially for larger cats and dogs. Fully parametric, so you can dial in the exact fit for your pet and your bowl. Parameters: outer_diameter - the outer diameter of the riser in mm. The difference between outer and inner is always 20mm. inner_diameter - your bowl's diameter plus 10mm . This is what determines the actual fit for your bowl. leg_length - the length of the legs in mm. A note on leg length The riser adds 20mm total height on its own, 10mm from the bottom base and 10mm from the top rim. So when calculating your desired leg length, subtract 20mm from your target height first. Finding the right height for your pet Every cat and dog is different. A quick search online for your specific breed will usually give you a good target height to aim for. This one was built for a Maine Coon using 70mm legs. My example settings My bowl has a diameter of 185mm, so I used inner_diameter 195mm and outer_diameter 215mm with 70mm legs. Print settings No supports needed. Printed in Bambu Lab PLA Pure, since it is food adjacent and safety matters here. Once you downloaded the generated model, just split it into separate objects in Bambu Studio. Updates: Update 21th Jul 2026: I've added separate files for the legs, bottom and top, so mobile users can generate them without the need to split them. Be aware you use the same the settings! description: This compact gravity-dispensing water dish is sized for jumping spiders and other small terrarium inhabitants. I was inspired by this model , but designed this version from scratch with a more natural rocky look and a fully printable water tank instead of requiring a separate vial. The removable 10 ml tank automatically replenishes the dish, while the anti-drowning gyroid infill provides secure footing and minimizes exposed open water. The tank includes a built-in air channel that allows water to dispense properly. A small triangle on top points toward the outlet cutout, making it easy to orient the tank during installation. Features Removable 10 ml water tank (fully printable) Gravity-fed water replenishment Anti-drowning gyroid infill Natural rocky aesthetic Compact size for small terrariums Cutouts sized for 8 x 2 mm magnets Dedicated tank profiles for transparent PETG and regular PLA Filling and Installing the Tank The water dish must be completely removed from the terrarium for refilling. Fill the tank with water. Hold the water dish upside down. Orient the tank with its outlet cutout pointing toward the back. The triangle on top indicates the direction of the cutout. Insert the tank, then flip the complete water dish into its normal upright position. Some water should begin flowing into the dish. Add a little more water directly to the dish until it reaches the top of the gyroid infill. This helps establish the flow from the tank. Rotate the tank so the outlet cutout points toward the front. Use a paper towel to briefly dab away any water standing above the gyroid. Use short dabs so the paper towel doesn't begin drawing water from the tank. Return the complete water dish to the terrarium. Printing Please use one of the included print profiles without rebuilding the setup manually in the slicer. The gyroid section, tank opening, and magnet cutouts are created using mesh modifiers and negative parts, so the original object settings need to remain intact. The gyroid infill percentage is carefully tuned for proper water flow from the tank. Do not change the gyroid infill percentage , as doing so may cause the dish to dispense too much or too little water. The water tank includes separate profiles for: Transparent PETG: Prints very slowly with the cooling fan disabled to improve transparency and watertightness. Regular PLA: Uses vase mode to produce a watertight tank and doesn't require the slower transparent PETG settings. For either tank profile, retain the included adaptive layer height and vase mode settings . Changing these settings may prevent the tank from printing correctly or holding water reliably. Magnet Sizing The included magnet cutouts are sized for 8 x 2 mm magnets . Because the holes are negative parts in the slicer, they can be resized before printing if you're using different magnets. You must fix the magnets in place using superglue.

PRESENT THE 4 PARTS OF SEA SLIDING THE ON THE CROSS TO MAKE SURE EVERY THING MATCHES. IF EVERYTHING IS CORRECTLLY PLACED YOU CAN JOIN THEM ALL AND GLUE THE FOR PARTS. THIS IS THE MOMENT OF SELECTING THE ORIENTATION YOU WANT YOUR OCEAN TO BE IN. MAKE SURE TO GLUE THE CROSS WITH THE WALL MOINT HOLE IN THE CORRECT PLACE AND HERE AGAIN I SUGGEST DOING A PLASTIC WELD BETWEEN OCEAN PARTS AND CROSS. PUT TOGETHER THE 4 FRAME PIECES, GLUE THEM AND AGAIN, IF POSSIBLE, DO A PLASTIC WELD. NOW YOU CAN ADD THE LED STRIP OF YOUR CHOICE. YOU´LL NEED EXACTLY 1.5 METERS OF LED STRIP. GLUE IT TO THE UPPER PART OF THE SIDE WALL OF THE FRAME AND PASS THE CONNECTION THROUHG THE OPENNING OF THE FRAME. THE OPENNING SHOULD BE THE PART YOU´LL PUT LOOKING DOWNWARD OR TOWARD YOU POWER CONNECTION. YOU NOW HAVE EVERYTHING DONE. ALL THAT REST IS PUTTING THE FRAM AND THE OCEAN PART TOGETHER. THIS IS WHAT IT SHOULD LOOK LIKE ONCE FINISHED (IF YOU DECIDE TO PAINT IT). FOR THOSE INTERESTED IN PAINTING IT, I USED REGULAR ACRILIC PAINT. FIRST DID AN ENTIRE COAT OF A MEDIUM TONE OF BLUE. THEN WITH A LIGHTER BLUE I STARTED PAINTING WITHOUT COVERING THE DEEP PARTS. LAST STEP WAS TO PUT A VERY WHITE TONE OF BLUE TO THE HIGN SPOTS. I HOPE ANYONE TAKING A TRY TO THIS PROYECT HAS THE SAME FUN I DID. IT´S EASIER THEN IT LOOKS AND FOR THE SIZE (ALMOST 50CM OF DIAMETER), IT TAKES LESS THEN A ROLL OF FILAMENT. ENJOY!

description: Frame artwork, pictures, tiles, signs, and more. FrameMaker is a fully parametric OpenSCAD generator for pictures, relief tiles, artwork, signs, cards, and other display inserts. Start with a simple hollow frame, then add styled edges, captions, content support, swivel retainers, and mounting features as needed. Click Customize to open the generator. 🚀 Quick Start 1. Define the Frame Enter the nominal width and height of your insert. Opening Clearance is added on every side, while Border Width and Frame Depth control the surrounding frame. Round the inner opening and outer corners independently. 2. Style and Personalize Choose a flat, chamfered, rounded, concave, ogee, or stepped edge. Add an optional aligned caption to any side, then emboss, engrave, or iron it onto the face. The selected border can expand automatically, or the text can shrink to fit. 3. Support the Contents Choose how the frame should support and load its contents: No Lip — a simple full-depth hollow frame Front Retaining Lip — covers the front edge of contents loaded from the rear Rear Support Lip — supports contents loaded from the front without covering their face Front-retaining frames can also include four or eight printable swivel retainers with matching pilot holes. 4. Mount, Preview, and Export Add an automatically fitted keyhole or two, four, or six rear magnet pockets. Use All Parts for printing, select individual parts when needed, or inspect the frame upright with Assembled . ⭐ Features Direct Dimensions Control the insert, clearance, border, and depth independently. Flexible Frame Styling Combine six edge treatments with independent inner and outer rounding. Measured Captions Fit aligned text on any side with three surface treatments. Optional Content Support Build a hollow, front-retaining, or rear-supported frame. Hardware-Aware Details Generate fitted retainers, keyholes, and balanced magnet pockets. 📜 Maker Scripts ℹ️ Notes For guidance, explanations, tips, and troubleshooting, see the FAQ. Secure swivel retainers with low-profile button-head screws driven into the pilot holes. Use screws long enough to engage securely without reaching the front face. description: # 🌿 Alocasia Azlanii Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Wer schon einmal dekorative Pflanzentöpfe mit aufwendigen Blattmotiven skaliert hat, kennt das Problem: Wandstärken verändern sich, Details werden unsauber und das Design verliert an Wirkung. Deshalb erhältst du hier vier separat angepasste Größen, die jeweils speziell für ihre Größe optimiert wurden. Jeder Topf trägt ein plastisch ausgearbeitetes **Azlanii Blatt**, das besonders bei einfarbigen Drucken hervorragend zur Geltung kommt und den Töpfen ihren charakteristischen Look verleiht. --- # 💧 Selbstbewässerungssystem Alle Größen wurden für die Nutzung als Selbstbewässerungstopf ausgelegt. Der eigentliche Pflanztopf sitzt im oberen Bereich. Darunter befindet sich ein separates Wasserreservoir. Über einen Kapillardocht, der durch die Bodenöffnungen des Orchideen- oder Aroid-Topfes geführt wird, kann die Pflanze selbstständig Wasser aus dem Reservoir aufnehmen. Dadurch wird eine gleichmäßige Wasserversorgung ermöglicht und die Gießintervalle können deutlich verlängert werden. Bei allen Größen wurde darauf geachtet, dass die Innentöpfe bequem von oben entnommen werden können, ohne im Topfinneren hantieren zu müssen. --- # 👀 Sichtfenster (optional) Auf der Rückseite befindet sich ein Sichtfenster, durch das sich Wasserstand und Wurzelentwicklung bequem kontrollieren lassen, ohne den Innentopf herausnehmen zu müssen. Das Sichtfenster ist als optionales Negativ ausgeführt und kann im Bambu Studio bei Bedarf aktiviert oder deaktiviert werden. ### Mit Sichtfenster ✅ Kontrolle des Wasserstands ✅ Kontrolle der Wurzelentwicklung ✅ Ideal für Orchideen, Alocasien und andere Aroid-Pflanzen ### Ohne Sichtfenster ✅ Geschlossene Außenwand ✅ Nutzung als Dekoration ✅ Nutzung als Vase ✅ Nutzung als Stiftehalter ✅ Nutzung als allgemeines Aufbewahrungsgefäß --- # 📏 Größen ## Größe S * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **6 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **100 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Einfaches Einsetzen und Herausnehmen des Innentopfes --- ## Größe M * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **7,6 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **200 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Einfaches Einsetzen und Herausnehmen des Innentopfes --- ## Größe L * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **9 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **400 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Ideal für größere Pflanzen mit höherem Wasserbedarf --- ## Größe XL * Passend für einen **10 cm Aroid-Topf** * Der Aroid-Topf ist tiefer und ragt bewusst leicht über den oberen Rand hinaus * Dadurch lässt sich der Innentopf besonders komfortabel entnehmen * Wasserreservoir: **500 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Aroid-Topf geführt werden zum Beispiel: Becher: https://amzn.eu/d/01GtIsBM https://www.variegata.de/produkt/toepfchen-der-toepfe/ AROID TÖPFE https://www.sybotanica.com/de-de/products/dursichtiger-plfanzentopf S und m 9 cm Klarsicht-Orchideentopf https://www.obi.de/p/2807519/ --- # ⚠️ Wichtiger Hinweis Die Druckdateien enthalten ausschließlich die dekorativen Außentöpfe. Folgende Komponenten sind **nicht Bestandteil der STL-Dateien**: * Orchideentöpfe * Aroid-Töpfe * Kunststoffbecher für die Wasserreservoirs * Kapillardocht Diese Komponenten müssen separat beschafft werden. description: Keep three drinks cool with a pair of reusable, refillable ice packs designed specifically around standard beverage cans. The shaped surfaces fit around three standard 330 ml cans, creating a compact and stable cooling bundle. The cans can be arranged either vertically or horizontally, making the system suitable for cooler bags, lunch bags, picnics, camping, road trips and outdoor activities. The central mast bears the entire bending moment of the cantilevered crossbars and requires maximum Z-axis shear strength. Crossbar Walls: Set to a minimum of 3 Wall Loops to safely support the weight of the birds without snapping. Material: PETG is highly recommended over PLA for its superior layer adhesion and impact resistance. [Customization Tip] Hemp Rope Wrapping: You can wrap the crossbars with hemp rope to enhance texture, improve grip, and add more fun for your birds. Medusa's Temple – Illuminated Greek Temple Legends speak of a forgotten sanctuary hidden among the mountains, where offerings were accepted long after the last priest had vanished. At its heart, a mysterious altar continued to glow beneath the watchful gaze of Medusa. Some believed the gods had abandoned the sanctuary. Others believed they had never left. About this model Inspired by classical Greek architecture, this semicircular temple is designed as a decorative display piece that combines detailed architecture with atmospheric lighting. Every part is printed separately for clean color separation and straightforward assembly. At the heart of the temple stands a magical altar bearing the image of Medusa, glowing with an eerie green light. The altar features inductive lighting, allowing compatible objects placed upon it to illuminate without visible electrical connections, as though they have been blessed by the gods. Lighting The model is designed around the Maker's Supply Wireless Inductive Coil Kit . The transmitter is hidden inside the base while the receiver is integrated into the removable altar centerpiece. Compatible wireless objects placed on the altar will illuminate without visible wiring. Printing The altar is best printed using a small layer height to preserve the fine details, especially on the removable centerpiece. While a 0.2 mm nozzle will produce the sharpest results, it is certainly not required—the entire altar has been successfully printed with a standard 0.4 mm nozzle. The optional Medusa pediment insert contains much finer details than the standard roof front and is therefore best printed with a 0.2 mm nozzle. If you're printing with a 0.4 mm nozzle, I recommend using the standard roof front, which features an engraved inscription and prints beautifully with larger nozzles. Filament Recommendations I experimented with several filament colors before settling on the final combination. I first printed the temple in Bambu PLA Basic Jade White, but the architectural details blended together more than I had hoped. I then tried Bambu PLA Matte Desert Tan, which brought out the details beautifully, but the overall appearance felt a little too dark for the look I wanted. For the model shown in the photos, I settled on the following filament combination after experimenting with several colors: Temple, Floor, Pillars, Roof: Bambu PLA Basic Light Gray Altar, Rock border and Tile grout: Bambu PLA Basic Dark Gray Altar centerpiece: Bambu PLA Basic Bronze Parts used All required components are listed in the Bill of Materials (BOM). Parametric Pill Columns Tray Generator (Modular Design) Create high-quality custom trays for organization, gifts, or home decor in the modern "pill columns" style. This project was developed to offer maximum flexibility: simply adjust the dimensions, and the script seamlessly recalculates the vertical column distribution around the perimeter, maintaining a flawless geometry designed for support-free 3D printing. Perfect for both personal use and the production of unique, exclusive pieces. --- DETAILED PARAMETER MANUAL --- 1. Basic Settings - Tray Shape: - Oval: Generates a classic stadium-shaped tray (straight sides with semi-circular ends). Perfect for keys, perfumes, or glasses. - Rectangular: Generates a rectangular tray with customizable rounded corners. Great for organizing boxes, drawers, or office items. - Tray Length and Width: The absolute maximum exterior bounds of the tray (measured in millimeters). The script uses these dimensions as constraints and automatically scales the column count to fit exactly inside these bounds. Note: Width must be less than or equal to Length. - Column Height: The total height of the boundary columns from the base to the top (mm). This determines how deep the tray cavity is. - Base Thickness: The height of the tray's bottom floor (mm). A value of 3mm is recommended to ensure structural rigidity, prevent warping during printing, and allow safe depth for bottom engravings without breaching the interior floor. 2. Pill Columns Style Settings - Column Radius: Half of the column's thickness (mm). A smaller radius (e.g., 3.3mm) yields many small, delicate columns, while a larger radius (e.g., 8mm or 10mm) results in fewer, chunkier pillars. - Lateral Overlap: Controls how deep adjacent columns merge into each other (expressed as a percentage: e.g., 0.15 = 15%). - Lower values (0.0 to 0.10): Columns barely touch, creating deep, sharp V-valleys on the outside (warning: values close to 0 make the print structurally weak). - Ideal values (0.15 to 0.25): Columns merge perfectly to form a strong, watertight, cohesive outer wall with a smooth, pleasing texture. - Higher values (0.30+): Columns interpenetrate deeply, flattening the outer texture. - Top Style: - Round: Finishes the top of each column with a smooth, spherical dome. This gives a very soft, organic look. - Flat: Cuts the columns flat at the top. Recommended if you want a clean, modern, architectural look. - Top Bevel Radius: Only active when Top Style is set to Flat (mm). It rounds off the sharp top edge of the flat pillars. A bevel of 1.0mm is recommended to eliminate sharp corners, make the top feel premium to the touch, and prevent print delamination. - Inner Wall Style: - Wavy: The inner wall mimics the wavy, scalloped shape of the columns. This looks highly organic and consistent but forms internal valleys that can catch dust or soap. - Smooth: A clean, flat inner wall is sliced directly into the columns. This creates a flat interior face, making it extremely easy to wipe clean and ensuring objects placed inside sit flat against the wall without catching. 3. Column Cross-Section Shape - Column Cross Section: - Round: Classic circular pillars. - Oval: Eliptical pillars. This allows you to squeeze or stretch the columns. - Oval Aspect Ratio: Only active when Column Cross Section is set to Oval. It scales the column's width along the perimeter path while keeping its radial thickness constant. - Values > 1.0 (e.g., 1.35): Stretches the columns along the perimeter, making the columns look wider and flatter horizontally. - Value = 1.0: Standard circular columns. - Values < 1.0 (e.g., 0.80): Squishes the columns, making them thinner along the perimeter and deeper radially. 4. Advanced and Customization Settings - Corner Radius: Only active when Tray Shape is set to Rectangular (mm). Controls the rounding radius of the tray's outer corners. Must be larger than the Column Radius. - Enable Top Text and Top Text Height: Adds raised (embossed) 3D text (such as a name or brand name) to the center of the tray's interior floor. You can configure the font size and height (typically 1.0mm is ideal). - Enable Bottom Logo and Engraving Depth: Engraves (debosses) a signature text, brand name, or website handle (e.g., @brand) into the bottom face of the tray base. The engraving uses standard text fonts. The depth is automatically limited to prevent piercing the base. Since it is engraved inwards, it does not affect the tray's stability on flat tables. - Display Mode: - Full: Renders the complete model ready for STL export. - Base Only / Border Only: Isolates parts to inspect details. - Cross Section: Cuts the model in half longitudinal to inspect wall thickness, internal clearances, and engraving depths before printing. description: Ultimate Onion Slicer Update 23/07/2026 : une V2 est désormais disponible ! Elle apporte plusieurs améliorations de conception : structure plus robuste, meilleure durabilité, temps d’impression réduit et emboîtement optimisé entre les deux parties du modèle. description: Modular Curtain Track System This modular curtain track system is infinitely extendable. You will find individual parts on separate print plates, allowing you to print exactly the quantity you need. Alternatively, there is a print plate containing 7 track segments and 2 end caps . Each track segment is 220 mm long. Seven segments are sufficient for a standard patio or balcony door and work well with most standard curtains. I joined the track segments using a small amount of super glue (cyanoacrylate) . Simply apply a thin layer of glue to each connector before pushing the pieces together. For best results, assemble the track on a long, flat surface such as a kitchen countertop. This helps keep the track perfectly straight while the glue cures. Once dry, the complete track is surprisingly rigid, even over longer distances. I mounted the finished track to the ceiling using thick transparent double-sided mounting tape . I intentionally avoided screws because I did not want to drill into reinforced concrete. Depending on your ceiling, you may prefer a different mounting method. Do not glue the end caps in place! They should remain removable so you can take the gliders out whenever you need to remove your curtains for washing. 😉 Final Thoughts The system performs surprisingly well and glides much more smoothly than expected. description: 💡 LOOP Lamp - Minimalist LED Table Lamp (Japandi Style) 📖 Description Welcome to my design of the LOOP Lamp ! This modern table lamp combines minimalist aesthetics with clever engineering. Inspired by the Japandi style (a fusion of Japanese and Scandinavian simplicity), this lamp is the perfect accent piece for any desk, side table, or as cozy ambient lighting. The Highlight: The entire design is engineered so that all cables and electronics are completely hidden inside the base! No cable clutter disrupts the clean geometry. The back of the base is closed flush with a custom-fit cover, ensuring the lamp looks flawless from every angle. Why you will love this model: Clever Cable Management: The internal cable routing from the LOOP ring into the base features a beveled edge . This ensures that the LED strip cable glides smoothly into the hollow compartment without any sharp kinks. Modular Design: The lamp consists of just a few, easy-to-assemble parts. Ready for Electronics: The base features precise, pre-designed cutouts for a standard screw-in DC power jack. 🔧 Required Hardware (BOM) In addition to the 3D-printed parts, you will need the following components: LED Strip: A 12V or 24V COB LED strip is highly recommended to avoid individual light dots and create a seamless band of light (approx. 50-60 cm / 20-24 inches in length). IMPORTANT: The COB strip must be max. 8 mm wide ! Power Supply: A matching 12V or 24V power adapter (ideally with an inline switch). Power Connector: A screw-in DC power jack (female panel mount). IMPORTANT: The thread diameter of the jack must be around 7.6 mm Wiring: Thin stranded wire for soldering and a soldering iron. Adhesive: Superglue (CA glue) or 2-part epoxy. 🛠️ Assembly Instructions (Step-by-Step) Prepare the Base: Take the LOOP ring and the base. Carefully apply adhesive (superglue or epoxy) to the contact surface of the ring and press it firmly onto the base. ATTENTION: Pay close attention to ensure that the small cable hole at the bottom of the ring aligns perfectly with the opening at the top of the base! Mount the LEDs: Peel off the protective film from your COB LED strip and stick it into the designated groove on the inside of the LOOP ring. Guide the end of the LED cable down through the beveled opening into the hollow base compartment. Thanks to the bevel, the cable will slide in without kinking. Insert the Diffuser: Carefully snap/click the printed diffuser ring into the LOOP ring. It should sit securely and cover the COB strip perfectly. Wire the Electronics: Mount the DC power jack into the cutout on the back of the base and screw it tight from the inside. Now, solder the cables from the LED strip to the jack inside the compartment. Attention: Make absolutely sure to observe the correct polarity (+/-), otherwise the LEDs will not light up! Finishing Touches: Snap the cover flush onto the back of the base to cleanly seal the electronics compartment. You're done! Plug in the power supply and enjoy your new LOOP Lamp!

description: Tired of not finding a practical system to make your own roller blinds? This is a complete, robust, and 100% DIY system designed for MakerWorld! This project allows you to create a custom roller blind at a very low cost. It uses a standard 22.5mm cylindrical wooden rod (readily available in any DIY or hardware store) and a smooth cord-pull mechanism. Key Highlights: Cost-Effective & Custom: Make it exactly to the dimensions of your windows without paying a premium. Versatile Mounting: Supports can be screwed directly into either the ceiling or the wall. Easy Maintenance: The clever slider design allows you to easily unhook and remove the brackets to wash the fabric. Smooth Operation: Features a 4-roller system acting as mechanical bearings for a frictionless roll. Bill of Materials (Printed Parts) 2x End Caps (to glue onto the ends of the wooden rod) 4x Rollers (mechanical wheels for smooth rotation) 1x Left Bracket 1x Right Bracket 2x Base Mounts (The sliding brackets to screw into the wall/ceiling) Hardware Required (Non-Printed) 1x Cylindrical wooden rod (22.5mm diameter). 1x Fabric curtain (cut and hemmed to your window size). 2x Screws and wall anchors (adapted to your wall or ceiling material). 1x Cord (approximately twice the total length of your curtain). Tools: Wood glue (to secure the end caps) and, to attach the fabric to the wood I personnally used staples but feel free to propose any alternative ! Step-by-Step Assembly Guide Prepare the fabric: Cut your fabric to your window's width and length, then hem the edges. Glue the 3D-printed end caps to both ends of the wooden rod. Attach the fabric to the wooden rod using staple for example Assemble the brackets (put the 4 rollers into their designated place, they are purposely loose but any proposal to improve that part is highly welcomed !) Mount the little rail to the wall / ceiling using a screw. Do a test to ensure they are properly placed with regard to the wooden rod length with their caps: Measure the exact distance needed, then screw the two Base Mounts into your wall or ceiling. Slide the left and right brackets onto them. Set up the cord: Wind the cord around the wheel (to ensure the cord doesn't slide around the cap I had to make 3 turns around the caps) of the dedicated end cap. Place the wooden rod assembly into the bracket rollers. Test the pull mechanism!

model_name: Scales of Injustice: The Weight of Society
description: This thought-provoking and highly detailed sculpture serves as a powerful allegory for societal inequality. As seen in the reference file image_313d45.jpg , the piece depicts an emaciated, struggling figure bearing the literal and figurative weight of a larger, dominant figure holding a staff and the scales of justice. This model is perfect for makers who appreciate classical-style, meaningful art pieces that spark conversation. The intricate details—from the strained musculature and visible ribs of the lower figure to the draped cloth and delicate balance scales—make this a highly rewarding print for those looking to test their printer's capabilities. Recommended Filaments: To achieve a traditional sculpted look, this model looks phenomenal in Matte PLA, Marble PLA, or Wood-fill PLA. A simple wash or dry-brush painting technique can further bring out the depth of the procedural and sculpted details. Recommended Print Settings: Layer Height: 0.12mm - 0.16mm (Lower layer heights are highly recommended to capture the facial details and the fine structure of the scales). Infill: 10% - 15% Gyroid or Cubic (High infill isn't necessary, but a sturdy pattern ensures the upper body has enough internal support). Supports: Yes, absolutely required. Pro-tip: Use Tree/Organic Supports to navigate the complex overhangs, particularly for the extended arms, the staff, the hanging scales, and the underside of the upper figure. Ensure your support interface settings are dialed in so they break away cleanly from the highly detailed areas. Brim: Recommended (especially if printing at a larger scale, to ensure the square base stays perfectly flat and avoids warping). Orientation: Print standing upright as imported. Happy printing! Please share your makes and painted versions in the comments—I'd love to see how your prints turn out!

Ich habe diese Futter-Spielzeuge entwickelt, weil mir die Auswahl an erhältlichen interaktiven Katzenspielzeugen zu klein und wenig abwechslungsreich war. Meine beiden Main Coons liebten die ersten neuen Herausforderungen und so erweitert sich meine Sammlung interaktiver Spielzeuge immer weiter, welche meine Katzen geistig herausfordern und immer wieder aufs Neue beschäftigen. Jedes Spielzeug bietet eine andere Aufgabe und ist unterschiedlich schwer (Tabelle der Spielzeuge und Schwierigkeiten am Ende). Allerdings sind alle Modelle seit über einem Jahr regelmäßig bei meinen beiden Katzen im Einsatz und funktionieren noch immer einwandfrei. Damit das Interesse erhalten bleibt, verwende ich in der Regel nur zwei bis drei Spielzeuge gleichzeitig. So können sich die Katzen auf eine Herausforderung konzentrieren, anstatt von zu vielen Optionen gleichzeitig abgelenkt zu werden. Geeignet für Trockenfutter oder kleine Leckerlis. Beschäftigt Katzen über lange Zeit, fördert ihren Entdeckerinstinkt und sie essen langsamer. Kein AMS oder Mehrfarbendruck erforderlich – alle Modelle sind für den Ein-Farbendruck entwickelt. Die Spielzeuge können miteinander verbunden werden, um eine größere Spielfläche zu bieten Die Favoriten meiner Katzen Nach über einem Jahr Nutzung haben sich einige klare Favoriten herauskristallisiert: Löcherkarton Rolle Abgedeckte Löcher Auch der Tunnel , der Vulkan und die Welle sorgen regelmäßig für viel Beschäftigung. Manche Katzen werden daran vermutlich eine Weile tüfteln, manche auch aufgeben – aber mit etwas Geduld und Konzentration ist die Aufgabe definitiv lösbar. 🖨️ Druck- und Pflegehinweise Alle Modelle und Druckeinstellungen habe ich für den Druck optimiert und lassen sich ohne AMS drucken. Meine Empfehlungen: Das neue PLA-Pure ist das Perfekte Material für diese Spielzeuge. Es ist sicher und nach hohen EU-Standards zertifiziert. Mit diesem Material muss man keine Sorge haben, dass deine Katzen schädliche Stoffe beim Fressen von Trocken oder Nassfutter aufnehmen. (Das Material selbst sollte trotzdem nicht gegessen werden, es ist immer noch Plastik!) Bei der Verwendung von ausschließlich Trockenfutter bei den Spielzeugen, was ich auch empfehle, kann auch das normale PLA Basic verwendet werden. Bitte beachte die jeweiligen Druckprofile der einzelnen Modelle. Die lange Druckzeit resultiert aus dem Glätten der unteren Flächen. Das Glätten sorgt für einen besseren Abschluss der Oberflächen. Wenn es dort zu Problemen kommt, liegt das an der Kalibrierung des Druckers, an einem abgebrauchten Druckkopf oder evtl. zu nasses Filament. Verwende Supports nur dort, wo sie in der Modelldatei empfohlen werden. Reinigung Die Reinigung ist bewusst einfach gehalten. In allen Fällen reichen warmes Wasser, etwas Spülmittel und ein weiches Tuch vollkommen aus. Bei geschlossenen Bereichen – beispielsweise im Inneren der Rolle – gelangt man nicht überall direkt mit einem Tuch hin. Hier genügt es, das Spielzeug mehrfach mit Wasser und etwas Spülmittel auszuspülen. Bei zu häufiger Reinigung könnte sich Kleber lösen. Einfach das Spielzeug wieder zusammenkleben. Ich empfehle, die Spielzeuge möglichst nach jeder Nutzung zu reinigen. In der Praxis reinige ich meine eigenen Modelle allerdings meist nur etwa einmal pro Monat. Durch das von mir verwendete Trockenfutter bleiben sie trotzdem überraschend sauber. Je nach verwendetem Futter können deine Erfahrungen natürlich unterschiedlich ausfallen. Automatischer Katzentrinkbrunnen Trinkbrunnen für Katzen, kleine Hunde und mehr. Je nach Größe eures Haustieres könnt ihr die Größe gerne anpassen. Dazu einfach im Bambu-Studio Skalieren. Für die Wasserförderung habe ich folgende Pumpe verwendet: https://funduinoshop.com/elektronische-module/ventile-pumpen/pumpen/miniatur-wasserpumpe-3v-5v-100-200ma-1m-kabel Funktioniert aber auch mit anderen Pumpen, z.B. USB betriebene aus diversen bekannten Onlineshops. Aber bitte auf die Größe, Fördermenge und den Schlauchanschluss der Pumpe achten. In Original Größe hat der Trinkbrunnen die Maße: 175*175*172 cm (+ Aufsatz) Dort hat die Öffnung für die Pumpe eine Größe von: 6,5*5,4 cm Wie auf den Bildern zu sehen habe ich den Trinkbrunnen noch in einer kleineren Version (70%) geruckt. Die Maße sind: ca. 12*12*11,5 cm (+ Aufsatz) Und die Öffnung für die Pumpe hat eine Größe von ca.: 4,5*3,8 cm Für die Version in 70% gibt es außerdem eine Unterlage auf der Drucktaster montiert werden können, So läuft die Pumpe nur dann wenn sie betätigt wird. Tipps zum Druck: Achtet vor dem Druck darauf in welcher Version ihr den Brunnen Drucken wollt! Soll es Mit Unterlage und Schaltern sein achtet bitte auf den Bauraum eures Druckers und passt die Größe dementsprechend an. Gerne könnt ihr dafür die Druckdatei Katzenbrunnen 70% nutzen dies sollte mit den meisten Druckern funktionieren. Achtet darauf möglichst viel Wandlinien (ich habe 5 verwendet) zu nutzen damit es auch Dicht wird. Supports sollten Aktiviert sein. Es gibt 2 Versionen vom Brunnen, Eine Version hat vorne und seitlich Öffnungen für die Kabel der Schalter, Die andere Version hat nur hinten eine Öffnung für ein Kabel (z.b.) für USB Pumpen. Schaut euch dazu gern die Rohmodelldateien an. In den Druckdateien seht ihr das es 3 Verschiedene Aufsätze/Wasserauslässe gibt. Am besten ausprobieren welcher bei eurem Haustier am besten angenommen wird. Die Druckdateien: Katzenbrunnen → Das ist nur die einfache Brunnendatei, ohne Löcher für Kabel usw. Katzenbrunnen mehrteilig → Der Brunnen in Originalgröße + mehrteilige Unterlage für die Drucktaster. Katzenbrunnen 70% → Die größe auf 70% nach unten Skalliert, damit ist die Unterlage für die Drucktaster knapp 25x25cm und kann mit den meisten Druckern am Stück gedruckt werden. Die Aufsätze/Wasserauslässe sind schon in der richtigen Größe beigefügt. Aufsätze → Die 3 verschiedenen Aufsätze/Wasserauslässe. Schlauchadapter → 4 Verschiedene Schlauchadapter. Zusammenbau: Das Kabel der Pumpe von oben durch die vorgesehene Öffnung führen, im Unterteil des Brunnens ist genügend Platz für ein Batteriepack, Stecker oder einfach um das übrige Kabel aufzuwickeln. Wollt ihr die Pumpe auch per Batteriepack betreiben empfiehlt es sich sie über einen Druckschalter steuern. Dafür in die vorbereiteten Locher einen Taster einkleben und die Kabel in den Unterteil des Brunnens verlegen. Wie auf den Bildern zu sehen habe ich 2 Taster benutzt, Je nach Bauart und Größe können auch mehr verwendet werden. Wichtig ist die Taster Parallel zueinander anzuschließen (Dann genügt es wenn ein Taster gedrückt wird). Für die Druckdatei Katzenbrunnen mehrteilig (in Originalgröße) Ist die Taster Unterlage zu groß um am Stück gedruckt zu werden, darum muss diese in 3 Teilen gedruckt und dann zusammengeklebt werden. Der Rest ist gleich. Je nachdem was ihr für eine Pumpe bzw. Schlauch verwendet kann es sein das ihr einen Schlauchadapter benötigt, dafür einfach den passenden aus der Druckdatei auswählen. description: 萌系黑龙/夜煞桌面摆件与屏幕挂件（3D 打印款）完整说明 一、项目主要特点 双形态互动设计： 巧妙的重心与姿态设计，使其既能像趴在屏幕边缘的“监工”一样稳稳挂在显示器上，也能作为独立的立体公仔稳固地站立在平坦的桌面上，兼顾实用与趣味。 超精细仿生鳞片： 尽管是 Q 版造型，但模型体表布满了极其精细的微缩龙鳞与皮革般的肌理纹路，极大地提升了手办的精致度与高级感。 分件灵动大眼： 标志性的超大眼睛极其适合分件打印（或多色 AMS 打印）。黑白分明的灵动大眼不仅是整个模型的灵魂，也大大降低了手残党的涂装门槛。 萌系治愈比例： 采用大头小身子、短手短脚的经典 Q 版拟人化比例，配合充满好奇的无辜神态，能瞬间融化打工人的心。 二、适用场景 & 适配人群 适用场景 电脑桌面 Setup： 绝佳的显示器屏幕挂件或机箱内部装饰，为冰冷的数码办公空间增添一丝奇幻与温馨。 车载治愈萌物： 配合无痕胶固定在车载中控台或屏幕上方，陪伴你的每一次出行。 潮玩盲盒展示： 独立站立姿态极其适合摆放在展示柜中，与其他动漫手办或盲盒完美契合。 适配人群 奇幻动画/萌宠爱好者： 对《驯龙高手》等奇幻 IP 中忠诚、可爱的龙形生物毫无抵抗力的玩家。 办公桌“软装”达人： 喜欢用各种治愈系小物件打造个性化工位、缓解工作压力的上班族。 3D 打印手办玩家： 追求高精度皮肤质感表现，喜欢给模型进行眼部点睛涂装的手工爱好者。 三、3D 打印设置（0.4mm 标准喷嘴通用参数） 为了完美还原极其细密的皮肤鳞片，确保这只小黑龙拥有高级的手办质感，建议参考以下切片参数： 层高（Layer Height）： 强烈建议使用 0.12mm - 0.16mm。头顶与背部等平缓的圆弧区域建议开启“动态层高（Adaptive Layers）”，以彻底消除顶部的等高线台阶。 墙数量 / 外轮廓（Walls / Perimeters）： 3 层。多层外墙能让表面的微小鳞片起伏更加立体扎实。 填充率（Infill）： 10% - 15%。推荐使用 聚 Gyroid（陀螺仪） 填充。若打算将其主要作为屏幕挂件，较低的填充率能减轻整体重量，使其挂在屏幕上时重心更稳。 打印速度： 外部可见区域（Outer Wall）建议降速控制在 40-60 mm/s，慢速不仅能大幅提升哑光耗材的表面光泽一致性，还能确保每一片微小的鳞片细节不糊、不拉丝。 四、补充打印 & 组装建议 尺寸缩放参考： 屏幕挂件款（80–100mm）： 专门为显示器定制的最佳尺寸，不挡视线，小巧灵动。 (注：缩放前请先使用卡尺测量您显示器边框的厚度，确保缩放后龙爪与身体的间隙能够刚好卡住您的屏幕边缘) 。 桌面标准款（120–150mm）： 适合作为独立的手办摆件放在鼠标垫旁或书架上，体表的鳞片细节表现力最强。 超大镇宅款（180mm以上）： 适合拥有大尺寸打印机的玩家，极致放大后的鳞片犹如真实的爬行动物皮肤般震撼。 耗材与色彩推荐： 强烈建议使用哑光黑（Matte Black） 或带有极细微闪粉的 星空黑（Galaxy Black）耗材打印主体，能完美过滤掉廉价的塑料反光，复刻出深邃的高级皮革质感。 眼睛涂装/点睛小贴士： 如果是单色打印，眼睛部分可以用丙烯马克笔（白色打底，黑色画瞳孔）轻松涂装。强烈建议在纯黑的瞳孔边缘点上一抹白色的“高光”，这能让整只小龙瞬间注入灵魂，眼神变得极其清澈灵动。 屏幕安全固定技巧： 虽然模型设计有卡住屏幕的物理结构，但为了防止不小心触碰导致其掉落摔坏，建议在挂上屏幕时，在龙的腹部或前爪内侧贴一小粒蓝丁胶（Blu-Tack）或透明无痕纳米胶，既稳固又绝对不会损伤显示器屏幕。

WICHTIG!!! P1-/X1-User: Die Modelle sind 250 x 250mm groß. Standardmäßig passt das (anscheinend??) nicht auf Eure Druckplatte. Ich musste mich entscheiden: Entweder, ich skaliere generell herunter und Nicht -P1-/X1-User skalieren auf 250mm hoch, oder umgekehrt. Ich habe mich für Letzteres entschieden, weil mir wichtig war, im Standard die maximale Fläche anbieten zu können. Ihr könnt die Modelle also nutzen, musst dabei aber im Bambus Studio einfach nur X und Y auf Eure Druckplatte herunterskalieren. Thema Druckbetthaftung: Da jeder Drucker unterschiedlich ist, gebe ich grundsätzlich keine Filamenteinstellungen (Profile) mit . Ich habe selber häufig Probleme mit der Druckbetthaftung, trotz sauberer Platte, daher drucke ich auch fremde Modelle niemals mit den ausglieferten Filamentprofilen. Im Druckprofil wird die erste Schicht um 50% verlangsamt gedruckt. Bei meinem Drucker hatte ich die ersten 4 Schichten dann nochmal auf 50% Geschwindigkeit heruntergestellt und die Druckbetttemperatur auf 85° hochgestellt (beides direkt über das Display). Ihr solltet Euch also sicher sein, dass Ihr über eine sehr gute Druckbetthaftung verfügt; alternativ solltet Ihr wissen, was Ihr tun müsst, um diese bei Eurem Drucker (zielgerichtet) anzupassen bzw. zu verbessern. Und nun zum Modell: Dank unserer Hunde müssen wir stellenweise immer mal Rasen ausbessern. Bekanntermaßen gibt es bei Makerworld jede Menge “Rasen-Reparatur-Boxen”, aber mir persönlich verbrauchen die viel zu viel Filament (dafür, dass man nur 25 x 25cm Rasen herausbekommt) und ich bin kein Freund davon, den frisch gewachsenen Rasen aus der Box heraus “zu bewegen”. Ich wollte somit eine Lösung “direkt im Boden” haben und diese sollte auch deutlich weniger Filament verbrauchen. Das Ergebnis sind diese Gitter. Eine Anleitung kann ich mir sicherlich sparen - das sollte selbsterklärend sein. Notfalls: Siehe Foto… Aus Lust und Laune heraus habe ich ein wenig mit den Mustern herumgespielt - herausgekommen sind nun 5 Varianten, bei denen die Basis dieselbe ist und sie sich lediglich in der Optik, dem Filamenverbrauch und der Druckzeit unterschieden. Über Likes, Fotos, Kommentare und natürlich auch Boosts freue ich mich sehr! 🤗

description: Ultimate Air Conditioner Flared Air Deflector Control Your Room's Airflow ! This modular deflecting system redirects HVAC airflow laterally, preventing direct thermal drafting on specific room areas or occupants. The design incorporates a mounting bracket system that permits the rapid detachment of the deflector when airflow redirection is not required. 🌬️ Key Features Targeted Air Routing Modular Architecture Directional Options Quick-Release Mechanism Prints without support End Cap to direct airflow Test Template (look at the end of the description) 🎯 Scaling Length Adjustment: Alter the Z-axis height within slicing software (such as Bambu Studio) to match the desired span for your AC unit. 🛠️ Installation Notes Mounting Strategy: Secure a minimum of two brackets to the underside of the unit utilizing high-quality double-sided tape. The total number of brackets required is directly dependent on the shear strength of the chosen adhesive. Brackets Installation: Apply double-sided tape to the brackets and slide them onto the deflector. Test-fit the deflector under the AC to check your desired placement. Finally, peel off the tape's protective backing and stick the assembly firmly into place. CRITICAL WARNING: DO NOT USE Alien Tape style of double-sided tape . Using it to hang objects upside down subjects the tape to constant gravity, creating a continuous peeling force. This steady weight slowly stretches the viscoelastic gel—replicating the exact parallel pulling motion used to safely remove the tape—causing it to inevitably lose its grip and fail over time. 🧩 Optional End Cap Module: Airflow Maximization: Designed to seal the narrow end of the deflector as tightly as possible. This forces a maximum volume of air through the flared opening, rising efficiency. Customizable Clearance: Designed with an optimized wall thickness that is sturdy enough and permits physical modification. Users can manually trim or notch the cap to create custom relief profiles, ensuring it does not obstruct the specific sweep of the AC unit's moving mechanical louvers. Assembly Protocol: After trimming the cap to the required operational dimensions, permanently bond it to the narrow terminal of the main deflector utilizing Cyanoacrylate (CA / super glue) adhesive. 💡 Material Recommendations PLA: Strictly recommended for cooling-only applications. PETG: Mandatory if the HVAC unit will be utilized for thermal heating (winter mode), as it possesses the necessary thermal resistance to prevent structural warping. Double-sided tape: NO Alien Tape!!! 📦 Pro Tips Have the AC running and check if it has horizontal louvers to help redirect the air to the left or right. Execute a test fit with the template before committing filament to the full-scale deflector. Distribute the brackets evenly across the span of the unit to balance the load on the adhesive. 🧠 Design Rationale Aerodynamic Efficiency Why does a curved geometry outperform a conventional flat plane? A standard straight angle acts as an abrupt mechanical barrier, whereas a flared profile provides a streamlined transitional ramp for the conditioned air mass. Mitigation of Turbulent Flow Flat Deflectors: High-velocity air colliding with a rigid, flat angle induces severe flow separation and chaotic turbulence. This collision generates acoustic disruption (wind noise) and drastically limits overall air output speed. Flared Deflectors: The continuous curvature allows the air to glide cleanly along the surface. Maintaining this streamlined flow translates to significantly quieter operation and preserves output velocity. Reduction of Mechanical Strain (Backpressure): Flat Deflectors: Impacting a flat surface generates significant aerodynamic backpressure. This resistance forces the HVAC blower motor to work harder, increasing energy consumption and mechanical wear just to clear the exhaust port. Flared Deflectors: A curved path offers minimal aerodynamic resistance. By providing a highly efficient exhaust route, the internal fan operates without artificial strain, preserving the mechanical integrity of the air conditioning unit. 📐 Test Template & Calibration Protocol: Uncheck the “uniform scale” before scaling anyting in the slicer. Profile Test Template: It is heavily recommended to print the test template first to execute a test fit and verify clearance for the unit's moving mechanical louvers (flaps). X/Y Axis Tuning: If the standard profile interferes with AC operation or fitment, uncheck the “uniform scale” and change scaling on the X and Y axes of the template until optimal clearance is achieved. Record the final scaling percentages and apply them to the primary deflector and bracket models before the final print.

Just upload, tweak, and generate. Shape options - Square, Circle, Hexagon Map features - Terrain, Buildings, Roads, Water Bodies, Trail (from GPX) Separated objects - Map features are separate objects inside the 3MF file, so objects can be printed separately. description: Hold a medically accurate piece of human anatomy right in your hands! (Read the last sentence for a curiosity question!) 🩻 Overview 🩻 This advanced 3D model is a highly detailed representation of the human shoulder (glenohumeral) joint, developed through a hybrid medical and digital workflow. The skeletal framework was extracted directly from real CT scans to ensure an anatomically correct bone morphology. The surrounding soft tissues were subsequently hand-modeled in Blender, carefully crafted based on anatomical studies and medical literature. To ensure the best possible 3D printing experience and educational clarity, this model focuses on the primary structures. Some minor or overlapping anatomical elements were intentionally omitted, providing a clean, understandable, and highly printable display piece without overwhelming the slicer or the viewer. 🦴 Included Anatomical Structures The model highlights the key bony landmarks and major soft tissues crucial for understanding shoulder biomechanics: Skeletal Framework (CT Extracted): Scapula (Shoulder Blade), Clavicle (Collarbone), and Humerus (Upper arm bone), featuring accurate articular surfaces and bone topography. 💪 Muscular System (Blender Modeled): Key musculature, including major components of the rotator cuff and biceps, which are essential for shoulder stability and movement. 🔗 Ligaments & Connective Tissue (Blender Modeled): Essential stabilizing ligaments and capsular elements highlighting the articulation points. 🎯 Intended Use Education & Study: A brilliant hands-on visual aid for medical students, anatomy classes, and healthcare professionals. Clinical Communication: Perfect for physical therapists and orthopedic specialists to easily explain shoulder mechanics, impingements, or rotator cuff injuries to their patients. Advanced 3D Printing Showcase: A fantastic display piece that highlights the precision of your printer on complex organic shapes. 💡 Print Settings & Recommendations Material: This model has been fully designed and optimized for standard PLA . No flexible or exotic filaments are required. Versatile Print Profiles: To make this model accessible to everyone, I will be uploading dedicated print profiles for both AMS and non-AMS setups . The multicolor profile is organized to maximize visual contrast and educational value. Based on the provided images, the recommended color mapping is: Bone White: Skeletal structures (Scapula, Clavicle, Humerus) and tendons. Red: Musculature (Rotator cuff and supporting muscles). Blue: Ligaments, and capsular structures. Different colors are presented in the non-AMS setup for printing reasons. SIMPLY INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE NO-AMS PROFILE ⚠️ Disclaimer: This model is intended strictly for educational, illustrative, and hobbyist purposes. It is not a clinical tool and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. For the most interested ones, a bit of anatomy! 🤓🫀🔬 The shoulder, or shoulder girdle, is a complex system designed to give the upper limb a very wide range of motion, with bones, muscles, tendons, and ligaments working together. In my model, the labeled parts show both the supporting framework and the soft tissues that stabilize movement. Bones 🦴 The scapula is a flat triangular bone at the back of the thorax, and it provides attachment for many shoulder muscles. The humerus is the upper arm bone, and its rounded head articulates with the scapula to form the glenohumeral joint, which is the main shoulder joint. The clavicle acts like a strut between the sternum and the scapula, helping keep the shoulder positioned away from the chest wall so the arm can move freely. Soft tissues 💪 The rotator cuff is made of four muscles and their tendons, and its main job is to keep the head of the humerus centered while the arm moves and rotates. The tendons connect muscle to bone, and the long head of the biceps tendon also contributes to shoulder stability as it passes near the joint. The ligaments connect bone to bone and reinforce the joint capsule, helping prevent excessive movement and instability. The subacromial bursa is a small fluid-filled sac that reduces friction between the acromion and the rotator cuff tendons during arm elevation. description: A fully 3D-printable Push-to-Open mechanism with 4 tactile click stages and a completely new rotating locking wheel concept. Snap-fit assembly No supports required No additional hardware No tools required 4 parts 1 printing plate Approx. 3 hours print time Approx. 110 g filament Tested with PLA, standard print settings and the printer X1E and X1C I designed a completely new Push-to-Open (Push-to-Lock / Push-Push) mechanism. This model is intended as a functional demonstration of the working principle and can be assembled quickly using snap-fit connections. I plan to use this Push-to-Open principle in future projects. Unlike other 3D-printed Push-to-Open mechanisms, this new concept is based on a wheel with movable print-in-place contact pins. To make the mechanism easier to understand, I added viewing windows to the model so every movement step can be observed clearly. The mechanism creates 4 distinct click sounds that provide both tactile and audible feedback during every cycle🔔: The first click indicates that the button can be released The second click confirms that the mechanism is locked Pressing again creates the third click, indicating that the button can be released. The fourth click confirms that the mechanism is open and the cycle can start again Additionally, the spring elements inside the mechanism are not permanently loaded in the locked or unlocked position, which increases durability (This does not apply to the spring that retracts the sliding latch). The locking wheel rotates 90° during each open-close cycle. Suitable Applications This functional model is suitable for: Educational and demonstration purposes Mechanical concept studies DIY projects Prototype development for Push-to-Open systems Just to have fun with the mechanism 😉 I believe this mechanism has potential for many different applications and further development. For example: Different spring forces for opening and closing could be implemented Different actions could be triggered after each 90° rotation The mechanism could be activated from all four sides I am open to application ideas, improvement suggestions, and remixes.👐 Print Settings and Material The mechanism can be printed without any special print settings. I tested the mechanism using PLA for all parts. Other materials may require adjustments and were not tested. In my tests, the spring elements of the locking wheel were stiffer when printed in standard PLA, which made the click sounds more noticeable. PLA Tough+ for the locking wheel was more flexible and allowed the mechanism to run slightly smoother, but the click sounds were less pronounced. Assembly The functional model consists of four parts: Housing ① Base plate ② Locking wheel ③ Spring-loaded sliding latch ④ Do not heavily load the spring elements immediately after printing. Allow the parts to cool down completely first. Check if the spring elements inside the locking wheel can move freely. Sometimes a small amount of plastic may fuse inside the gap during printing. This can usually be separated easily. Press each pin toward the center as shown in the image. 2. Insert the spring-loaded sliding latch into the housing as shown in the image. Make sure the guide rails are aligned correctly. 3. Place the locking wheel into the housing. The locking wheel must sit flush inside the housing as shown in the image. 4. Slightly press down the spring-loaded sliding latch at the push point while inserting the base plate from the top until the snap-fits lock into place. 5. Finished!🥳 Do not store the spring of the sliding latch in a permanently preloaded position, as this may reduce the spring force over time. From my experience, the mechanism runs smoother after several cycles. It is important that the locking wheel can rotate freely. Too much friction may cause the mechanism to malfunction. This was a problem in my first prototypes, but the newer versions worked reliably. If you experience any issues, feel free to leave feedback.🤔 Detailed Function Description (Now things start getting a bit more technical😉) I marked the most important elements with colors: The housing contains: First locking position (pink) Second locking position (purple) The locking wheel contains: First contact pin (red) Second contact pin (yellow) These pins can move toward the center and spring back afterward. The locking wheel also contains: Spring-loaded locking sliders (blue) Rotation stops (green) The following section explains the closing and opening sequence of the mechanism. The circled numbers correspond to the images shown below. Closing Process During closing, the spring-loaded sliding latch is inserted from the top by hand and presses against the first contact pin, causing the locking wheel to rotate clockwise ①. At the same time, the second contact pin is pushed toward the center by the side wall of the sliding latch and becomes preloaded, creating enough space for the sliding latch to move to the end position②. As soon as the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the first locking position ③. This prevents the locking wheel from rotating backward. The spring-loaded sliding latch can now move backward slightly using the spring force (spring not shown). Due to the previous rotation of the locking wheel, the return path of the sliding latch is blocked by the rotation stop ④. Because of this, the sliding latch can only move back to the rotation stop position and the mechanism is now locked ⑤. In this position, the preloaded second contact pin can move back into the matching recess of the sliding latch ⑥. Once this happens, the Push-to-Open mechanism can be opened again. Opening Process Opening is performed by pressing the sliding latch a second time by hand. The sliding latch pushes the second contact pin downward until the end stop is reached ⑦. The required travel distance is only 5 mm. During this movement, the first contact pin is preloaded against the side wall of the sliding latch ⑧. When the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the second locking position to again prevent the locking wheel from rotating backward ⑨. The sliding latch can now be fully pulled out of the mechanism by the spring force (spring not shown) ⑩. Since the first contact pin is no longer pressed against the side wall of the sliding latch, it can spring back into its original position ⑪. The system is now back in its starting position and the cycle can begin again. Thanks for checking out the project! 😁

description: The project This life-size 3D model is a realistic human hand skeleton. It was created starting from a real CT scan to keep the true shape of the bones. After cleaning up the scan, custom joints were added directly into the design. The result is a highly accurate model that prints in one single piece and moves just like a real hand. ⚙️ Print-in-Place Kinematics & Anatomy Unlike standard static models or complex multi-part assemblies, this hand is designed to be printed as a single, continuous piece: Zero Assembly Required: The complex mechanical joints are built directly into the geometry. Once the print is finished, the fingers and thumb are immediately ready to flex, extend, and move. Bio-realistic Movement: The internal joint constraints were specifically calibrated to respect the natural limits and range of motion found in a real human hand. Medical-Grade Accuracy: Features true-to-life representations of the carpal bones, metacarpals, and phalanges, preserving the organic textures and shapes of the original scan. 🎓 Perfect For: Clinical & Academic Study: A fantastic, hands-on visual aid for medical students, physical therapists, and anatomy teachers. Biomechanical Demonstration: Easily explains how the skeletal framework behaves during grasping, finger articulation, and thumb opposition. 3D Printing Showcase: An incredibly impressive project to demonstrate your printer's dimensional accuracy, bridging capabilities, and print-in-place tolerances. Artistic Reference: A great physical tool for artists and animators studying lifelike hand poses. 💡 Print Guidelines Format: 100% Print-in-Place. Material: Optimized for standard PLA. Rigid materials work perfectly to demonstrate the skeletal kinematics—no TPU or flexible filament is needed. Scale: Pre-scaled to match the proportions of an average adult human hand (1:1 scale). description: Modular Articulated DNA Educational Model Let your students build, connect, and explore the DNA with this colourful modular model designed for hands-on learning. Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases, while the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone. This model is great for classrooms, STEM projects, biology demonstrations, or anyone who wants a fun physical way to understand nucleotide pairing and DNA structure. I also plan on extending this model with a couple of more pieces for better demonstration of topics like Transcription and Translation . Feel free to leave a like and follow if you'd like to stay updated. Parts You can print as many of the individual parts as you like and connect them with each other! Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases and the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone: Cytosine Guanine Adenine Thymine Uracil Assembly & Colouring The backbone pieces can be clicked together with a little bit of force. It is recommended to use 5x2 (dxh) magnets for both the backbone pieces and nucleotides, to better hold them in place. Place the magnets into the slot (make sure you have them oriented all in the same way!) and use a paper clip, a scredriver, or something similar to push the magnet all the way into the slot. You can also remove the magnets if needed using a paper clip from the other side. Feel free to adjust the colouring of the pieces to your needs. My file uses the colours according to the Wikipedia nucleic acid image: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid#/media/File:Difference_DNA_RNA-EN.svg Versions There are two Versions of nucleotides: Standard Set (recommended!) nucleotides have no chamfer/fillet on the connection pin. This makes them harder to separate from their counterparts, but results in a more stable double strand. Rounded Nucleotide Set contains nucleotide pieces with a rounded down connection pin. This makes them easier to separate, e.g. when demonstrating something, but obviously also reduces the stability of the entire double strand in terms of base pairs disconnecting when you move the double strand around. If you have any suggestions, feel free to let me know!

My Educational Mechanical Examples Series This model is one of my educational mechanical mechanism examples on 80mm x 80mm base plates. You can find all models of the series in this collection => [Mechanical Mechanism Examples] The present model This is an educational model of a Hart's A-frame, which is one of the exact straight-line linkages. Brief Description The approximate straight-line mechanisms introduced so far — Watt's linkage, the Chebyshev linkage, and the Grasshopper linkage — are all based on four-bar linkages. The coupler point need not lie at a joint between two links; it may sit at the midpoint of a link or on its extension. Even so, these simple linkages confine the coupler point to a path that is only approximately straight — and they do so without any linear guide or prismatic pair. A four-bar linkage, however, cannot trace an exactly straight line. Hart's A-frame achieves exact straight-line motion by raising the number of links to six. Five of them move; the sixth is the base plate itself, which serves as the hidden ground link. Laid out as the capital letter A, each slanted side is built from a long link and a short link half its length, joined end to end, and the two short links meet at the apex. The lower end of each long link is pinned to the base plate, and these two fixed pivots are spaced apart by twice the length of the crossbar. The crossbar — the horizontal stroke of the A — joins the two long links at the points that divide them in a 3:1 ratio, with the longer portion toward the fixed pivot. Only these two lower pivots are anchored; every other joint is free to move. Under this arrangement the apex of the A, which is the coupler point, is constrained to travel along a perfectly straight line: the vertical line engraved on the base plate, which is the perpendicular bisector of the two fixed pivots. Move the coupler point by hand and you can feel it being held to this line. As you play with the model, though, you will find that this is not the only path open to the coupler point: the motion branches at the midpoint between the two pivots. There, the coupler point can leave the straight line for a second, skewed path that traces a distorted triangle, also engraved on the plate. Pushing on the coupler point alone will not carry it past the corners of that triangle; there you must also control how the links fold in order to pass through. To keep the motion well-behaved, confine the coupler point to either the upper or the lower half of the straight line, or guide it through the midpoint so that it does not slip onto the other branch. Reference https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hart%27s_inversors Related Models Case This model is compatible with the case included in my first set . Printing Use the models named ???-printable.stl for printing . The models named ???-assembled.stl are provided just to show how they should be assembled. Use well-dried PETG to have better dimensional accuracy. Use 0.1 mm or 0.08 mm layer height to have smoother surfaces. Use slow printing speed for overhangs. Select “Random” seam position to have smoother rotation. Randomly distributed seam should be easily worn out after some wearing.Printing Sanding and Filing Note that, in this model, the rotation of the bases for bearings is intentionally made not too smooth. Sometimes, the gears suffer from the stringing effect and/or elephant foot effect, resulting in a too tight fit to the shafts (they are designed with a 0.15 mm radial clearance). If you see rough surface on the shafts due to stringing, sand off the roughness with a small piece of sand paper. If you feel the gears do not rotate smoothly due to an elephant effect, widen the hole slightly by using a thin round bar file. Without those issues, the parts should rotate very smoothly with minimal friction. Assembly Secure the links onto the shafts with the retaining rings. Find them in this collection: https://makerworld.com/collections/15048577-my-educational-mechanism-models Happy printing! This 3D printable SEL tool gives children a simple finger tracing path to support calm breathing, focus, and emotional regulation.
