description: 🍄 Violet Fungus Necrohulk Miniature – Colossal Fungal Undead Brute This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The creature has a huge, broad humanoid body with an extremely muscular and heavy silhouette, but almost none of its original anatomy remains untouched. Its entire form has been transformed into dense layers of purple fungal flesh, fibrous growths, swollen nodules, mushrooms, and hanging tendrils . The torso is massive and barrel-chested. Across the chest, thick rib-like ridges of fungal tissue form a distorted organic structure, creating the impression of an exposed rib cage that has been rebuilt from fungus rather than bone. The abdomen is covered in layered folds, knotted growths, and clusters of swollen pustule-like nodules. The head is largely consumed by the fungal colony. Instead of a clearly recognizable humanoid face, the upper body transitions into a distorted mass of violet fungal tissue beneath several broad mushroom caps. Small recessed facial features are barely visible among the growths, making the creature appear more like a walking fungal organism than a living humanoid. Several large overlapping mushroom caps grow from the shoulders, upper back, and neck. Their broad, irregular forms create a distinctive fungal canopy around the upper body. The undersides show deep radial gills, while the upper surfaces are rough and covered with smaller nodules and wart-like growths. One arm is raised high in an aggressive striking pose. The forearm and hand have become an enormous malformed fungal club, swollen with thick organic tissue and covered in clusters of nodules. Long root-like tendrils hang from the underside of the arm. The opposite arm hangs lower and reaches forward. It remains vaguely humanoid but is heavily mutated, ending in long, twisted fungal fingers and dangling tendrils. Thick nodules and irregular growths cover the shoulder, forearm, and hand. The legs are massive and powerful, supporting the creature in a wide, stable stance. Their surfaces are covered with fibrous fungal textures and swollen organic growths. Around the knees, thighs, and lower legs, the original anatomy gradually disappears beneath the spreading colony. At the feet, thick root-like fungal tendrils and mycelial strands grow directly into the terrain, physically connecting the creature to the base. Additional hanging tendrils emerge from the abdomen, arms, and lower torso, but remain thick and structurally suitable for a printable miniature. The entire creature is dominated by deep violet, purple, magenta, and dark fungal tones , with lighter highlights emphasizing the ridges, nodules, gills, and fibrous textures. For close encounters and clearing obstacles, the front fascia is dominated by a heavy, bolted-on dozer blade. All standard glass is replaced with rugged wire-mesh guards, offering limited visibility but excellent protection against rocks and improvised projectiles. The Scourge is more than just a vehicle; it's a mobile fortress and a statement of dominance in the endless fight for survival. description: Ghoul Lacedon Miniature – Drowned Hunter of the Deep This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Ghoul Lacedon is presented as an aquatic undead predator shaped by long exposure to black water, flooded crypts, and lightless coastal depths. It retains the ravenous anatomy of a Ghoul, but its body has become broader, heavier, and more adapted for movement beneath the surface. Webbed claws, fin-like growths, water-swollen flesh, and a low amphibious stance immediately distinguish it from the land-dwelling Ghoul while preserving the same corpse-born hunger. The creature has a powerful, hunched humanoid frame with broad shoulders, a thick upper back, and long arms that nearly reach the ground. Its torso is gaunt around the ribs and abdomen, but the shoulders, forearms, thighs, and calves remain dense with unnatural muscle. This contrast creates the impression of a drowned corpse that has become a specialised underwater hunter rather than a weakened cadaver. The spine curves sharply forward, lowering the head between the shoulders and giving the miniature a compact, predatory silhouette. Its head is large, bald, and distinctly aquatic. A broad mouth opens into a savage snarl, exposing irregular needle-like teeth and prominent fangs suited to tearing flesh. The jaw is heavy and slightly extended, while the lips are peeled back around the teeth. Deep-set eyes sit beneath a pronounced brow, giving the creature a hostile, animalistic expression. The nose is flattened and partially decayed, with wide openings that suggest an amphibious or drowned physiology. The cheeks and neck are deeply ridged, and the sides of the head may feature short fin-like membranes or hardened gill structures. A series of thick, jagged fins runs from the back of the skull along the neck and upper spine. Additional fin ridges appear on the forearms and calves, giving the creature a strong aquatic identity without resembling a fish-person or sea demon. These structures are broad, layered, and firmly connected to the limbs, avoiding thin translucent membranes or fragile spikes. Smaller ridges may continue along the elbows and shoulders, reinforcing the flowing direction of the body. The Ghoul Lacedon is posed in a wide, low crouch as though it has just dragged itself from the water. One foot is planted on a raised section of rock near the front of the base, while the other braces farther behind. Both feet are large and fully webbed, with thick clawed toes gripping the terrain. The torso leans forward, and both arms are extended to either side in an aggressive balancing posture. One claw reaches toward its prey, while the opposite hand is drawn slightly back, ready to strike. The hands are oversized and amphibious, with webbing between the fingers and long hooked claws. The fingers remain thick and partially grouped to ensure dependable printing. The webbed membranes are sculpted as solid, shallow connections rather than delicate sheets. Similar webbing stretches between the toes, giving the feet a broad footprint and increasing the model’s physical contact with the base. Its corpse-like skin has a slick, waterlogged texture. Deep folds gather around the neck, joints, and abdomen, while cracks and tears expose darker tissue beneath. Barnacle-like growths, scarred patches, and hardened nodules may appear across the shoulders and limbs, but these should be large and simplified enough to remain readable after printing. Ragged remains of cloth hang around the waist, soaked against the hips and thighs. The garment consists of broad connected panels with torn edges, avoiding long unsupported strips. The ideal palette combines dark teal, drowned blue-grey, cold green, and desaturated turquoise. The belly, face, palms, and inner limbs may be lighter and more corpse-pale, while the back and fin ridges can be darker. Purple, black-red, and brown shading around wounds and joints enhances the drowned appearance. Teeth and claws provide strong contrast in stained ivory or yellowed bone. The round tabletop base represents a flooded ruin or rocky shoreline. Uneven stone, shallow sculpted water, broken masonry, shells, and a few low aquatic plants surround the creature’s feet. The water remains a textured part of the base rather than a transparent effect, with ripples sculpted directly around the planted limbs. All environmental elements remain low, solid, and physically connected. Born beneath black water. Hunger that never drowned. The deep sends it ashore. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Ghoul Lacedon design based on the Monster Manual 2024 creature. Clearly differentiated from a standard Ghoul through aquatic anatomy and terrain. Broad, hunched silhouette with long arms and powerful swimming limbs. Large predatory head with recessed eyes, flattened nose, and fang-filled jaws. Thick fin-like ridges along the head, neck, spine, forearms, and calves. Webbed hands and feet with durable, integrated membranes. Oversized hooked claws suitable for both climbing and underwater hunting. Low amphibious crouch suggesting emergence from deep water. Both feet firmly planted with broad contact across the round base. Water-swollen corpse skin with scars, folds, wounds, and hardened growths. Ragged soaked garments securely connected to the hips and legs. Strong asymmetrical action pose with both arms spread for balance and attack. Thickened fingers, fins, claws, and joints for reliable miniature printing. Flooded ruin base with stone, ripples, shells, and compact aquatic details. No floating water, bubbles, spray, magical effects, smoke, or unsupported scenery. Designed for high-detail resin printing and achievable on finely tuned FDM printers. Excellent for underwater encounters, flooded crypts, coastal ruins, and undead groups. 🎨 Great for Painting Begin with a dark blue-grey, desaturated teal, or drowned green basecoat. Apply a deep navy, purple-black, or green-brown wash into the recesses around the ribs, joints, face, fins, and skin folds. Rebuild the raised areas with lighter turquoise-grey, pale green, or cold corpse-flesh tones. Use lighter, more desaturated colors across the chest, face, palms, and inner limbs to create a waterlogged appearance. Glaze the shoulders, elbows, knees, and wounds with muted purple, bruised blue, and blackened red. The fin ridges can be painted in darker teal or blue-black, followed by pale edge highlights to define their shape. Paint the mouth interior in dark burgundy or purple-red, with the teeth progressing from dirty beige to aged ivory. The claws can be finished in yellowed bone, dark horn, or pale grey. A small amount of gloss varnish on the skin, mouth, and webbing can create a convincing wet finish. The ragged garment works well in faded brown, black-green, or washed-out maroon. Paint the base in cold stone greys and muted coastal browns. Sculpted water can be layered with dark teal, medium blue-green, and pale blue-grey highlights along the ripples, followed by gloss varnish. Shells and stones offer small accents in beige, off-white, and muted orange-brown. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

description: Ghast Gravecaller Miniature – Herald of the Restless Dead This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts . The Ghast Gravecaller is depicted as a more cunning and ritualistic form of undead predator: a corpse-born summoner that does not merely hunt among the graves, but commands the darkness beneath them. Its silhouette combines the gaunt brutality of a Ghast with the visual authority of a necromantic leader, creating a miniature that is immediately distinct from the common Ghast while remaining clearly part of the same undead lineage. The creature has a tall, lean, and heavily emaciated humanoid body with long arms, powerful thighs, and a broad but hollow chest. Its posture is hunched forward, yet more controlled than the feral crouch of an ordinary Ghast. The Gravecaller stands with its legs spread widely across the base, one foot slightly advanced and the other braced behind, giving it a stable ritual stance. The torso twists subtly toward the outstretched arm, creating a strong diagonal line through the body and making the pose feel active without relying on magical effects. Its head is hairless and corpse-like, with a high, angular skull, pointed ears, deeply sunken eyes, and a mouth stretched open in a guttural command. The jaw is filled with irregular teeth and prominent fangs, while the cheeks are gaunt and drawn tightly against the bone. Several long, string-like tendons or decayed strips of flesh hang from the lower jaw and chin, giving the face a grotesque, ceremonial appearance. These strands should be grouped into thick, connected forms rather than sculpted as individual fragile threads. The left hand grips a tall grave-calling staff planted firmly into the base. The shaft is made from dark, weathered wood or bone-bound timber and is reinforced with wrapped cords, metal bands, and crude ritual bindings. At the top sits a large skull framed by smaller bones and curved supports, creating a dramatic focal point. Every decorative element is physically attached to the staff structure, and the lower end connects directly to the ground for added stability. The staff should appear ancient and macabre, but not overly delicate or overloaded with tiny ornaments. The opposite arm reaches forward with the palm open and the fingers curled, as if the Gravecaller is directing nearby undead toward its prey. The hand is oversized and clawed, with long but thickened nails. Its gesture is commanding rather than mindless, separating this creature from the more animalistic Ghast. The arm remains slightly bent at the elbow to reduce overhang and improve printing strength. The Gravecaller wears a collection of decayed ritual garments and scavenged grave ornaments. A torn mantle hangs from one shoulder and falls behind the upper arm in broad, connected folds. Around the waist is a heavy belt decorated with a central skull, bone plates, and several large talismans. Ragged cloth panels descend between and beside the legs, forming a dark ceremonial skirt. The fabric is heavily damaged, with irregular pointed edges, but all hanging pieces connect to one another or to the legs to avoid unsupported sections. Its exposed skin is stretched tightly over the ribs, shoulders, arms, and legs. Scars, open wounds, hardened growths, and areas of rough necrotic tissue cover the body. The chest remains visibly hollow and starved, while the thighs and shoulders retain enough muscle to suggest the unnatural strength of a Ghast. The fingers and toes end in hooked claws, and both feet are planted securely against the base. The color palette is dominated by desaturated green-grey, pale corpse flesh, and bruised blue. Dark purple and blackened red can be used around wounds, eyes, and the mouth. The garments suit faded violet, charcoal, dirty burgundy, or mouldy black, while the bone ornaments provide pale focal points. The staff works well in dark brown wood, aged ivory, tarnished bronze, and old blood tones. The round tabletop base represents a desecrated burial site. Several skulls, large bone fragments, cracked earth, and grave debris are embedded around the creature’s feet. The staff is planted among these remains, visually connecting the Gravecaller to the dead it commands. The terrain stays low and compact, ensuring that the model’s silhouette remains clear and that no scenery becomes fragile or distracting. A voice beneath the soil. A command the dead obey. The grave answers back. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Ghast Gravecaller design based on the Monster Manual 2024 creature. Clearly differentiated from the standard Ghast through ritual gear and commanding posture. Tall, gaunt undead anatomy with long limbs and visible ribs. Wide, stable stance suited to a necromantic battlefield leader. Grotesque head with pointed ears, sunken eyes, fangs, and hanging jaw tendons. Large grave-calling staff planted directly into the base. Staff topped with an integrated skull and securely attached bone decorations. One clawed hand extended in a commanding summoner-like gesture. Heavy ritual belt with skull ornamentation and large bone talismans. Torn shoulder mantle and layered ceremonial cloth panels. All fabric sections attached to the body or neighbouring garments for print safety. Thickened claws, tendons, staff details, and bone elements for dependable printing. Both feet firmly connected to the round base. Desecrated graveyard terrain with skulls, bones, and cracked earth. No floating spirits, magical energy, smoke, aura effects, or separate components. description: About Models: These models are designed to represent real animals as naturally as possible, with focus on accurate size, shapes, proportions, colors, fine details, and natural movement or pose. Some models include articulated, hinge, or flexi parts for motion and flexibility, while others are non-articulated and focus on realistic appearance. Some parts, such as legs, can be carefully adjusted with gentle heat for a more natural pose, but too much heat can damage or deform the model. Print: All settings are pre-configured and optimized for a balance between detail, print time, strength, functionality, and easy support removal. I recommend printing the models at their original scale. Scaling down may cause issues such as fused moving parts, small hinges not working correctly, or fine details not printing properly. Difficulty Guide: The difficulty icon is a general overall guide and may vary depending on your printer, filament, slicer settings, calibration, and experience. It mainly reflects print complexity, filament changes, possible waste, fine details, support use, and support removal. Multicolor prints may create more waste on single-nozzle AMS or AMS Lite systems, such as A1 with AMS Lite, compared to dual-nozzle or lower-waste systems like X2D or H2C. Level 3 / Supports: For higher difficulty models, especially Level 3, I recommend using Support Material for PLA. It can make support removal much easier, cleaner, and safer for delicate parts. This is especially helpful when the model has many supports, thin details, legs, antennas, or other fragile areas. Note / Handling: Some models may have very small hinge parts or delicate thin areas, such as legs, antennas, tails, or other small details. On some models, these parts may disconnect or break more easily if handled roughly. Please handle the models with care. They are not intended for aggressive play, but rather as educational models, display pieces, or gentle collectible toys. Durability may vary from model to model. Some models are stronger and may be suitable for careful play, while others are more delicate and better suited for display on a shelf. Articulated / Hinge Versions: For models with moving parts, hinges, or flexi sections, please open the included 3MF file, ideally in Bambu Studio. Exporting to another slicer may cause hinge problems. My hinges are created and tested by me, usually designed to print without supports, and are added this way so they can be moved, adjusted, customized, or removed when scaling the model down. STL / 3MF Note: STL files are usually provided without moving parts. The prepared articulated or hinge version is inside the 3MF file. This helps avoid problems with small scaled-down models, where moving parts, gaps, or hinges may fuse or fail. If needed, you can remove the hinges and print the model as a solid version. description: Glabrezu Miniature – Four-Armed Tempter of the Abyss This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Glabrezu is presented as a towering four-armed demon whose immense physical power is matched by a cruel and manipulative intelligence. Its design combines a broad bestial torso, massive crushing pincers, smaller clawed arms, a snarling canine-like head, and a heavy predatory stance. The result is a distinctive Large creature that feels dangerous from every angle while remaining practical for 3D generation and reliable miniature printing. The Glabrezu has a huge, top-heavy body with a deep chest, thick abdomen, and powerful hunched shoulders. Its upper silhouette is dominated by two enormous pincer arms that rise from the sides of the torso. These limbs are much larger than the lower pair and resemble the crushing claws of a monstrous crab. Each arm is heavily muscled and plated with rough chitinous growths, ending in a broad pincer made from two thick opposing blades. The claws should look capable of crushing armour and bone, but they must remain robust rather than needle-sharp. Their outer edges are slightly jagged, with broad hooked tips and thick hinge structures. Beneath the pincer arms is a second pair of smaller humanoid arms. These limbs are leaner but still powerfully muscled, ending in long hands with hooked black claws. One lower hand reaches forward in a grasping gesture, while the other is held closer to the torso as though preparing to seize, strike, or bargain. The asymmetry gives the model a more natural and threatening composition. The fingers remain thick and partially grouped, avoiding fragile separation. Its head has a brutal, canine quality with a long muzzle, heavy brow, pointed ears, and a wide mouth filled with irregular teeth. The lips are pulled back into an intelligent, predatory snarl. A pair of thick, backward-curving horns rises from the skull, framing the head without extending into overly thin points. Smaller horn ridges and bony plates may continue along the cheekbones, neck, and upper spine. The recessed eyes should appear calculating rather than mindless, reinforcing the Glabrezu’s role as a manipulator as well as a destroyer. The creature’s lower body is supported by two massive digitigrade legs. The thighs are extremely muscular, narrowing at the backward-bent joints before widening again into heavy lower legs. Each foot ends in broad, clawed toes that spread firmly across the base. Both feet should make full contact with the terrain, giving the miniature a stable, grounded stance. The pose is wide and slightly crouched, with the torso leaning forward and the pincer arms raised on either side. This creates a powerful triangular silhouette and suggests that the demon is closing in around its prey. A long tail extends from the lower back and curves behind one leg before resting against the base. It is thick at the root and tapers gradually, with a ridged or spined upper surface. The tail remains connected to the ground or rear leg along part of its length, providing structural support and avoiding a vulnerable unsupported extension. The Glabrezu’s surface is a mixture of coarse skin, dense musculature, and natural armour. The chest, abdomen, thighs, and lower arms are covered in leathery hide stretched over heavy muscles. The shoulders, forearms, back, and pincer limbs feature thicker chitinous plates, rough ridges, and broad spines. These transitions should remain visually clear, allowing painters to distinguish skin from hardened carapace. Scars, shallow cracks, and old wounds can be added across the torso, but the model should avoid excessive micro-texture. The creature wears no armour or clothing. Its natural hide and immense body are its protection. A few heavy rings, broad metal bands, or broken chains may be integrated around one wrist or ankle to suggest past summoning or imprisonment, but these details must remain securely attached and secondary to the anatomy. A strong palette combines deep crimson, dark maroon, black-red, and bruised purple. The pincer arms and armoured plates can be darker than the softer flesh, using near-black burgundy or brown-red. The chest and abdomen may shift toward warmer red, while the muzzle, hands, and lower legs receive subtle purple or grey shading. Horns, teeth, and claws provide contrast in dark bone, black horn, or stained ivory. The round tabletop base represents a scorched abyssal battlefield or shattered summoning chamber. Cracked stone, broken masonry, embedded chain links, and low jagged rocks surround the creature’s feet. The tail and both legs connect firmly to this terrain. The scenery remains low and compact, ensuring that the Glabrezu’s four arms and towering silhouette remain the primary focus. Four arms. One cruel mind. Promises forged in ruin. Every bargain ends in blood. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Glabrezu design based on the Monster Manual 2024 creature. Massive four-armed demon with an unmistakable broad silhouette. Two enormous upper pincer arms with thick, durable crushing claws. Two smaller lower arms ending in hooked humanoid claws. Canine-like demonic head with long muzzle, pointed ears, and intelligent expression. Thick backward-curving horns integrated securely into the skull. Huge chest, powerful shoulders, and heavily muscled abdomen. Digitigrade legs with broad clawed feet firmly planted on the base. Long tapering tail supported against the base or rear leg. Clear contrast between leathery flesh and hardened chitinous armour. Broad ridges and spines designed to remain durable during printing. Strong forward-leaning combat stance with raised pincer arms. No weapons, floating magic, smoke, aura effects, or detached accessories. Optional broken chains or metal bands integrated directly into the body and terrain. Thickened fingers, claws, horns, joints, and tail for dependable printing. Compact abyssal ruin base with cracked stone and embedded debris. Designed for high-detail resin printing and carefully calibrated FDM printers. Excellent as a major demon encounter, summoning centerpiece, or abyssal commander. 🎨 Great for Painting Begin with a dark crimson, maroon, or black-red basecoat. Apply a deep purple, brown-black, or dark burgundy wash into the recesses around the muscles, joints, facial features, and armour plates. Rebuild the raised flesh with warmer reds, muted scarlet, or desaturated crimson, concentrating highlights across the chest, shoulders, thighs, muzzle, and knuckles. Paint the pincer arms and hardened carapace in darker shades such as black-burgundy, deep brown-red, or near-black purple. Use brighter red-brown or muted orange edge highlights along the ridges, hinges, and claw edges. A restrained satin finish can help separate the harder chitin from the more matte leathery skin. The horns and claws work well in black, dark brown, or stained bone. Build the horn tips toward charcoal grey, beige, or aged ivory depending on the desired contrast. Paint the mouth interior in deep purple-red, with teeth in dirty beige and pale bone. Small gloss accents inside the mouth and around the eyes can create a wet, predatory appearance. Broken chains or metal bands can be painted in blackened iron, tarnished bronze, or rusted steel. Finish the base with dark grey stone, scorched brown earth, and dusty ash highlights. Orange-brown rust, old blood stains, and subtle red glazing in the deepest cracks can reinforce the abyssal atmosphere without requiring sculpted fire or magical effects. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Large Recommended Base: 50 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

Customize it directly in the MakerWorld / OpenSCAD customizer to fit straps, webbing, cords, paracord, loops or flat mounting tabs — no CAD software required. This model generates a real two-part buckle: male part with flexible snap arms and rigid center guide; female part with side-release windows. Improved snap-fit durability V2 includes several geometry improvements: rounded arm roots to reduce stress concentration; chamfered and rounded entry mouth for smoother insertion; side windows sized so the arms can relax when locked; adjustable latch geometry and arm stiffness. One-parameter fit tuning The most important parameter is clearance. description: Make your own text stamp for clay, soap, leather, play dough, fondant, and normal ink-pad stamping. Up to three lines of custom text, round or rectangular head, emboss or deboss, optional border, and a comfortable twist-lock handle. Prints support-free. Type your text and print a personal stamp. The rigid PETG/PLA version presses crisp, readable impressions into polymer clay, air-dry clay, soap, soft leather, play dough, fondant, and similar soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping, a tested option is to split the stamp face in the slicer and print the actual raised letters/rim in TPU, with the base and handle in PETG, so the letters flex slightly like a softer stamp face. Features: - Up to three lines of text, automatically centered. - Mirrored text by default, so the stamped impression reads correctly. Turn mirroring off to print a readable display plaque instead. - Two impression styles: "raised" presses your text INTO the material (debossed impression), "recessed" leaves your text standing proud (embossed impression). - Round or rectangular head with adjustable size and optional border ring - the border stamps a clean frame around your text. - Adjustable text depth (0.8-3 mm) for shallow or deep impressions. - Comfortable mushroom handle with a bayonet twist-lock: insert into the head back and twist clockwise to a firm stop. The locked handle cannot pull off, even when lifting the stamp out of sticky clay. Print one handle and many heads: name stamps, date stamps, logo text, gift tags. - Tested TPU-face workflow: print the raised letters/rim in TPU and the base + handle in PETG for a softer face that also works better as a normal ink-pad stamp. - Console warning if your text is too wide for the chosen head size. - Both parts print flat with no supports. The model checks your text width against the head size and prints a note in the customizer console if a line will not fit. Note: rigid PLA/PETG stamp faces are best for clay, soap, leather, dough, and other soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping on paper, the tested TPU-face workflow gives a more forgiving contact surface than a hard FDM face. Results still depend on ink pad, paper, layer height, and surface finish, so test first. Custom Fonts: You can use any font MakerWorld has installed , type it into font_name as "Family:style=Style". Examples: Liberation Sans:style=Bold (default) Liberation Serif:style=Bold (bookplate look) Liberation Mono:style=Bold (typewriter) Liberation Sans Narrow:style=Bold (fits longer text) DejaVu Sans:style=Bold DejaVu Serif:style=Bold Stick to Bold styles thin strokes don't stamp well and can be fragile. Customization Notes - line_1 / line_2 / line_3: your text; leave lines empty to use fewer lines. - font_name: keep the default Liberation Sans Bold for reliable width warnings; other bold fonts work, but check the preview. - mirror_text: leave ON for stamping. Turn off only for display plaques. - text_style: "raised" = pressed-in (debossed) impression, "recessed" = raised (embossed) impression. - text_depth: 1.5 mm default; use 2-3 mm for soft doughs, 1-1.5 mm for firm clay and leather. - head_shape / head_diameter / head_width / head_height: face size. Bigger faces fit longer text. - border_enabled / border_width / border_inset: frame ring around the text. - border_depth: rim height, independent of text_depth. Match text_depth for a classic one-level stamp, or make the rim taller than the text so it contains the material and controls impression depth like a cookie-cutter frame - useful for wax-seal-style stamps and uniform clay medallions. - fit_clearance: twist-lock clearance. Increase by 0.05-0.1 if the handle is hard to insert or twist; decrease toward 0.05 for a tighter lock. - part: "all" prints both pieces; "head" alone for extra stamp faces for a handle you already printed; "fit_preview" is preview-only - do not print. description: Windproof Heavy Duty Sand Pegs Stakes with 19mm HEX Designed For Extreme Beach Camping Stop watching your tent fly away in coastal gales. Built out of pure necessity, these heavy-duty screw-in sand pegs were designed to withstand the brutal realities of off-grid wild beach camping. When you are exposed to relentless 70–80 km/h winds , standard tent stakes just won't cut it. These aggressive, deep-threaded spiral anchors bite hard into loose ground to keep your shelter, tarp, or beach umbrella firmly rooted. Smart, Optimized 3D Print Design As a maker and avid camper, I designed these pegs from scratch to solve two major problems: weak ground holding and wasteful printing. The geometry has been carefully tuned for the 3D printing process: Zero Supports: Engineered to print completely support-free, saving post-processing time. Fast & Efficient: Optimized design drastically cuts down on print time and filament waste without sacrificing structural integrity or toughness. 3 Included Models & Sizes To ensure you have the perfect anchor for any beach topography, the package includes 3 distinct variations: 1x Medium Size: Great for compact packing, firmer damp sand, and standard setups. 1x XL Standard: Extended length for deep penetration into shifting, loose sand to provide massive pull resistance. 1x XL Wide-Thread: Features a significantly wider screw thread configuration. This is engineered specifically for extra strength and maximum surface area bite if you are dealing with ultra-fine, super dry, or powdery sand. 1x XXL Ultra Wide-Thread (19mm Hex): A beefed-up, heavy-duty version featuring our widest thread yet and a robust 19mm hex head for maximum torque and strength. (Note: Untested, feedback welcome!) Print Settings & Material Recommendations ⚠️ For Best Results: Print with high infill (minimum 40-50%) and at least 4-5 perimeters/walls to ensure maximum torsional strength when screwing them into the ground. ASA (Highly Recommended): If your stakes are going to sit in the blistering direct sun all day, ASA is the top choice . It offers excellent UV resistance and high thermal stability, ensuring the pegs won't soften, warp, or deform under intense beach heat. PETG (Budget/Alternative Option): PETG works perfectly fine with a simple trick! If you use PETG, dig a hole in the sand until you reach the damp, harder layer, screw the pegs in there, and then bury them back up with sand. As long as they are buried away from direct sunlight, PETG will stay cool enough to maintain its strength and hold your gear secure. Pro-Tip for Maximum Hold in Loose Sand: To get the absolute best anchorage on windy beaches, don't just screw them into the dry, powdery top layer. Dig a small hole until you reach the dense, wet sand underneath. Screw the anchor directly into that wet layer so the wide threads can lock into the compacted sand. If the sand is completely dry or you can't dig deep enough, pour a bottle of sea water over the area after screwing it in to tighten and pack the sand around the threads. Fill the hole back up and stomp it down! Update: New Model Added! (4. description: This one was quite the task! I originally did my clicker bar using these transparent bead storage cases which worked perfectly fine while making the odd one at home but I ran into a bit of an issue when we took it to our events. The first was they were quite small in height meaning I couldn't put a lot of keycaps in them, it also caused overflow into the other containers when people were digging around for the colour they wanted so I had random letters mixed in with each other. 😩 They were also a pain to put out on display because they came with an attached lid so I had to keep them closed after people left or use double the space to keep them open. Not great when you're already busy enough building the actual clickers and limited on table space! That got me motivated to upgrade the display - I looked around for a while but couldn't find anything that really matched what I needed so I set myself to work. The main issues I needed to resolve were: It had to be modular so I can always add extras for new keycaps if needed. Had to be held together somehow during the events so it doesn't get pushed over easily by people but needs to be able to accommodate for different sized bins and layouts due to table restrictions. A slot to show the letters/symbols as people often got lost trying to find letters if keycaps were flipped upside down in the box, worse if letters got mixed around already. Ideally stackable so I can just stack them together after events and pack it away in a box for ease of use. A lid preferably so they don't accidentally fall out or have other small objects fall into them. Features of the storage bins: Fully modular. x1, x4 and x9 bins. Bins are stackable. Please note x9 bin requires 256mm x 256mm build plates but you can print a x4 with x1 and combine to make a x9 for A1 Mini users. Two coupler versions for joining displays. Bins can be attached with the row or the quad coupler. There are both snug and loose fits so print the one best for your printers/filament calibration. Quad couplers are for holding 4 bins together or for joining large 9 bins with 4 bins. The row coupler is if you wanted to build horizontally/vertically only. Display slot version and one without. Slots are slide in and can be removed after event completion by placing it inside the bin with the keycaps for easy storage. Personally I like the slot version but I included one without in case others wanted to use these for other purposes. Stackable. Please note there is a small gap where they are stacked - this finger gap is INTENTIONAL so you can actually separate them easier without them getting stuck. (Mishaps have happened during testing...) Various lid options. x1 lids have handles and coupler holes, x4 lids have coupler holes, x9 lid have no holes. If using the handle versions for x1, please secure handles using GLUE. I could add more variations but I feel like for most people these versions should suffice. For handles I have a short and a taller version as well. There are two sizes to these in case you find them too tight to fit into the hole on the lids. Recommended Print Settings: Layer Height: 0.2mm Nozzle: 0.4mm Wall Generator: Classic Infill: 15-20% Gyroid Supports: Not required Speed: 20-50mm/s for layer 1, then 150-200 for the rest. description: ## Short Description Generate round spacers, rectangular shims, or tall standoffs with custom dimensions, hole sizes, clearances, and copy count. ## Full Description This parametric generator creates simple workshop spacing parts for 3D printers, enclosures, jigs, furniture fixes, craft builds, mounting jobs, and everyday repairs. Choose between a round spacer/washer, a rectangular shim plate, or a taller cylindrical standoff, then set the exact dimensions you need. The default model prints a small support-free batch of round spacers with central clearance holes and no unnecessary side notch. Switch to rectangular shim mode for flat plates with 0-4 mounting holes, or tall standoff mode for longer cylindrical stand-offs. A clearance parameter lets you slightly oversize holes for real-world FDM fit, and the copy count parameter lets you print one part or a small set at once. Optional finishing controls include chamfered spacer edges, engraved or raised top labels, and a countersunk top variant for flush-fit screw applications. This is intended as a practical custom-fit utility print. It is not a certified precision, load-rated, or high-temperature hardware replacement. For functional assemblies, print one test piece first and adjust the clearance for your printer, filament, and screw/bolt size. ## Customization Notes - Use `part_style` to choose `round_spacer` , `rectangular_shim` , or `tall_standoff` . - Use `copy_count` and `copy_gap` to print one part or a small batch. - For round spacers, tune `outer_diameter` , `inner_diameter` , and `spacer_height` . - For tall standoffs, tune `outer_diameter` , `standoff_height` , and `standoff_hole_diameter` . - For rectangular shims, tune `shim_length` , `shim_width` , `shim_thickness` , `hole_count` , `shim_hole_diameter` , and `hole_spacing` . - Use `clearance_extra` to add real-world hole clearance. Start around 0.20 mm for PLA, then test and adjust. - Use `chamfer_enabled` and `chamfer_size` to soften round spacer/standoff edges. - Use `label_enabled` , `label_style` , and `label_text` for engraved or raised top labels such as `M4 5mm` . - Use `countersink_enabled` , `countersink_diameter` , and `countersink_depth` for a countersunk top variant. - `edge_marker_notch` is off by default; enable only if you want a visible orientation/counting notch.

description: 本模型仅供个人下载使用，您不得以任何形式出售此模型的数字及物理打印版本。 项目背景 在过去很长一段时间里，每次准备焊接，我都需要把电烙铁、PCB 夹具、焊锡丝、烟雾净化器等工具一个个搬到桌面。 焊接结束后，又要逐一收回。 随着焊接工作越来越频繁，我发现真正浪费时间的并不是焊接本身，而是 准备焊接和整理桌面 。工具越来越多，桌面越来越拥挤，不仅影响工作效率，也让整个工作环境显得杂乱无序。 另一方面，我一直使用空气净化器作为临时方案处理焊接烟雾。随着焊接时间增加，我希望增加专业的焊烟过滤器，但市面上的产品大多是独立设备，这意味着桌面上又会增加一个新的设备，进一步加剧原本就混乱的焊接环境。 我开始意识到，我真正需要解决的问题，并不是增加一个新的工具，而是 重新组织整个焊接环境。 愿景 于是，我开始构思一个新的概念—— 焊接坞（SolderDock） 。 它不仅仅是一台焊烟过滤器，更应该成为焊接工作中所有常用工具的”停靠点”。 我希望它能够同时承担以下几个角色： 焊烟过滤 常用工具挂载 焊接工具收纳 模块化扩展平台 更重要的是，希望焊接结束后，我只需要移动一个设备，就能快速完成整个焊接环境的收纳，让工作台能够迅速从 焊接模式 切换到 装配、拼接、测量 等其它工作模式。 设计思考 既然希望所有工具最终都能围绕同一个主体展开，那么首先需要确定整个系统的核心。 观察整个焊接环境后，我发现焊烟过滤器本身就是体积最大的设备，也是所有工具中位置最固定的一部分，因此决定以焊烟过滤器作为整个”焊接坞”的核心。 随后，我开始寻找市面上的现成方案。 经过一段时间的调研后，我基本放弃了现有产品，原因主要有三个： 1. 体积与成本 过滤效果较好的产品通常体积较大，价格也相对较高，不适合作为桌面长期使用的中心设备。 2. 滤芯成本与维护 很多产品使用专用滤芯，不仅需要重新验证过滤效果，后期更换时也难以保证长期稳定购买，维护成本较高。 3. 扩展能力不足 市面上的焊烟过滤器几乎都是独立产品，并没有预留安装其它工具的可能，更无法作为整个焊接环境的中心。 因此，我希望最终的方案能够满足几个目标： 使用价格低廉且容易获得的标准滤芯； 成本尽可能低； 能够方便集成其它焊接工具； 保留后续模块化扩展能力。 实现方案 基础选型 整个设计首先从滤芯选型开始。 我希望直接采用已经成熟、供应稳定的标准滤芯，这样不仅能够降低成本，也方便后期长期更换。 最终，我选择了小米车载空气净化器所使用的滤芯。 原因很简单： 市场保有量大； 原厂、副厂滤芯供应充足； 更换成本低； 后续维护几乎没有压力。 确定滤芯之后，我曾考虑直接改造小米车载空气净化器。 不过很快发现两个问题。 第一，原机采用多面进风设计，作为焊烟过滤器时，无法将吸力集中到焊接区域。 第二，原机出风方向与理想结构并不一致，同时也没有预留任何工具挂载空间。 相比继续修改原机，重新设计整个外壳显然更加合理。 随后，我开始研究风扇和驱动方案。 最初计划单独购买离心风扇和驱动板，再重新设计整体结构。 但在比较价格时，我突然意识到： 直接购买二手小米车载空气净化器，反而比单独购买风扇和驱动电路更便宜。 于是最终选择拆解整机，仅保留： 风扇 驱动板 电源系统 除此之外，这块驱动板还带来了意外收获： 它不仅支持三档风速调节，还可以连接米家 App，通过蓝牙查看简单的空气质量信息，为整个产品增加了一些不错的交互体验。 结构设计 确定核心硬件后，整个设计开始围绕”焊接坞”这一理念展开。 优化风道 重新设计外壳，使进风口与出风口保持相对方向，让烟雾能够沿着更合理的路径流动，提高吸烟效率。 精准反向工程 由于原厂风扇安装孔位和接口均为异形结构，为保证装配精度，我通过 3D 扫描获取原始模型，并进行反向工程设计，使电机卡扣准确入位。 模块化扩展 外壳预留了大量标准 M3 安装孔，方便后续增加新的功能模块，也方便用户根据自己的需求进行扩展。 焊锡支架 顶部增加挡风罩，并将标准焊锡丝线轮集成其中，在保证风道效果的同时，也方便焊接过程中直接取锡。 焊锡分装收纳盒 整卷焊锡丝负责储存，分装盒负责使用。 通过可挂载的焊锡分装盒，让焊锡丝在 储存、收纳与焊接 之间自由切换。 PCB 夹具 通过金属万向软管安装 PCB 夹具，使夹具能够直接固定在焊接坞主体上，进一步减少桌面设备数量。 铜丝球清洁挂载 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

Ecco un progetto semplicissimo per rinfrescarvi nelle estati roventi davanti al pc. Un creativo e funzionale modello di Ice Cooler, a praticamente costo zero. L'idea è piuttosto semplice: sfruttare il ghiaccio per rinfrescare l'aria. Mettete una bottiglia di plastica da 500ml nel vostro freezer (attenzione a lasciare la bottiglia piena solo al 75/80% massimo, altrimenti esploderà!) e lasciatela congelare. Inseritela nell'alloggiamento del mio Ice Cooler e avviate la ventola. Entro pochi secondi, aria freschissima uscirà e vi donerà un gradevolissimo refrigerio. E può funzionare per diverse ore prima che il ghiaccio sia completamente sciolto e perda la sua efficacia!!!! Tutto quello di cui avrete bisogno è: - 1 ventola da PC 120x120mm a 12v - Un alloggiamento Batterie da 9v - 4 viti almeno da 50mm Io ho utilizzato questo hardware perchè il più comodo per me: ciò non toglie che potete valutare un'alimentazione da USB, o da PowerBank, con Regolatori di velocità etc etc. Sta solo a voi: il mio modello esige solo una ventola da 120mm; il cavo della ventola fuoriesce dal posteriore del Case e da lì potete fare quello che preferite. Una volta stampato tutto, testate i contatti della ventola unita al pacco della batteria da 9v, in modo da poter verificare la corretta direzione di rotazione della ventola (deve buttare aria FUORI dal Case, non dentro). Sì, la ventola è un 12v e la batteria un 9v, ma funzionerà benissimo, ad una velocità leggermente inferiore. Una volta verificato questo e segnato i corretti fili, inserite il filo della ventola nel buco in alto a sinistra e fatelo uscire dal posteriore, unendolo poi al pacco batteria. Avvitate la ventola nel case e inserite l'alloggiamento della bottiglia nel Case, prestando attenzione che la parte aperta sia in direzione della ventola. Ora, potete inserire la bottiglia ed accendere! Potete anche utilizzare il tappo per contenere al meglio la temperatura della bottiglia, migliorando la resa grazie anche ad un piccolo effetto “Venturi” causato dai piccoli fori in alto da cui viene aspirata l'aria che, scendendo attraverso la spirale, si raffredda più velocemente. Entro pochi secondi, sentirete una magnifica aria fresca uscire dal vostro nuovo Ice Cooler! Non dimenticate, quando cambiate la bottiglia, di verificare se la vaschetta di raccolta dell'acqua causata dalla condensa è da svuotare (alla base del Case dove va in appoggio la bottiglia). 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

I've always had a soft spot for the SKÅDIS pegboard system — cheap, endlessly flexible, and there's an accessory for pretty much everything. But there was one thing I could never find for it: a version of one of my favorite pieces of design history, an iconic modular storage unit from the late 1960s, originally made as a single molded block of compartments and hooks. You can actually buy the original — it's a single molded block holding all the compartments at once — but it's pricey and pretty bulky for what is, at the end of the day, a desk organizer. description: Ultimate Parametric Pipe & Cable Clip Looking for a pipe or cable clip that fits your exact needs? This fully parametric generator lets you customize almost every important dimension, making it easy to create a clip tailored to your application. Create perfectly sized clips for pipes, cables, hoses, conduits, and many other round objects without having to modify the model manually. Simply adjust the parameters and generate the size you need. Whether you're organizing cables, mounting plumbing, or securing larger pipes, this generator gives you complete control over the most important dimensions. Features Fully parametric design Adjustable pipe/cable diameter Adjustable clip width Adjustable arm thickness Adjustable opening angle Adjustable wall distance Adjustable mounting hole diameter Compatible with multiple mounting methods: Countersunk screw (default) Socket head screw Hex nut By default, the model is generated with a countersunk screw recess. If you prefer a socket head screw or a hex nut , simply adjust the corresponding parameters described in the guide below. For rigid pipes, I recommend using a slightly larger opening angle to make installation easier. For cables, you can even print the clip in TPU . Thanks to the flexibility of the material, the cable can be inserted easily while still being held securely in place. Parameter Guide Gap Angle Controls how far the clip arms are opened. Adjust this value to change how tightly the clip wraps around the pipe or cable. Do not exceed 150° , as larger values may cause the model geometry to become invalid. Wall Distance Controls the minimum distance between the wall and the nearest point of the pipe or cable . A minimum value of 10 mm is recommended, but feel free to experiment. Need to move the pipe farther away from the wall? Simply increase this value and use a longer mounting screw. Arm Thickness Controls the thickness of the clip arms. Thicker arms provide greater stiffness and strength. A value between 3–5 mm is recommended for most applications. Larger pipe diameters may benefit from thicker arms. Pipe Diameter Outside diameter of the pipe or cable. Remember to add a small clearance (for example 0.1 mm ) unless you want a tight press fit. Clamp Width Controls the overall width of the clip. Increase this value for larger or heavier pipes and cables if additional strength is required. Hole Diameter of the mounting hole. Remember to add enough clearance so the screw can pass through freely. Head Nut Depth Used when mounting with a socket head screw or a hex nut instead of the default countersunk screw. Measure the height of the screw head or nut, add a small clearance (approximately 0.2 mm ), and enter the result here. Head Size Controls the diameter of the socket head screw recess. The default value is 1 mm , which disables the recess. If you're using a socket head screw, simply measure the screw head diameter, add a small clearance, and enter the result here. When using this parameter, keep Nut Size set to 1 mm. Nut Size Controls the size of the hex nut pocket. Measure the nut across the flats , add approximately 0.2 mm of clearance, and enter the result here. When using this parameter, keep Head Size set to 1 mm. Printing Recommendations Recommended material: PETG TPU is an excellent choice for cable management applications No supports required Print flat on the build plate I designed this generator to eliminate the need for creating a new model every time you need a different pipe or cable diameter. description: Platethora , the open-source, public-domain, quick-release Plate system with a Plethora of applications. Platethora was inspired by systems like Gridfinity, the Honeycomb storage wall, and tripods. I aimed to create a quick-release plate you could use for anything you want, not just cameras. I tried to make the design as simple as possible while using also as little hardware as possible, but an M4x14-16 screw with a nylon nut is still required, although a regular nut with some superglue should also work. The main goal is for people to create their own bases and plates for whatever they need, which is why I shared the editable step files and put the whole project into the public domain, meaning you can do whatever you want with these files. I recommend printing in PETG in the orientation shown above. This isn't supposed to be a replacement for conventional tripods for cameras and such. It's supposed to be an option to be able to use tripods and quick-release plates with things you usually can't use them with. Things like lights and the other examples in the photos. If you have a really nice camera, then I encourage you to buy a nice tripod for it with a proper metal quick-release plate. But if you want something a little more out there, like helping hands that can be switched from being used on a flat surface to being used with a desk clamp, then I would argue my system is the better option. It's a solution for very specific problems, which is exactly what 3D printing is for.

description: A modular filament storage system inspired by one of the best designs on MakerWorld. Before anything else, I want to give full credit to Antiphrasis. Their modular filament rack has deservedly become one of the most popular storage systems on MakerWorld, with thousands of downloads, and it was their design that inspired me to explore a different engineering approach. After using their system myself, I became interested in solving one particular design challenge in a different way. Could I redesign the modular connection system so that each joint only required a single upright while still creating a strong, rigid structure? After building my own interpretation, I contacted Antiphrasis to show them what I'd created and to ask if they were happy for me to publish it on MakerWorld. Thankfully they gave me their blessing, so I'm delighted to be able to share it with the community. 🧵 Why I designed this version The original system is excellent and has proven itself over thousands of prints. Rather than trying to improve every aspect of it, I focused on solving one specific engineering problem: Creating a connection system that locks adjacent modules together while using a single shared upright instead of two. The result is a storage system that is solid and stable while reducing the number of uprights required and maintaining a clean, modular appearance. I genuinely recommend taking a look at Antiphrasis' original design as well, then deciding which approach best suits your needs. 📦 Modular by design Each module baes stores three filament spools. Using two base sections and two uprights creates storage for six rolls, with additional modules simply extending the system. Note: Always orient your bases in the same way The photographs show just a few possible layouts, including my own corner installation storing 36 spools along with additional shelving for boxed filament. 🖨️ Print notes Two print profiles are included: - PLA Basic - PETG No AMS required. Assembly is required. Please refer to the photographs to see how the modules lock together during assembly. Make sure you are consistent with how you orentate the bases. 💡 Future expansion If there's enough interest, I'd love to expand the system with additional modules such as: Storage shelves IKEA SKÅDIS-compatible panels Additional accessories and organisers If there's something you'd like to see, let me know in the comments. 🙏 Credit where it's due This project would never have existed without Antiphrasis' original modular rack system providing the inspiration. description: Fresh3D Detachable Wall-Mounted Storage Containers Overview A modular wall-mounted storage system with individually removable trays for quick, convenient access. Each tray features a smooth pull-out and rotate action, interchangeable labels, and full access when removed. Designed for strength, easy printing, and tool-free assembly, requiring only your preferred wall mounting method. Features Quick, individually removable containers Strong, easy-to-operate wall locking mechanism Smooth pull-out and rotate action for easy access to parts Full tray access when removed from the wall and laid flat Interchangeable tray labels Modular design for easy expansion Optimized for strength with minimal support material Easy assembly No additional hardware required, except your chosen wall mounting method (4 mm screws or adhesive) Dimensions Case: 60 × 60 × 60 mm (excluding protruding handle) Internal tray storage: approximately 45 × 44 × 40 mm Included Files (STEP) STEP files are included for self-slicing, modification, and further development (encouraged!). Bracket – Expandable snap-together wall bracket. Central mounting hole designed for a 4 mm screw with a maximum head diameter of 10 mm. Case – Main housing for the tray and locking mechanism. Tray – Sliding and rotating storage container. Label – Removable label insert with an easy-removal leverage tab. Lock – Sliding latch that mounts the container to the wall bracket. Snaps together with the handle. Handle – Used to remove the container from the wall bracket. Snaps together with the lock. Print Settings The print profile includes all of these settings by default, but if you'd prefer to slice it yourself, here are my recommendations. Global Settings Layer Height: 0.20 mm Walls: 3 Top/Bottom Layers: 4–5 Infill: 15% Gyroid or Cross Hatch Material: PLA is recommended due to easier support removal, although any material that allows clean support removal should work well. Supports: Manual Tree Supports (Case & Bracket) Part Settings Bracket – Manual tree supports on the four overhanging surfaces. Case – Manual tree supports on the three overhanging surfaces. Tray – Print-in-place part. Do not disassemble or split. Label – Edit the text before slicing. A 5–6 mm font works well. Use Arachne wall generation for improved text definition. Assembly (See the photo instructions in the carousel.) Print all required components, remove the supports, and ensure all supported surfaces are clean and free of debris. Needle nose pliers work well for bracket support removal. Container Assembly Take the case and tray and rotate them upside down so the print-in-place legs are secured. Press the leg tabs inward while pushing the tray into the case. This requires a fair amount of force, so don't be concerned. Once inserted, slide the tray back and forth a few times to ensure the tabs are seated correctly in the channels. Turn the assembly upright and insert the lock through the rear of the case with the "Top" text facing upwards. Insert the handle through the front of the case, again with the "Top" text facing upwards. Press the handle firmly into the lock until it clicks into place. Press the label firmly into the tray slot. To replace a label later, insert a flat-head screwdriver into the horizontal opening and gently pry it out. Check that the tray slides smoothly and locks in the parked position. Check the handle and lock operate freely under their own weight. If the handle does not go all the way down when locking to the bracket, this is because there is support material still on the bracket piece that needs removing. Bracket Assembly The brackets can be assembled before mounting or snapped onto an existing wall-mounted bracket assembly. Place one bracket onto another so the snap hooks overlap. Press firmly near the overlapping hooks until they snap together. Due to the strength of the snap-together design, only every other bracket in an array needs to be fixed to the wall. description: Thanks to ExtremeElementz for their awesome case! I spent the last day or two getting to know what I need to with Fusion360 to make these. I know there are many, many different vial types/sizes out there. Below are the height and width of the vials I used (which matched the many I have so I'm pretty sure they're standard). Boxes: 3ml - I tried to make it as close to the, uh… standard storage case a 10 pack normally comes in. description: 3D Printable Kerfmaker (Bridge City Inspired) Precision Joinery Without Measuring A kerfmaker is one of those simple woodworking tools that quickly becomes indispensable. It allows you to accurately size dados, grooves, rabbets, and other cuts to perfectly match the actual thickness of your material—without measuring, calipers, or complicated math. This is my own interpretation of the classic kerfmaker. I did not invent the kerfmaker , and credit for the original concept belongs to the woodworking community. My goal was to create a version that closely matches the functionality and style of the excellent Bridge City Toolworks Kerfmaker , while being easy to print, simple to assemble, and built with inexpensive, commonly available hardware. After searching MakerWorld, I noticed that many of the available printable kerfmakers were incomplete or required significant modification to become functional. This design is my attempt to provide a complete, easy-to-build solution that any woodworker with a 3D printer can make. Features Compact footprint 100 mm overall length 15.5 mm wide 38 mm tall Adjustable for a wide range of material thickness Captured hardware prevents nuts from spinning during adjustment Tight sliding keyway for accurate, repeatable settings Uses only four inexpensive pieces of hardware Perfect for table saws, router tables, dado setups, and joinery work Hardware Required You'll need: 1 × M4 × 16 mm flat head (countersunk) machine screw 1 × M4 × 20 mm flat head (countersunk) machine screw 2 × M4 hex nuts I used this metric hardware assortment: Metric Machine Screw Assortment Kit (Amazon) https://a.co/d/0eF5b6EH Any standard M4 hardware of the same sizes should also work. Assembly Assembly is straightforward and only takes a few minutes. The M4 nuts are captured inside the printed knobs during a pause in the print , creating comfortable hand-tightened knobs without requiring glue. The sliding fit between the parts is intentionally snug. The screw joining the two smaller pieces rides inside the keyway of the main body. The first 15–16 mm of travel may require some firm pressure as the screw head enters the slot. This is intentional and helps keep the assembly together during use. Once the screw passes this initial section, movement becomes much smoother while still maintaining a precise fit. If your printer runs slightly oversized, a light pass with fine sandpaper or a small file can make initial assembly easier. Why I Designed This I enjoy designing woodworking tools that solve practical problems in the shop. After looking around MakerWorld, I couldn't find a printable kerfmaker that checked all the boxes I was looking for, so I decided to design my own. My goals were to create a kerfmaker that was: Easy to print Easy to assemble Compact Durable Accurate Built using inexpensive, readily available hardware It's become a permanent addition to my own woodworking shop, and I hope it becomes one in yours as well. Disclaimer This is an original CAD model created by me. The kerfmaker concept has existed in woodworking for many years, and this design is inspired by the style and functionality of the Bridge City Toolworks Kerfmaker. description: Kumihimo Marudai Bracelet/Rope braiding stand This is a beginner friendly Kumihimo Marudai stand to make bracelets or rope using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The Marudai (Japanese, lit. “ Round Stand ”) allows you to move multiple strings at once using even back and forth movements of string to interlace the strings to form the weave of the bracelet or cord. This results in a faster weave compared to a hand-held portable Round Kumihimo Disc for round bracelets , but is less portable due to its larger form factor. Marudai stand with weighted bobbins and counterweight Usage A Kumihimo weave being formed through the center hole and pulled down by a counterweight attached to it The Marudai is used together with a center weight to pull on the formed weave through the hole in the center, and smaller weighted bobbins , called tama, on each individual string around the outsides. Commonly, the ratio of the weight is that the center weight will be between ½ to ⅔ of the combined weight of the outside weights. This balance ensures that the woven pattern will be consistent between each movement and result in a uniform shape and pattern of the bracelet/ropes. There is no hard rule of which side of the spectrum you decide on, it can depend on the particular use case of the weave. Using a heavier center weight will increase the pulling force and can result in a looser weave, whereas less center weight will provide lower resistance and give a tighter weave. You may purchase weighted bobbins and counterweights online or use 3D printed ones such as my Weighted Bobbin for Kumihimo braiding - Tama . Many different patterns of braids can be formed using a Marudai, such as alternating lines, dotted patterns, spirals and more. Assembly The assembly is quick and easy and can be done without tools. Hardware required Printed base , I recommend printing the weighted base, which gives the stand a stronger support Printed top disc , pick from a series of different discs depending on your level of experience and convenience desired Numbered Top disc with 32 notches and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Great for beginners or those transitioning from a Kumihimo hand disc due to the familiar style Numbered Top disc with 32 round guides and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids A nice balance between full notches and a fully round disc, giving the best of both worlds holding the strings loosely in position, but being able to move them with a push rather than having to lift them out of the notches to re-arrange for complex patterns Top disc with 32 round guides and markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Same disc, but without number labels Numbered Top round disc without indentations. Markers for 8-string and 16-string braids This is the traditional form of a marudai disc and allows for quick re-arranging of strands following a series of moves. This requires practice as the strings will only be held in place by gravity as they are not guided to a particular location Top round disc without indentations. Markers for 8-string and 16-string braids Same disc, but without number labels Connecting rods (4x) You can either: Get 1/2 inch (12.7mm) round dowel rods (such as round wooden dowels ) from your local hardware store and cut them to size (I recommend a length of ~9inches, or 20-25cm for each rod) Or print the provided rods (24cm in length - you may resize the length as desired and based on your printers print bed) Optional rod connectors to extend the heigh of the stand, by connecting multiple rods together to form a taller stand A1 mini print size variant Someone requested a variant to fit on the A1 mini print bed, so I've published a A1 mini (180mm) size print profile - the top discs are resized to fit the bed and the connecting rods shortened as well. The weighted base is the same between the A1 mini and regular size and can be used interchangably with the same spacing between rods. The A1 mini profile contains 3 top disc variants: Notches with numbers and guide marks Round guide petal with guide marks Round disc with guide marks Assembly steps Place the bottom disc on the table or stable surface - this may either be the weighted bottom disc Weighted bottom disc or you can also decide to use one of the other pattern top disc as a bottom disc Round top disc being used as a bottom disc Push the four (4) connecting rods into the slots If you want to give it a stronger hold, you may use some glue and attach them permanently to the base Now attach the top disc to the top side of the connecting rods If you want to be able to change between different top plates, then I recommend not using glue for the top side. Optionally: if you want to make the stand taller , use the printable rod connectors to connect multiple rods to form a taller stand You may want to place additional weights onto the bottom to ensure the stand remains stable Rods extended using the optional rod connector Print Settings Supports / Brim: No Layer height: 0.20 mm Infill: 15% cubic for parts, 100% rectilinear for weighted base Walls: 2 Wall generation: Arachne for smooth curves Top/bottom pattern: Monotonic Orientation: Flat on the bed Material: PETG or PLA Kumihimo collection I've made a series of Kumihimo braiding related models to help me make neat Kumihimo braids, check them out: Weighted Bobbins for Kumihimo braiding To complement your Marudai, if you don't already have weights, you can print a set of Weighted Bobbin for Kumihimo braiding which make it easier to make neat braids by maintaining an even tension on the braid.
