This generator lets you create one instead of digging through drawers full of funnels that are somehow all the wrong size. Adjust the funnel bowl, outlet, wall thickness, spout length, taper, and bend geometry to create everything from a basic straight funnel to a long offset funnel with two smooth bends. The default two-bend setup curves away from the center and then bends back so the final outlet points straight down again. Everything is generated as one continuous model with a smooth internal flow path. 🔧 Funnel Body Controls Setting What It Does Top Opening Diameter Controls the inside diameter of the large funnel opening. Outlet Diameter Controls the inside diameter where the funnel bowl transitions into the spout. Funnel Height Changes the height and steepness of the funnel bowl. Wall Thickness Controls the thickness of the funnel body and spout walls. Top Rim Turns the reinforced rim around the top opening on or off. Rim Height Controls how tall the rim extends above the funnel body. Rim Thickness Controls how far the rim extends outward. 📏 Spout Controls Setting What It Does Spout Length Controls the total centerline length of the complete spout, including all straight and curved sections. Spout Style Selects a straight-diameter or tapered spout. Spout End Diameter Controls the outlet diameter at the very end when a tapered spout is selected. Spout Path Selects a straight spout, one bend, or two bends. The spout length is measured along the entire path, not just vertically from the funnel. Increasing a bend angle or radius uses more of the selected spout length. ↪️ First Bend Controls Setting What It Does First Bend Start Distance Controls how far the spout travels straight down before the first bend begins. First Bend Angle Controls how far the first bend turns away from vertical. First Bend Radius Controls how tight or wide the first curve is. First Bend Direction Selects whether the spout bends left or right. A larger bend radius creates a smoother, wider curve. A smaller radius creates a tighter elbow. ↩️ Second Bend Controls Setting What It Does Distance Between Bends Controls the straight section between the end of the first bend and the beginning of the second. Second Bend Angle Mode Selects whether the second bend automatically matches the first bend or uses a custom angle. Second Bend Angle Controls the second bend angle when Custom mode is selected. Second Bend Radius Controls how tight or wide the second curve is. Second Bend Direction Selects whether the second bend continues in the same direction or bends back the opposite way. Match First Mode When the second bend is set to Match First and the direction is set to Opposite , the second bend automatically cancels the angle of the first bend. For example: First bend: 55° right Second bend: 55° left Final outlet direction: straight down This creates an offset spout while keeping the outlet vertical. Custom Mode Select Custom to control the second bend independently. This allows the final outlet to point inward, outward, sideways, or at any angle between the available limits. 🛡️ Automatic Geometry Protection The generator automatically checks the selected measurements and adjusts impossible combinations that would otherwise create broken geometry. This includes: Bend angles that consume more than the available spout length Bend start distances that are too long Excessive spacing between the bends Bend radii that are too tight for the selected spout size Negative final straight sections Invalid outlet or wall-thickness combinations Any automatic adjustments are shown in the OpenSCAD console so you can see which setting was limited. 💡 Possible Uses Automotive fluid funnels Oil and coolant funnels Bottle filling Powder transfer Seed and pellet funnels Resin and paint transfer Workshop machines Aquarium equipment Kitchen containers Hard-to-reach fill ports Offset container openings Custom replacement funnels Because every dimension is adjustable, the same generator can create a small precision funnel or a large workshop funnel. 📐 Design Notes The curved spout is generated as one continuous swept tube. Both the inside and outside follow the same centerline path through the straight sections and bends. This creates: Smooth internal transitions Consistent wall thickness No sharp joints between sections One continuous watertight model Proper tapered geometry through the curves

description: Apothecary Cabinet Generator V1.1 This is a fully parametric apothecary cabinet generator that lets you make a custom little drawer cabinet without having to model the whole thing from scratch every time. You choose the cabinet size, drawer size, number of rows, number of columns, wall thickness, clearances, top cap, base style, drawer face details, and a bunch of other options. The generator builds the cabinet around the drawer size you choose, then also generates one matching drawer that fits that cabinet. This version uses one uniform drawer size across the whole cabinet. That means every opening is the same size, and the tool generates one matching drawer that you can duplicate in your slicer. So if you make a 4x3 cabinet, you print one cabinet and duplicate the drawer 12 times. Simple, clean, and way less annoying than generating a pile of separate drawer files for no reason. The cabinet is built around the drawer size you pick. Change the drawer width, height, or depth, and the whole cabinet recalculates around it. You can make tiny parts drawers, craft storage, dice drawers, bead organizers, mini hardware cabinets, display cabinets, or whatever other small nonsense needs organized. 🧰 Display / Export Modes Setting What It Does Both Shows the cabinet and one drawer side by side. Good for previewing the full setup. Cabinet Shows only the cabinet body. Use this when exporting the cabinet STL. Drawer Shows only the matching drawer. Use this when exporting the drawer STL. Fit Test Shows one drawer placed inside the cabinet so you can check the fit before printing everything. The Fit Test mode is useful before wasting filament on a big cabinet. You can choose which row and column the test drawer appears in and how far it is pulled out. 🗄️ Cabinet Grid Settings Setting What It Controls Columns How many drawer openings go across the cabinet. Rows How many drawer openings go up the cabinet. Drawer Width The outside width of the drawer body. The cabinet openings are calculated from this. Drawer Height The outside height of the drawer body. This controls the height of each opening. Drawer Depth The depth of the drawer body. This also controls how deep the cabinet needs to be. Drawer count is: Rows x Columns Examples: Cabinet Size Drawer Count 2x2 4 drawers 3x3 9 drawers 4x3 12 drawers 5x4 20 drawers 6x5 30 drawers You only need to export one drawer, then duplicate it in the slicer until you have the right amount. 📏 Clearance Settings Setting What It Does Fit Clearance XY Clearance around the drawer on the left, right, top, and bottom. This is what lets the drawer actually slide. Fit Clearance Depth Extra space behind the drawer so it does not bottom out against the back panel. Divider Thickness Thickness of the walls between drawer openings. Back Panel Turns the cabinet back panel on or off. Back Thickness Thickness of the back panel if enabled. Important part: Fit Clearance XY is per side. So if you set: Fit Clearance XY: 0.5 mm That gives the drawer: Side Clearance Left 0.5 mm Right 0.5 mm Top 0.5 mm Bottom 0.5 mm That means the actual cabinet opening becomes: Drawer Width + 1.0 mm Drawer Height + 1.0 mm Start with 0.5 mm for most FDM printers. If your printer is super dialed in, you can try less. If the drawers are tight, bump it up. Tiny drawers are tolerance nightmares (sometimes), because apparently plastic enjoys lying to us! 🏛️ Cabinet Style Settings Setting What It Controls Cabinet Front Frame Adds a raised frame around the front outside edge of the cabinet. Cabinet Frame Width How wide that front frame is. Cabinet Frame Projection How far the front frame sticks out from the cabinet face. Top Cap Turns the top cap on or off. Top Cap Thickness How thick the top cap is. Top Cap Side Overhang How far the top cap sticks out on the left and right sides. Top Cap Front Overhang How far the top cap sticks out over the front. Top Cap Back Overhang How far the top cap sticks out in the back. Set this to 0 for a flat back. Base Plinth Adds a raised front base piece under the cabinet. Base Plinth Height How tall the base plinth is. Base Plinth Projection How far the base plinth sticks out from the front. For a cabinet that sits flat against a wall, use: Top Cap Back Overhang: 0 That keeps the back clean instead of giving it a useless little roof spoiler. 🦶 Base Foot Styles Option What It Does No Feet No extra feet added. Clean flat cabinet. Four Block Feet Adds block feet at all four corners. Front Block Feet Adds feet only on the front. Good for a more decorative front-facing cabinet. Side Runners Adds long runner-style feet along the sides. Full Raised Base Adds one full solid raised base under the cabinet. Setting What It Controls Foot Width Width of each foot or runner. Foot Depth Depth of block feet. Foot Height How tall the feet or raised base are. 📦 Drawer Body Settings Setting What It Controls Drawer Wall Thickness Thickness of the drawer side walls. Drawer Bottom Thickness Thickness of the drawer floor. Drawer Front Thickness Thickness of the visible front face of the drawer. Drawer Front Overlap How much the drawer face overlaps the cabinet opening. Drawer Face Gap Gap between neighboring drawer fronts. Helps stop drawer faces from colliding. The drawer body is hollowed automatically. The front face is slightly larger than the drawer body so it covers the opening cleanly. The overlap is automatically limited so if you make a bunch of drawers side by side, the fronts do not crash into each other like badly parked shopping carts. 🎛️ Drawer Front Detail Switches Instead of a confusing preset menu, the drawer details are controlled with simple on/off switches. Switch What It Adds Use Raised Border Adds a raised rectangular border around the drawer face. Use Round Knob Adds a simple centered round knob. Use Bar Pull Adds a horizontal handle across the drawer front. Use Label Holder Adds a raised rectangular label holder. Use Card Catalog Face Adds a card-catalog style label frame and pull lip. Use Cup Pull Face Adds a wider raised pull plate style front. For the classic apothecary/card catalog look, I recommend: Setting Value Use Raised Border True Use Card Catalog Face True Use Round Knob False Use Bar Pull False Use Label Holder False Use Cup Pull Face False That gives it the old little-label-and-pull-lip look without turning the drawer into decorative soup. 🏷️ Raised Border Settings Setting What It Controls Raised Border Width Thickness of the raised border lines. Raised Border Raise How far the border sticks out from the drawer face. Raised Border Inset How far inward the border sits from the edge of the drawer front. Use this when you want the drawer face to look more finished and less like a plain cube pretending to have a personality. 🔘 Round Knob Settings Setting What It Controls Knob Diameter Size of the round knob. Knob Projection How far the knob sticks out. Knob Height Position Vertical position of the knob on the drawer front. Good for simple drawers or old cabinet-style fronts. 🧲 Bar Pull Settings Setting What It Controls Bar Pull Width Percent Width of the bar pull as a percentage of the drawer width. Bar Pull Diameter Thickness of the bar handle. Bar Pull Projection How far the handle sticks out from the drawer front. Bar Pull Height Position Vertical position of the bar handle. This makes the drawer look more modern or industrial. 📝 Label Holder Settings Setting What It Controls Label Width Percent Width of the label holder based on drawer width. Label Height Percent Height of the label holder based on drawer height. Label Frame Thickness Thickness of the label holder border. Label Raise How far the label holder sticks out. Label Height Position Vertical position of the label holder. Good for parts drawers, craft storage, bead storage, hardware sorting, and all the other tiny organized-chaos stuff. 🗂️ Card Catalog Face Settings Setting What It Controls Card Plate Raise How far the card catalog details stick out. Card Pull Lip Diameter Thickness of the little pull lip. Card Label Width Percent Width of the card label frame. Card Label Height Percent Height of the card label frame. Card Label Height Position Vertical position of the label frame. Card Pull Width Percent Width of the pull lip. Card Pull Height Position Vertical position of the pull lip. This is the best setting group for the classic apothecary look. It gives the drawer that old card-catalog vibe without needing actual metal hardware. 🥣 Cup Pull Face Settings Setting What It Controls Cup Pull Width Percent Width of the cup pull plate. Cup Pull Height Percent Height of the cup pull plate. Cup Pull Raise How far the cup pull plate sticks out. Cup Pull Height Position Vertical position of the cup pull. This gives the drawer a chunkier pull face. It works better on larger drawers. On tiny drawers, it can get crowded fast, because tiny drawers are dramatic. 🖨️ Printing Workflow Set your rows, columns, and drawer size. Set Fit Clearance XY to around 0.5 mm . Use Fit Test mode to check one drawer in the cabinet. Export the cabinet using Cabinet mode. Export the drawer using Drawer mode. Duplicate the drawer in your slicer. Example: Cabinet What To Print 4x3 cabinet 1 cabinet + 12 drawers 5x4 cabinet 1 cabinet + 20 drawers 6x5 cabinet 1 cabinet + 30 drawers ✅ Suggested First Test Setting Value Columns 2 Rows 2 Drawer Width 42 mm Drawer Height 28 mm Drawer Depth 55 mm Fit Clearance XY 0.5 mm Fit Clearance Depth 1.0 mm Divider Thickness 2.4 mm Drawer Wall Thickness 1.6 mm Drawer Bottom Thickness 1.8 mm Print a small 2x2 first before going huge. Once the fit is good, scale it up and go nuts. ⚠️ Current Limitation This version uses one drawer size for the whole cabinet. That means all openings are the same size. A future version may add different drawer sizes per row or multiple drawer types, but this one is meant to be clean, usable, and not an OpenSCAD crime scene with knobs.

Mount with screws through the backplate, or leave Add_Screws off and stick it down with VHB tape/adhesive for a no-drill option. This is my most complicated parametric model upload so far. Parameters: Object_Width / Object_Depth — size of the item you're gripping Gripper_Height — how tall the jaw is (more height = more grip) Jaw_Backplate_Distance — affects jaw flex/strength; lower = tighter grip, higher = easier insertion Wall_Thickness — structural wall thickness Rib_Height — decorative/grip ribs, 1–2mm advised Screw_Body_Diameter / Screw_Head_Diameter / Screw_Spacing — mounting hole sizing Add_Screws — 1 for screw holes, 0 for a clean adhesive-mount back Print notes: PETG is a good shout here since the jaws rely on some flex to spring closed — PLA works too but will be a bit more brittle over repeated open/close cycles. 3–4 walls recommended for jaw strength, 0.20mm layer height. 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: Membership 🔐 MEMBERSHIP UNLOCK 🎁 Monthly custom model just for YOU 🛍 Full print/sell rights on all my models 📸 Access to my photos & post templates 🙏 Support my family + fuel my madness Threaded Bottle & Cap Generator This generator lets you create a completely custom threaded bottle and matching screw-on cap without having to manually model either part. Adjust the bottle size, wall thickness, shoulder, neck, thread profile, cap grip, sealing style, and more. The bottle and cap are generated together so the threads stay matched, and the bottle includes a solid collar that gives the cap a proper mechanical stopping point instead of letting it screw down until the threads become loose. The default settings create a compact general-purpose container, but the same generator can make small parts jars, hardware containers, storage bottles, prop containers, decorative bottles, and larger screw-top canisters. 🧴 Output Mode Choose exactly what the generator displays: Setting What it does Bottle Only Generates only the threaded bottle Cap Only Generates only the matching cap Bottle and Cap Places both parts in a printable layout Assembled Preview Shows the cap installed on the bottle Exploded Preview Separates the parts vertically so the thread alignment can be inspected 📐 Bottle Settings Setting What it controls Bottle Diameter Overall width of the main bottle body Bottle Height Overall height of the body below the shoulder Wall Thickness Thickness of the bottle’s outer walls Bottom Thickness Thickness of the solid printable base Shoulder Height Height of the transition between the body and neck Shoulder Style Changes how sharply or smoothly the bottle narrows Neck Diameter Outer diameter of the bottle neck before threading Neck Height Available threaded height above the bottle shoulder Bottom Edge Radius Rounds the outside bottom edge while keeping the base flat The internal cavity automatically follows the exterior dimensions while preserving the selected wall and bottom thicknesses. 🔩 Thread Settings Setting What it controls Thread Pitch Vertical distance between each thread rotation Thread Depth How far the thread extends from the neck Thread Clearance Radial space between the bottle and cap threads Thread Direction Generates right-hand or left-hand threads Thread Profile Controls the printable shape of the thread Thread Resolution Controls the smoothness of the helical geometry The bottle and cap threads automatically extend through the usable neck and cap height. This allows the cap to catch immediately at the opening instead of having the first usable thread buried inside the cap. The default thread profile is designed around FDM printing rather than using an excessively sharp mechanical V-thread that may look accurate in CAD but print poorly. 🛑 Cap-Stop Collar The bottle includes a collar directly below the threaded neck. This gives the cap a solid stopping surface and prevents it from being tightened past the useful thread engagement. Setting What it controls Collar Height Vertical thickness of the stop collar Collar Overhang How far the collar extends beyond the cap Collar Lower Bevel Softens the lower outside edge of the collar The upper collar surface remains flat so the cap always stops at a consistent height. 🧢 Cap Settings Setting What it controls Cap Height Total height of the screw-on cap Cap Wall Thickness Thickness surrounding the internal thread Cap Top Thickness Thickness of the closed top surface Cap Clearance Additional fit allowance between the cap and bottle Grip Style Selects the exterior cap texture Grip Depth Controls how strongly the grip pattern projects Grip Count Adjusts the number of ribs or scallops Top Style Selects a flat, raised, recessed, or rounded top Cap Edge Radius Rounds the outside top edge Available Grip Styles Smooth Vertical Ribbed Hex Scalloped The cap is automatically placed open-side-up in the preview and flipped into a printable orientation when using the separated print layout. 🔒 Seal Options Setting What it does No Seal Uses only the threaded cap and bottle lip Compression Ring Adds a raised contact ring beneath the cap top Internal Plug Adds a plug that enters the bottle opening when tightened The seal features can improve closure alignment, but actual liquid sealing depends heavily on printer accuracy, material, layer quality, and the selected clearance. This generator is not intended for pressurized containers. 🖨️ Fit Adjustment The default thread clearance is intended as a practical starting point for normal FDM printing. Increase the clearance when the cap is too tight or decrease it when the fit is excessively loose. Different printers, materials, nozzle sizes, extrusion settings, and part cooling can all affect the final fit. A small test bottle is recommended before generating a very large container. ⚠️ Important Use Notes This tool creates general-purpose printed containers. Printed parts should not automatically be considered watertight, airtight, food-safe, chemically resistant, or suitable for pressure. Suitability depends on the selected material, printer, coating, and intended use.

description: ⚠️ Measure your power strip before printing! This is a parametric model. Do NOT print it using the default dimensions unless your power strip matches them. Before generating the model, carefully measure your power strip and enter its dimensions. 1. Add extra length The length of the enclosure should be slightly longer than the actual power strip. Since the power strip is inserted from the top at an angle, it needs some extra clearance during installation. If the enclosure is exactly the same length as the power strip, inserting it will be difficult or even impossible. I recommend adding at least 5 mm (typically 5–8 mm) to the measured length to ensure easy installation. Example: Measured power strip length: 250 mm Enclosure length: 255–258 mm The width and height can remain much closer to the actual dimensions, but the length should always include this additional clearance. 2. Check the cable exit position Before printing, check the distance between the top surface of the power strip and the top of the cable exit (see reference image). This check is important because the power strip is inserted from above. If the cable exits too close to the top of the power strip and your desk is thick, the cable may interfere with the underside of the tabletop during installation. You can verify the required height using this rule: Measure the distance between the top of the power strip and the top of the cable exit . Subtract your desk thickness . Subtract 6 mm (design clearance already accounted for in the model) . Available clearance = (top-to-cable-exit distance) − desk thickness − 6 mm If the result is positive or zero , the default height is sufficient. If the result is negative , increase the model height by that amount (absolute value). Example Top to cable exit: 20 mm Desk thickness: 25 mm Result: 20 − 25 − 6 = −11 mm → Increase height by 11 mm 3. Printing instructions This is a parametric model , meaning you only need to adjust three main values to fit your power strip: Length Width Height Once these values are set, the model will automatically adapt to your specific power strip dimensions. Two-part design The model is split into two separate parts : Top part Bottom part Both parts must be generated using the exact same dimensions to ensure a proper fit. Orientation for printing After exporting the models: The bottom part can be printed as-is. The top part must be rotated 180° before printing to ensure correct orientation and printability + This is necessary due to the geometry of the design. Assembly After printing, the bottom part must be permanently glued to the top part . Once glued, the two parts form a single rigid enclosure ready for installation into the desk. Important note This model was created in Fusion 360 , and while it is fully functional and parametric, this also means there are some design limitations related to the way parameters and exported bodies behave . For this reason, always double-check the exported geometry before slicing. If you follow the steps above, the model should print and assemble without issues. i may try to remodel this in open scad in the future About this model Turn any standard power strip into a clean, recessed desk power outlet. Instead of buying an expensive built-in desk power strip, this parametric model lets you install a regular power strip directly into your desk. Simply customize the dimensions to fit your own power strip, print the enclosure, cut an opening in the tabletop, and press-fit the insert into place. Why I designed this Most recessed desk power strips available online are: expensive available in only a few sizes often made by unknown brands with questionable quality Instead, I bought a high-quality standard power strip from a trusted manufacturer and designed this enclosure to create the same built-in look. The result is: lower cost better electrical quality freedom to choose the power strip you trust a clean and professional-looking installation If you build one, I'd love to see your Make!

Designed to securely hold everything from a Nintendo Switch to a large iPad/Tablet , it’s the perfect companion for road trips. Key Features Universal Compatibility: Adjustable clamp system that fits smartphones, gaming consoles (Nintendo Switch), and tablets. True Quick-Release: Drop your device in and lock it in seconds, making it effortless to take your device with you when leaving the car. Innovative Fast-Thread Nut: The locking nut only has threads on one half. This means you can slide it freely into position and tighten or loosen it with just a quarter-turn ($1/4$ turn) . Do not try to screw it into place—simply press it firmly together. Print Settings & Tips Material: Since this sits in a car, PETG, ASA, or ABS is highly recommended to withstand summer heat. Avoid standard PLA as it may deform on hot days. Orientation: Check the sliced preview or standard print profiles for the optimal printing orientation. Step-by-Step Guide Prepare the Parts: Gather the main arm, the tablet/Switch clamp components, and your hardware (or the 3D-printed press-fit bolt). Snap the Clamp Together: The main holding bracket and the adjustment nut snap directly together. No tools are needed for this part—just align them and press until they click. Orient the Fast-Thread Nut: When sliding the components onto the main threaded rod, make sure the innovative Fast-Thread Nut is positioned at the very top . Secure the Pivot: Use the M5 x 35mm bolt and nut (or the 3D-printed press-fit pin) to secure the tilt/angle mechanism. If using the 3D-printed pin: Remember to press it firmly into place rather than screwing it. Your headrest mount is now ready to be installed in the car! How to Setup & Use (Daily Operation) Once assembled, setting up your mount for the first time is incredibly easy, and daily use is lightning fast thanks to the quick-release mechanism. Initial Setup (First Time Only) Set the Height: Move the top nut (the Fast-Thread Nut) to the desired height where you want your device to sit, and twist it a quarter-turn to lock it in place. Insert Your Device: Place your iPad, Nintendo Switch, or phone into the bottom clamp. Secure the Base: Srew the bottom nut up against the device and tighten it gently. ⚠️ Note: Do not overtighten! Just tighten it enough so your device sits securely and cannot slide out. Daily Use (Quick Release) Once the bottom bracket is set to your device's size, you never have to adjust it again! Taking your device out: Simply loosen the top Fast-Thread Nut with a quarter-turn (1/4 turn) , slide it up, and take your device with you. Putting your device back in: Drop your device back into the cradle, slide the top nut down against it, and lock it with a quarter-turn . Voilà! Rod Spacing: The distance between the two headrest rods (either measured center-to-center, or the inner clearance between them). description: I was not a fan of the Packout M12 battery plate. It's awkward to squeeze the tabs to remove the batteries. Theirs only holds 4 batteries. So I designed my own…. It holds up to 10 Milwaukee M12 Batteries or 10 Bosch 12V Batteries. They are angled so that gravity holds them in and they are easy to remove. If you use the Large M12 batteries, you can only use one per row so it only holds 5 of those. Mix and match to your hearts delight. There are three separate models: H2 Sized Version: Prints diagonally to fix on a build plate. For H2D and H2C, uses filament in the left extruder to overcome printing size limitation. A1/P1/P2/X1/X2 Sized Version: Prints as a top and a bottom part which slides together with pins to lock everything in place. Identical to H2 Sized version once joined together. A1 Mini Sized Version: A smaller version that only holds two rows of batteries but is small enough to print on almost any printer. All versions include a foot and wedges to lock them into place. To install it, insert it into the wide section on the bottom. Slide it up into the section with the grooves. Then put the wedge in. The dimples on the wedge are on the lower side. Squeeze the tabs and push down evenly. When everything is flush and the foot can't slide out, you've done it perfectly. The fit is pretty tight, but all three of my worked in ABS, PETG and ABS on my three Bambu printers. Because of PLA creep, I recommend printing in ABS or PETG, but I am trying PLA for the first time, time will tell. This design does not have a clip to prevent you from lifting it off, gravity does a good job of that. I have a variety of designs for hanging things from Milwaukee Packout Mounting plates. description: Fly Swatter Fan – Holographic Fly Deterrent Help keep flies away from your food without chemicals or loud buzzing! This Fly Swatter Fan uses spinning TPU blades that display the holographic texture transferred from a textured PEI build plate. As the blades rotate, they create constantly changing flashes of reflected light that discourage flies from landing near your food. How It Works Flies have compound eyes that are highly sensitive to movement and rapidly changing light. As the holographic blades spin, they create constantly shifting reflections that can make the area appear unstable or difficult for flies to land in. Because of this, flies will often choose to fly somewhere else instead. Unlike sticky traps or chemical repellents, this design relies only on motion and reflected light to help discourage flies from landing near your food. Features 🪰 Designed to help discourage flies from landing on food. ✨ Uses a holographic/textured PEI build plate to create reflective effects. 🧪 Chemical-free operation. 🔇 Very quiet while running. 🔋 Powered by 3 AAA batteries using the Maker's Beginner Kit motor and battery hardware. 🛡️ Flexible TPU blades are designed to stop spinning if they encounter resistance, such as being touched, helping reduce the chance of injury. Printing Recommendations Print the blades in TPU for flexibility. Print the reflective side directly on a holographic/textured PEI build plate for the best effect. Use a light-colored filament to maximize the holographic reflections. Balance the blades for smooth, quiet operation. Disclaimer This device is intended as a fly deterrent, not a guaranteed insect repellent. Effectiveness may vary depending on lighting conditions, fly species, and the surrounding environment. This is my first design including motors so issues may arise and I love to hear feedback. If you enjoy this design, please leave a like, upload a Make, and share your print settings. Motor Assembly Place Part 1 (pictured at the bottom from left to right) over the motor. Slide the gear Part 2 onto the motor shaft. Install Part 3 on top of the gear. Insert the completed motor assembly into the bottom of Part 4 . Apply a small drop of glue to Part 1 to secure the motor assembly inside Part 4 . Slide Part 5 into place and snap the assembly together. Blade Assembly Slide the two TPU blades into the slots on the top hub, making sure the holographic textured side is facing upward . Main Tower Assembly Connect the motor to the battery box using the supplied wires. Insert the + (cross-shaped) axle into the motor shaft. Apply a small amount of glue around the outside of Part 5 inside the motor housing. Slide the completed motor assembly into the bottom of the cone until it is fully seated, making sure the cross-shaped axle protrudes through the top. Install the battery box by fitting its four corners into the matching slots in the cone. Ensure the ON/OFF switch is facing downward . Press the blade assembly onto the cross-shaped axle until it is fully seated. Install 3 AAA batteries , switch the fan on, and enjoy a quieter, chemical-free way to help discourage flies from landing near your food.

Stuff with intricate parts that were controlled by one smooth motion, and did something complex with it. Bar linkages come to mind most for me. Walking machines that are controlled by one single rotary motor, long gear trains, they all stuck out to me. When looking at finger mechanisms, I noticed that all of them required many intricate moving parts in order to get that smooth finger motion with one smooth motion. I knew I could probably do something like that with less parts, and I had some prior knowledge on bar linkages, so with some time, I got a working finger that had very few parts to it that was also proportioned correctly. With some more adapting, I successfully added a palm for 4 more fingers, and an adjustable wrist, and now, it's a wearable prosthetic! the back is carved out so that someone can put there arm into the back, and use a custom silicone mold to make it a snug fit. the fingers are controlled by strings running from the knuckles to the wrist and then strapped to your upper arm, where bending your elbow will make the fingers curl into a fist. there are a few ways to make the fingers retract, those being either a spring mounted under the knuckle, or a rubber band connecting the knuckle axle with a joint axle further up the finger. This model has many small parts, so if possible, exchange the axles for metal wires. The attached images depict how you should assemble it: Each part number is labeled so that its easier to tell axles apart. follow instructions CAREFULLY, and use the guide as closely as possible. I highly recommend using a 0.2mm nozzle instead of 0.4, but I didn't have a 0.2mm nozzle, so that's why the print profile is set to 0.4 Pins may have a tight tolerance, so sanding the holes to be wider is necessary. Most parts of the model have the tight tolerances accounted for, making them looser, but certain segments of the model require manual hole compensation, due to not all printers being perfect. feel free to scale up the model to whatever size fits you, but the model is scaled to the size of the average person's hand. description: You drop it in the hole, give the knob a turn, and it locks. No wiggle, no lifting out when you plane or sand. A wedge inside the pin spreads three collet fingers against the wall of the dog hole, so the harder your workpiece pushes back, the more the pin bites in. When you are done, back the knob off half a turn and it drops right out. This is the locking version of my In-Line Bench Dog Clamp . The original held with friction alone, which works for planing but can creep out under vibration from an orbital sander. This one grips mechanically and stays put. Two variants, pick the one that matches your holes: EU / MFT for 20mm holes US for 3/4 inch holes Both use the same cheap M6 hardware. Key Features Locks into the hole, does not lift out under sanding or side load One pin covers a range of hole sizes, so slightly worn or oversized holes still grip Uses standard M6 hardware, a dollar at any hardware store and available worldwide Releases with half a turn, no tools Collet body prints support free, only the pusher arms need light support Which variant EU / MFT : fits holes 19.7 to 20.1mm US : fits holes 18.8 to 19.2mm If your holes were drilled with a 20mm bit, use EU. If drilled with a 3/4 inch bit, use US. When in doubt, measure an actual hole with a caliper, the number matters more than the bit that made it. Hardware you need One M6 x 60mm screw One M6 nut A standard hex nut is fine. Both parts press into their sockets, no glue needed. Assembly Press the M6 screw head into the hex socket on the underside of the cone Push the cone up into the pin, ribs lining up with the slots The screw shaft comes up through the top of the pin Set the T pusher onto the pin crown Press the M6 nut into the knob Thread the knob onto the screw and tighten Using it Drop the pin into the dog hole. Turn the knob to lock, the cone pulls up and spreads the fingers against the hole wall. The pusher end presses your workpiece. To release, back the knob off about half a turn. If it was cranked down hard and the cone stays wedged, unscrew a bit more and press down on the knob, it pops free. Hints PLA works, tested under an orbital sander with no lift The pin prints vertical as oriented on the plate and needs supports The pusher prints flat, add brim ears at the narrow tip so it does not lift Cone and knob print flat, they only need support inside the nut socket Do not leave it clamped down for long stretches, PLA can take a set under constant load. Want a cute storage solution for your knick-knacks? Wish you had a quick and easy setup for displaying them at a market or craft fair? Look no further! I combined these concepts into one 3-tiered solution. This is the mini version, meaning each box is ~45mm wide and ~35mm deep (except for the bottom box, which is closer to 40mm deep). (Full-size version is near-complete, but it doesn't stay together as securely as Id like!) I designed them to sit nicely on top of each other when closed, and used the back-brace as a way to secure it all together as well as support it when displayed. When fully open for display, I noticed the middle box sagged backwards a little, so I made a little spacer that wedges into the middle divider and against the topmost box to keep it straight! The back-brace also shifts down to support the full height of the display when open, and back up when it's packed up again. I can hold and shake this thing sideways, frontways, upsidedown, and toss it into a large box with other loose things, and it stays closed quite well! I recommend PETG for the bolts that hold the screws on, but PLA should work too. (Just be sure to sloooow down the first layer of PETG if you use it, I had a fun time working out how to get the thing to stick down with such a small object). Requires: Two (2) 2.5mm x 10 mm screws (to hold the back brace on) and Sixteen (16) 2.5mm x 8mm screws (to attached the levers to the boxes). I used machine screws as that's what I had, but any screw in those sizes should work! The holes for the screws may need a bit of loosening if your filament has sagged down, I found this was easier than dealing with supports for them. Assembly is as simple as attaching the levers and the back-brace to the boxes as shown in the photos. The top lid slides on and off, and has a small lip to secure it in place when closed. I usually just keep the spacer wedge for the middle box inside one of the middle compartments for when I open it up. This is my first proper 3D model! I'm very open to improvements, so please try it out for yourself and let me know what you think!

description: Drill perfectly centered, perfectly perpendicular 10 mm holes for Blum TIP-ON (push-to-open) units – no drill press, no wandering bit, no worn-out plastic guides. The jig slips over the front edge of the cabinet side panel and guides the drill through two stacked steel ball bearings, so the bit never touches plastic. Steel-on-steel guidance means zero wear and a dead-straight hole, every single time. The bearings are the cheap and ubiquitous 6800 / 61800 size (10 × 19 × 5 mm) – two per jig, a few cents each. Two print profiles Single – one cabinet side: the hole lands exactly in the middle of an 18 mm board. Double – two cabinets standing side by side: drill the first hole, rotate the jig 180°, align with the same mark, drill the second. Hole spacing comes out at exactly 18 mm, both holes at the same height. Features Ball bearing drill guide – two stacked 6800 bearings in a press-fit seat, dropped in from the top Sight slits – through slits in both side walls, exactly in the hole axis; line them up with your pencil mark on the panel face Chip evacuation channel – a full-length channel at board-edge level, open at both ends, so chips escape along the edge instead of packing under the bearings Lead-in chamfers on the slot for easy fitting over the panel Usually prints without supports (if the relief holes are big enough, but turn supports on and let slicer decide) How to use Mark the TIP-ON position on the panel face with a pencil. Slide the jig over the panel edge and align the sight slits with the mark. Drop the two bearings into the seat. Drill to depth, pecking a few times – chips clear through the side channel. A standard 10 × 133 mm bit easily reaches the ~50 mm needed for TIP-ON (the jig adds 15 mm of travel). Double variant: rotate the jig 180°, re-align with the same mark, drill hole number two. Fully parametric (Customizer) Everything is adjustable: board thickness, drill diameter, bearing dimensions and count, tolerances, wall thickness, slot depth and more. The highlights: board_thickness – default 18 mm, set it to whatever your panels are bearing_od, bearing_thickness, bearing_count – use whatever bearings (or drill sleeves) you have on hand bearing_fit – default +0.05 mm press fit; if the seat comes out too tight on your printer, increase it or use X-Y hole compensation in the slicer double_seats – with bearings or sleeves small enough (OD ≤ board thickness − 0.4 mm), the double variant can generate both seats side by side, no rotating needed relief_width – chip channel width; 0 = automatically matched to the drill pass-through hole It also works as a general centered edge-drilling guide (dowels and similar) – just set the drill diameter and bearing size to match. Printing Orientation: top face (bearing seat opening) on the bed - supports recommended Any rigid material; PLA or PETG with 3–4 walls works great Test-fit the bearings first – the chamfered seat opening helps press them in straight If you don't have the bearings yet, search for "6800" or "61800 bearing" (10 × 19 × 5 mm). You need two. Or any other with 10 mm inner diameter, you can always customize the model.

This is a super strong pegboard standoff, compatible with Ikea SKÅDIS. It is a redesign of a previous model . The previous model is fully 3D printed, whereas the model here uses an M4 bolt and nut for strength, which also makes it compatibility with the commercial equivalent. Features: looks similar to, and is interchangeable with, the Ikea SKÅDIS standoff (has the same thread and shape) super strong and reliable no print supports needed (internal sagging may occur but it is not visible) additional components needed: M4 16mm, hex head bolt and nut. Assembly The print comes in 4 parts: a standoff , which has lugs on the top that fit into the pegboard a knob , which is a disk that look just like the equivalent commercial part, it has a screwdriver slot on top a washer , which is a thin flat disks with a hole in it a filler , which is a small rectangular part with two prongs on one side. You will also need: a M4 16mm hex head bolt (similar lengths may also work), a M4 head head nut . Here are the steps. The slot in the standoff does not have print support. Check the slot and hole for any obstructions, removing any filament that did not properly adhere. Insert the M4 bolt into the knob , such that the head of the bolt is fully inside the knob. Slide the washer over the bolt and seat the washer into the knob . If the washer is loose that is okay. Insert the nut into the slot of the standoff and slide the nut into the recess. I find it helpful to use the bolt to position and pull the nut into place, but you may use other tools. Insert the filler into the slot of the standoff , prongs in first. The filler is tapered to match the taper of the joiner - the face of the filler that was on the build plate should be up, i.e., towards the lugs on the joiner. Warning : only insert the filler after the nut is properly in place in the standoff. Once a filler is pressed in, it can only be removed destructively. It's now ready to attached to your pegboard.

The hinge uses alternating barrel sections wrapped around a captive full-length pin. Adjustable clearances keep the moving parts separated during printing, while small breakaway tabs support the pin until the hinge is flexed free. 📐 Hinge Size Adjust the main dimensions to create anything from a small enclosure hinge to a larger cabinet-style hinge. Barrel outer diameter Captive pin diameter Radial clearance Axial knuckle clearance Knuckle count Left or right outer knuckles Leaf-to-barrel spacing Barrel reinforcement overlap The knuckle count is automatically kept odd so the alternating barrel pattern remains properly captured at both ends. 🔒 Captive Pin The pin runs through the entire hinge and includes retainers on both ends, preventing it from sliding out during use. The pin diameter, barrel size, clearance, retainer thickness, and end spacing can all be adjusted. Small breakaway tabs support the pin during printing. Flexing the hinge after printing breaks these tabs and releases the movement. 🔩 Mounting Holes Each hinge leaf has its own mounting-hole controls. Independent hole count per side Mounting-hole diameter Distance from the outer edge End spacing Straight holes Countersunk holes Counterbored holes Adjustable screw-head diameter Adjustable screw-head depth Set either side to zero holes for a blank leaf that can be glued, drilled manually, or modified in another program. 🖨️ Print Layout The hinge is generated in its correct print orientation with both leaves lying flat. model_name: Customizable NFC swatch folder (print in place)
description: Customizable Foldable Filament Swatch Folder A compact, print-in-place folder for organizing larger filament color swatches, with optional embedded NFC tags . The folder opens into an easy-to-browse swatch collection and folds into a compact stack for storage. Its larger 34 × 34 mm swatches provide plenty of visible filament surface and enough internal space for NFC stickers that are easier to scan reliably. The complete design is parametric. You can adjust the number of columns and rows, swatch dimensions, spacing, margins, thickness, hinge size, hole placement, and print tolerances directly in the MakerWorld Customizer. Main features Fully parametric folder and swatches Print-in-place folding mechanism, no separate hinge pins, screws or other hardware required Adjustable number of rows and columns Larger 34 × 34 mm swatches to accommodate larger NFC stickers that scan well Optional embedded NFC sticker compartment Four-swatch AMS profile for printing four filament colors together (tell your slicer to print by object, not by layer!) Adjustable swatch size, thickness and corner radius The supplied folder configurations holds: 48 swatches in a 6 × 8 arrangement, printable on H2 and A2L series printers. 28 swatches in a 4 × 7 arrangement, printable on P1, X1, X2, A1 series printers. 5×7 would fit in theory but the customizer allows increments of 2, so the folder can be closed properly. Choosing a swatch profile Single swatch with NFC Use the NFC-enabled single-swatch profile when you want to embed an NFC sticker. This version must be printed individually using a layer pause. Printing multiple swatches sequentially “by object” cannot be combined reliably with the required layer pause. Single swatch without NFC Use this profile when you only need a normal filament sample. No pause is required. Four swatches without NFC This profile places four swatches on one plate. Each swatch is a separate object, so four AMS filament slots can be mapped to four different colors. The four-swatch profile does not contain NFC cavities and does not require a pause. Inserting an NFC sticker The NFC option creates an enclosed cavity inside the swatch. The print must be paused immediately before the first layer that closes the cavity. Slice the NFC-enabled swatch. Open the layer preview. Locate the final layer where the NFC cavity is still open. Add a pause after that layer, immediately before the closing layer begins. Start the print. When the printer pauses, place the NFC sticker flat inside the cavity. Make sure the sticker is completely below the current print surface and cannot catch the nozzle. Resume the print so the following layers seal it inside the swatch. The exact layer number can change with your selected layer height, so always verify the pause in the sliced preview. Program and test the NFC sticker before sealing it inside the swatch. Important: NFC versus four-color printing The two workflows are intentionally separate: NFC enabled: print one swatch at a time and use the required layer pause. NFC disabled: no pause is needed, and you may use the four-swatch AMS profile to print four different filament colors together. Do not use the four-object sequential-print workflow for NFC swatches. A layer pause applies to the print sequence as a whole and does not provide the correct insertion point independently for every object. Bambu Slicer just does not (yet?) support multiple pauses in print by object mode. Printing the folder The folder prints in place with the hinges already assembled. After removing it from the build plate, gently move each hinge through a small range before folding it completely. If the hinges or swatches are too tight or too loose on your printer, adjust the corresponding tolerance values in the parametric model. No supports or assembly hardware are required with the supplied profile. Design acknowledgement This project was inspired by the folding arrangement of the Foldable Color Swatch . The concept and visual relationship are acknowledged intentionally. This version was rebuilt as a new parametric model and substantially extended with larger swatches, optional embedded NFC stickers, a print-in-place parametric folder, adjustable dimensions and tolerances, an optional retention pattern, and dedicated single- and four-swatch printing workflows.

Add a belt loop : Leatherman Holster Tired of your Leatherman Signal rattling around loose at the bottom of a bag or pocket? This holster keeps it in place, protects the blade, and mounts wherever you want with a single screw. It replaces the original nylon sheath with a bi-material printed part: a rigid shell for structure and protection, and a soft zone that cushions and grips the tool without scratching it. 🧩 The part 🛡️ PETG shell — rigid, heat- and impact-resistant. 🩹 TPU 95A zone — soft, cushions and adds grip. 🔗 No-glue bond — both materials printed together, joined by beam interlocking . 💡 Why this part? The point of bi-material is having PETG's stiffness and TPU's flexibility in the same part, with no screws or glue between them. A small boss on the top guide presses against the tool to lightly lock it in place — enough that it won't drop out, not so much that you fight to remove it. And since it mounts on a single screwed point, plenty of uses are possible — your call depending on your needs. 🖨️ What is "beam interlocking"? It's a Bambu Studio slicer feature, not a magic property of the model: instead of just stacking PETG and TPU (which bond poorly), the slicer interlaces the two materials with tiny cross "beams" at the interface — a strong mechanical bond without glue . I printed this on a Bambu Lab H2D , using its dual head to lay down both materials in a single pass. 🛒 What you need 🖨️ A bi-material printer (ideally dual-head like the H2D) 🧵 PETG for the shell 🧵 TPU 95A for the soft zone 🔩 1× M5 screw + 1× M5 nut for mounting 📁 Files included .stl — the holster to print .3mf — the ready-to-print Bambu Studio project (bi-material / beam interlocking) ⚙️ Print settings Shell: PETG, standard PETG settings. Soft zone: TPU 95A, reduced speed recommended. Bi-material: enable beam interlocking at the PETG/TPU interface. 🧱 Material change via a modifier: the second material is assigned through a modifier in Bambu Studio (add the modifier, then set the second filament on that region). Do not change the height of the modifier — it defines exactly where the material split happens. 🖨️ No dual-head printer? You can still print it as a single material : PETG (for water resistance) or TPU . ⚠️ I haven't tested single-material prints myself — so consider them experimental until someone confirms. ✅ Compatibility Tested by me: Leatherman Signal — printed and physically fitted on my own tool. ⚠️ Not tested: any other Leatherman model. description: I needed a compact pill splitter with built-in storage for spare tablets. I didn't have any extra Bambu Lab scraper blades, which ruled out most pill splitter designs available on MakerWorld. The few designs that relied on a printed plastic blade didn't work for me either. My medication is very fragile, and every attempt to split it using a "printed blade" ended up crushing the tablet instead of cutting it. However, I still had a few spare Bambu Lab filament cutter blades that came with my P1S , so I decided it was time to design my own solution. The model is best printed in two colors, although you can also add a third color for the symbol on the top half. I wanted to be able to safely carry the container while traveling without the risk of accidentally touching the blade, so I designed the enclosure with built-in magnets. You'll need four 5 × 2 mm magnets , or alternatively eight 5 × 1 mm magnets . The enclosure also includes a separate storage compartment where you can keep whole tablets before splitting them in the cutting chamber. Joining the two halves of the enclosure may require a little force, but versions with larger clearances became too loose during use, so I intentionally chose a slightly tighter hinge. The tolerances were tested using Bambu Lab filaments. Assembling To install the blade, carefully hold the metal end between two fingers and insert the plastic part into the slot in the lid at an angle. Then use flat pliers to gently push the blade into its final position. Tip: You don't have to insert the blade all the way to the end of the slot. The slot is intentionally longer so you can adjust where the blade contacts the tablet. For smaller tablets (≤ 10 mm), the blade can remain fully inserted. For larger tablets (> 10 mm), moving the blade slightly backward allows it to strike closer to the center of the tablet. I recommend trying a few different positions to find the one that works best for your medication. Parts Bambu Lab filament cutter blade 4 × 5 × 2 mm magnets (or 8 × 5 × 1 mm magnets)

description: Lubricating oil needs to be added to the rotating parts The prototype of this model is a work by (YY the length). I believe there are some irrational aspects in the prototype. Therefore, I conducted a redesign, and all the new designs are aimed at making printing and usage more convenient. This is not a simple replica, but an optimized parallel version. The following is a description of version differences: *Bearing-free design The bearing-free design is not simply about removing bearings. It requires ingenious design to achieve smooth rotation without bearings. The original version must use specific bearings. *Completely unsupported Completely unsupported is not simply a matter of changing the position of the model, but rather a redesign of the structure. The original version uses a lot of support. *The main structure is integrally printed and molded To reduce assembly difficulty and achieve an integrated main structure, various details need to be considered, necessitating a redesign of the structure. The original parts cannot be printed as a single unit, but are all separate, making assembly challenging. *The shell is intact, with the elastic band concealed A complete spherical shape also requires precise design, and it cannot be achieved simply by making some changes. The rubber band is hidden inside, making the shell more intact. The original version has its internal structure exposed. * Add angle limit to the interior of the rotating shaft A limit stop is incorporated inside the rotating shaft to maintain a consistent angle when pressed. The original version has no limit on the rotation axis, and it rotates randomly when pressed. *Gear cover with concealed buckle locking The gear cover features a concealed buckle design, which locks with a single press. The original version is complex to install, requiring materials to be inserted and fixed. Due to printing tolerances, it is sometimes difficult to insert them. * The innovative addition of a ring buckle allows for more playful ways to use it, and it can even be rotated without the need for a rubber band (completely without any additional accessories) The original version does not have this function *Introducing a smaller version with a diameter of 5cm. The 5cm size is not just a simple reduction; all details have been adjusted to ensure smooth operation. The original version does not have a small-sized version, nor can it be printed in a smaller size.

description: Think you've got diver's lungs? Prove it — or prank someone who thinks they do. The Diver's Lung Tester looks like a simple blow-challenge toy: put your lips on the mouthpiece, blow, and try to spin the internal wheel as fast as you can. Turn it into a challenge: "Bet you can't spin it faster than me!" Hand it over. Most people instinctively blow straight into the main hole without plugging anything — and get a face full of flour instead of a spinning wheel. description: This planetary gear fidget spinner is a super satisfying toy that spins for a surprisingly long time. At the center is a sun gear surrounded by four planet gears , all meshing together inside an outer ring gear . Hold the center grip steady and spin the outer ring , and all four planets spin right along with it, letting you watch the whole gear train turn as one . Every gear was meticulously prototyped , dialing in the perfect clearances so that every gear meshes perfectly with the rest. To prevent the pieces from coming apart , I designed a custom rail system to each gear that keeps the assembly locked in place . Since this fidget is entirely print-in-place , everything comes off the build plate already assembled , with zero assembly or supports needed. The outer ring is finished with a beautiful knurled texture broken up by smoother cutouts , giving it a bold mechanical look and a solid grip no matter how you spin it. Taking just 79 minutes and 23.13 grams of filament to print, this planetary fidget spinner is the perfect print for anyone who loves watching gears in motion and fidgeting with a good spinner . model_name: Clicky Bread – Yamagata Bread Fidget Toy
description: Clicky Bread – Yamagata Bread Fidget Toy A soft and fluffy-looking loaf with three little peaks! 🍞 Clicky Bread – Yamagata Bread is a cute fidget toy inspired by Yamagata shokupan , a Japanese-style bread loaf known for its rounded, mountain-shaped top. The three-peaked loaf sits inside a tiny square woven basket with a cloth liner, creating a warm and cozy bakery scene. Press the bread to activate the hidden MX-style mechanical keyboard switch and enjoy a satisfying click with springy feedback. It works as a relaxing little desk toy, a charming bakery-themed decoration, or a cute addition to your Clicky collection. This is the third model in the Anda Lab Clicky Bread series. Features Satisfying Clicky Action Press the Yamagata bread to enjoy a satisfying clicky fidget experience. The entire loaf moves as one piece, activating the mechanical switch hidden inside the basket. The rounded three-peak shape makes the bread fun to press while giving the model a clear and recognizable silhouette. Inspired by Yamagata Shokupan Yamagata shokupan is a Japanese-style loaf baked without a lid, allowing the dough to rise naturally above the bread pan and form a soft, rounded mountain-like top. This model turns that distinctive shape into a cute three-peaked Clicky Bread design. Its smooth curves and full upright shape give the model a warm, fluffy, and playful appearance. Tiny Square Woven Basket The Yamagata bread is paired with a small square woven basket that complements the shape of the loaf. The basket hides the internal mechanical switch while creating a cozy everyday bakery scene, as if the freshly baked bread has just been placed inside for serving. Separate Cloth Liner The cloth liner is a separate printable part and can be printed in a different color from the basket. It creates a soft visual layer between the bread and the basket while making it easy to experiment with different color combinations. Standard and Keychain Versions Included The download includes two versions: Standard Version – suitable as a desk fidget toy, decoration, or collectible. Keychain Version – includes a keychain attachment point so you can carry your Clicky Bread with you. Both versions use the same Yamagata bread and cloth liner parts. The main difference is the basket design. Please note that keychain hardware is not included in the printable files and must be prepared separately. Separate Parts for Easy Color Printing The model is divided into the following printable parts: Yamagata Bread Cloth Liner Standard Basket Keychain Basket Each part can be printed in a different color, so no additional painting is required. A multi-color printer is not necessary. The parts can be printed separately and assembled afterward. Additional Parts Required One compatible MX-style mechanical keyboard switch is required to create the clicky movement. For the keychain version, you will also need your own keychain ring or suitable keychain hardware. The mechanical switch and keychain hardware are not included with the printable model files. Assembly Install the mechanical keyboard switch into the basket. Place the cloth liner in the correct position. Connect the Yamagata bread to the switch. Press the bread several times to make sure it moves smoothly and returns properly. For the keychain version, attach your own keychain hardware to the connection point. Please refer to the assembly images on the model page for the correct part orientation and installation order. Printing Notes The Yamagata bread, cloth liner, and basket are separate parts and can be printed in different colors. Please use the provided print profiles for the recommended orientation and print settings. Before applying glue, if required for your chosen assembly method, check that all parts fit correctly and make sure the bread can move freely. Welcome Back to Clicky Bread This Yamagata Bread design expands the Clicky Bread series into the world of Japanese-style bread. The previous models introduced a French bread in a woven basket and a rustic country loaf in a proofing basket. This model adds a soft-looking, upright loaf with three rounded peaks and a square basket. Together, they continue the main idea behind Clicky Bread: Cute baked goods, warm bakery-themed scenes, and satisfying clicky interaction. I hope this tiny three-peaked loaf brings a little warmth and clicky fun to your desk. Happy printing! 🍞 Love this design? 👇Click the image below to explore more creations from the Clicky Series! Super Leggiero is the first aircraft in the Ultralight Series , designed around the principles of minimum weight, efficient aerodynamics, and slow, floaty flight . With its ultralow wing loading and optimized airframe, it delivers long, graceful glides in indoor environments and calm, no-wind conditions. The Ultralight Series also introduces an expert hybrid construction technique , where the frame of the plane is printed directly onto lightweight tissue paper. This reduces the flying weight from 9 g to just 5 g —a 45% weight reduction —resulting in even slower flight, lower sink rate, and exceptional indoor performance. While the standard version is designed for simplicity and easy assembly, the hybrid version offers experienced builders the opportunity to explore the limits of ultralight 3D printed aircraft. Finetune the pitch by adjusting the elevator control surfaces. If the glider pitches up or stalls: add more down elevator . If the glider dives: add more up elevator . TwistCore — 32-Piece Sliding Fidget Ball TwistCore is a print-in-place fidget made from 32 curved sections that move along a twisting internal guide. The mechanism is built to keep each section captured while allowing controlled movement around the rounded body. Design Story This project began as a challenge to create my own version of a sliding fidget from scratch. The first design used 20 sections. After receiving feedback asking for a higher piece count, I tested several new versions and adjusted the spacing, clearances, wall thickness, and internal rail. A 35-piece version was also tested, but the smaller sections did not hold onto the guide as reliably as I wanted. After more redesigning, 32 pieces gave the best balance of movement, strength, size, and printability. The final version uses a mostly concealed guide and catcher system so the outside stays clean while the mechanism remains secure. Features 32 moving sections Twisting sliding motion Internal guide and catcher system Print-in-place construction Designed for FDM printers No supports required Refined clearances to reduce fusing Rounded outer profile Printing Notes This model uses small moving gaps, so printer calibration is important. Avoid an overly compressed first layer, since excess elephant foot may join the sections together. Recommended Settings 0.16 mm layer height for the first print 0.12 mm layer height for finer surface detail Supports off Brim off Arachne wall generator recommended PLA or PLA+ recommended Check the sliced Preview to confirm that the moving gaps remain open TwistCore went through multiple prototypes, failed ideas, and geometry changes before reaching this version. It is the most complete and reliable design I have made from this concept so far.

description: D20 Spinner – The Wheel of Fate Spin your destiny! Required Parts 2x Bearings - 17mm x 23mm x 4mm - Amazon Link 12x Magnets - 5mm x 2.8mm - Amazon Link Assembly Instructions Install the Bearings Press-fit one bearing into each side of the wheel. Ensure both bearings are fully seated and spin freely. Install the Wheel Magnets Press-fit the 10 magnets into the wheel. Important: All magnets must be installed with the same polarity facing outward . Double-check the orientation before pressing each magnet into place. Install the Wall Magnets Press-fit the 2 magnets into the magnet wall. Orient them so they attract to the magnets in the wheel (not repel). Test the orientation with the wheel before fully seating the magnets. Assemble the Axle Slide the two axle pieces together until they are fully engaged. Install the Wheel Push the assembled axle through the bearings in the wheel. Add the Spacers Place one spacer onto each side of the axle between the wheel and the side walls. Attach the Side Walls Position the two side walls on either side of the wheel assembly, ensuring the magnet wall is on the correct side. Install the Assembly into the Base Press the completed assembly into the base until it is fully seated. Test the Spinner Give the wheel a spin. It should rotate smoothly on the bearings and snap cleanly into each of the 20 positions as the magnetic detents engage.

description: Un simpatico T-Rex puzzle 3D facile da montare, educativo e perfetto per stimolare creatività, logica e manualità nei bambini. Pensato per unire gioco, creatività e manualità in un modello semplice, accattivante e piacevole da assemblare. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il T-Rex si sostiene in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo sia un simpatico personaggio decorativo per camerette, scuole, asili o spazi gioco. Il design è pensato per essere adatto ai bambini: forme morbide, aspetto simpatico, sorriso inciso, dettagli scavati e dentini ricavati direttamente nel modello, senza necessità di parti aggiuntive o colori separati. Puoi realizzarlo tutto dello stesso colore, in versione bicolore oppure con più colori diversi per un effetto più allegro e creativo. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il T-Rex diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. A dimensioni standard, il modello è pensato per una stampa rapida , indicativamente in circa 2 ore , a seconda della stampante, del materiale, della velocità, dell’altezza layer e delle impostazioni utilizzate. Consigliato in PLA , anche con piatto texturizzato / PEI texturizzato , per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e dall’aspetto più professionale. La faccia anteriore del modello risulta particolarmente gradevole se stampata a contatto con il piatto texturizzato. TRI-OMINOS Bookcase Edition TRI-OMINOS Bookcase Edition is a 2-4 player strategy game from 1965 and is similar to Dominoes , in that players are laying tiles that match up to other tiles in the play area, with the goal to get 400 points. In TRI-OMINOS , the pieces are triangles with numbers that are matched on each side. Each triangle has 3 numbers at the points, so to place a piece next to it, it must match two numbers on the sides. This special edition TRI-OMINOS includes INTERLOCKING TILES so that during play, the tiles are not mistakenly moved. This edition also includes 4 WILD CARDS for faster play and 4 Score Counters . GAME COMPONENTS The TRI-OMINOS Bookcase Edition set includes: 56 interlocking TRI-OMINOS Tiles 4 Wild Card (star) Tiles 4 Score Counters 1 Bookcase Edition Box BOOKCASE EDITION BOX The TRI-OMINOS Bookcase Edition game also includes a Bookcase Edition Box with a slide top. This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the all the TRI-OMINOS tiles, and scoring counters. To store the scoring counters, place pairs of counters face to face then place flat in the box. The tiles are added to the box face up (number side up) so when you empty the box, the tiles will lay face down (TRI-OMINOS logo upwards), so that they may be easily shuffled on the table. INFORMATION & ASSEMBLY All parts were printed with PLA filament, matt or flat colored PLA filaments work best for bookcase edition games. I use a textured plate for adhesion. Some parts will need to be superglued, for example, the book spine is glued to the square cornered side of the bookcase box. A small drop of printer oil on the edges of the box lid will help with the slide into the box top. Score Counter Assembly 1. Print the all score counter parts (top, base and slides). Lightly sand any print inperfections if necessary. 2. Add 3 slides to each base. The slide arrows will point up. 3. Apply a light amount of superglue to the base making sure not to apply to the slides or inner edges. 4. Add the the counter top by aligning the tabs and press firmly till the glue sets. 5. Ensure slides move freely. IMPORTANT NOTE: I've turned off the prime tower in order to upload the model but turning it on (if it will fit on your plate) will help the quality of your prints. Assemble as indicated in the last image (which comes from the non-spiky version): I strongly recommend applying lubricant (grease, silicone oil etc) on the click mechanism before assembling it (see photo). Insert piston into tube; use optional assembly tool or a pen etc. to push it through, so it sticks out on the other side. Press button part onto piston part. Use some force and the parts join with a strong click (see image). Remove assembly tool. Insert spring and close with cap. The button might get stuck pressed down the first few times; just pull out and push again to break it in and make operation smother.

Whichever color faces up kicks next! Kicker: insert plunger shaft UP through the hole in the base BEFORE putting a coin in the pocket. Press the cap onto the shaft (tiny drop of superglue). Drop the nut into the hex pocket, push the bolt through from the other side, snug it — the leg should swing freely. Goal: glue base pads to the frame's rear face (pins align it). Slide the rod in FROM THE FRONT through the bearing (the collar stops it sliding back), then glue the handle on the rear end and the keeper on the front — the D-flat sets the orientation. Net hood slides over from behind; friction fit, glue optional. OPTIONAL ~26mm coin (2-Euro) in the base pocket as ballast — recommended for hard kicks, glue it in Spring version has a seat for a return spring. Without it the leg's weight returns the plunger as best as possible (button may rest a few mm low; printing the leg at 100% infill helps (already set up)). I didn't find a spring that fit well — mine were all too narrow or too stiff — so treat it as experimental.

description: Una dolce pecorella puzzle 3D facile da montare, educativa e perfetta per stimolare creatività, logica e manualità nei bambini. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo intuitivo. description: My own original design from scratch of a balisong (butterfly knife) trainer — no blade, no sharp edge, built purely as a fidget/flipper toy for practicing flips and tricks safely. This is a fully printed model. No metal blade, no cutting edge — just a smooth, satisfying flip.
