ROTA Board Game - Bookcase Edition ROTA Board Game ROTA (Radmühle, Terni Lapilli or Wheel Mill) is a 2-player ancient Roman and Greek strategy game. The authenticity of the game is uncertain and was found during excavations. ROTA is played on a wheel board with 9 spaces. Each player gets 3 coin tokens. The first person to align 3 tokens in a row (across the center or along the edge) wins. MILL Board Game The larger board is used to play the game MILL , where players take turns moving their 9 coin tokens to form a Mill (3 in a row), allowing them to capture opponent tokens. The game ends when a player is reduced to 2 tokens or is unable to move. “There she found the swaggering suitors, just then amusing themselves with boardgames before the doors, lounging on hides of oxen…” Translation from HOMER (Book 1 The Odyssey lines 106-108) 700BCE GAME COMPONENTS ROTA Board Game - Bookcase Edition set includes: 2 Level Board ( ROTA -Upper & MILL -Upper & Lower) 9 Black Coins 9 Silver Coins 1 Bookcase Edition Box BOOKCASE EDITION BOX The ROTA Board Game - Bookcase Edition game also includes a Bookcase Edition Box with a slide top. This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the ROTA board and coin tokens. The coin tokens are stored in the bottom of the box in a single layer and the ROTA board is stored above the tokens. INFORMATION & ASSEMBLY All parts were printed with PLA filament, matt or flat colored PLA filaments work best for bookcase edition games. I use a textured plate for adhesion. Some parts will need to be superglued, for example, the book spine is glued to the square cornered side of the bookcase box. A small drop of printer oil on the edges of the box lid will help with the slide into the box top. Antiquing the Coin Tokens The coin tokens were printed with matt PLA (black) and PLA (white or light gray). The black tokens were antiqued by applying a very small amount of gold color acrylic paint using a dry brush technique by lightly brushing the tops. The white or light gray tokens were antiqued by painting with a dark gray acrylic paint and immediately wiping the paint off leaving only a small amount in the crevices. IMPORTANT NOTE: I've turned off the prime tower in order to upload the model but turning it on (if it will fit on your plate) will help the quality of your prints. description: Turn your kid into an excavator. Slide your forearm into the sleeve, grab the roller bar inside the bucket, and dig - the bucket curls on real pivots just like the actual machine. Scoop, lift, dump, repeat. Works just as well in snow as in sand. Why you'll like printing this one: Zero supports, zero glue. Every part prints in its ideal orientation. Everything assembles with a coin or finger. All joints use chunky printed trapezoidal screws - two pivot bolts and one grip axle. Fully serviceable: any part that ever breaks can be reprinted and swapped. Bike-pedal grip. The bucket handle is a free-spinning roller on a fixed axle - comfortable for repeated scooping, and the axle cross-ties the bucket for stiffness. Sand-proof by design. Loose 0.6mm running clearances at every moving joint so grit won't seize it. If it gets crunchy, rinse and go. Parts list (one full toy): 1× sleeve, 1× bucket, 1× grip axle + 1× grip tube, 2× pivot barrels, 3× screws. Print settings: PETG strongly recommended (sun and rough play; PLA gets soft in a hot car). 0.20mm layers, 15% gyroid, 3 walls - use 4 walls on the barrels, screws, and axle if you want better strength. Assembly (about 2 minutes): Hold the grip tube between the bucket cheeks, slide the axle through - its square head seats into the side pocket - and snug a screw into it from the far pocket with a coin. Then set the bucket between the sleeve plates, push a barrel through each side from the outside, and screw a screw into each from inside the bucket. Snug until the head meets the barrel end, then back off 1/8 turn so the bucket swings freely. Optional velcro strap through the floor slots keeps it on smaller arms. Sizing: Default fits smaller adults all the way down to little kids (88 × 78mm forearm opening). Safety: Adult assembly recommended. Not for children under 3 - contains small parts (screws). Check screws for snugness now and then; a tiny dab of glue on the threads makes them permanent.

description: I wanted to create a fidget toy that was just as enjoyable for younger children as it was for adults. One thing I noticed with a lot of gyro-style fidgets is that there's very little to actually hold onto. Younger children often end up grabbing the moving rings, stopping them from spinning altogether. With that in mind, I designed this with three large outer grip areas, giving little hands somewhere comfortable to hold while leaving the moving hexagons completely free to rotate. The print tolerances have also been carefully tuned. My own kids actually had just as much fun blowing on the hexagons and watching them spin as they did flicking them by hand! As an added bonus for those with a commercial licence who sell at craft fairs and markets, I've included a simple display stand. It makes the fidget look much more professional on a stall, keeps it upright for customers to interact with and also makes a great display piece at home. An unexpected bonus I discovered is that the closed version doubles as a surprisingly practical coaster. At first glance it looks like a stylish geometric coaster, but as soon as you pick it up the hexagon rings spring to life and spin freely before settling flat again when you put it back down. It's a fun little talking point for any maker's desk. Everything prints in place with no assembly required, so once the print has finished, simply start spinning. description: “雷电五传的秘密、鸣神大社的怪谈...呵呵，你想先听哪一个？” 大家好！今天给大家带来新建模的——《原神》鸣神大社宫司大人：八重神子（Yae Miko）高精度3D打印模型！ 模型以 米哈游官方经典手办 为参考进行重新建模与雕刻。无论你是打算打印白模摆件，还是进行高精度的涂装上色，这套模型都能满足你的需求！ ⚙️ 配置文件与打印说明（非常重要！请按需打印） 为了兼顾不同机型的打印能力和玩家的后期涂装需求，我精心准备并上传了 两个不同的配置文件 ，请大家根据自己的设备情况选择对应配置： 🟢 版本一：【拆件版本】（推荐全部机型使用） 适用机型： A1, P1P, P1S, P2S,X1C 等所有单头/多头打印机，及光固化打印机。 配置特点： 模型已进行 科学合理的拆分与打孔/插槽设计 ，大幅减少了悬垂部分的支撑需求。 拆件打印不仅成功率极高，而且完美避开了关键细节（如面部、手指）的支撑缺陷。 强烈推荐给有涂装上色需求、或使用基础单耗材打印的玩家！ 分件涂装会轻松很多！ 🔴 版本二：【未拆件 / 一体化版本】（高难度 · 仅限特定多头机型） 推荐机型： 搭载多喷头系统的旗舰机型（如 X2D、H2C 等）。 配置特点： 保留了模型整体的高姿态与完整性，无需后期拼接。 ⚠️ 避坑警告： 由于一体模型结构极其复杂，凌空的飘带、发丝和地台存在大量极端悬垂与死角， 强烈不推荐使用普通单头打印机搭配同质材料支撑打印！ 否则拆除支撑时极易断裂、毁坏细节，且支撑面极其粗糙。 正确打开方式： 仅建议使用 X2D、H2C 等多头打印机，开启「异料支撑（如 PLA + PETG 互为支撑接口，或使用专用支撑材 Support W/G）」 进行打印。利用异料零距离支撑的特性，才能在一体打印的同时保证完美的接触面和轻松的拆除体验。 💡 打印与后期建议 层高建议： 建议使用 0.08mm 或 0.12mm 层高（推荐开启可变层高 Adaptive Layer Height），以最大程度保留面部细节和飘带的平滑度。 耗材推荐： 强烈推荐使用 拓竹 PLA Basic 哑光白/骨白 或 PLA Grey 灰色 作为基础白模材料，细节显现度最好，也最容易观察涂装瑕疵。 组装提示： 拆件版在拼接时，建议先假组确认公差，部分接口可使用少量 401/502 瞬间胶辅助固定。 上色参考： 为大家提供官方手办样式用于上色参考⬇️ 🎉 喜欢这个作品的话，请务必给我一个点赞、收藏或助力（Boost）！ 你们的支持是我持续创作和开源更多模型的动力！非常期待在评论区看到大家的 返图和涂装神作 ！有问题随时留言，我会第一时间回复解答~

description: Un simpatico camaleonte puzzle 3D facile da montare, educativo e perfetto per stimolare creatività, logica e manualità nei bambini. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il camaleonte si sostiene correttamente in piedi, appoggiando bene sulle due zampe, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo sia un simpatico elemento decorativo per camerette, scuole, asili o spazi gioco. Il design è pensato per essere riconoscibile e adatto ai bambini: corpo tondeggiante, coda arrotolata, espressione simpatica, occhio inciso/scavato nello stesso colore del modello e dettagli puliti che funzionano bene anche in stampa monocolore. Ogni singolo pezzo può essere stampato con qualsiasi colore a scelta, permettendo di creare combinazioni personalizzate e rendere ogni camaleonte unico. Puoi realizzarlo tutto verde, in versione monocolore, bicolore oppure con più colori diversi per un effetto ancora più creativo. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il camaleonte diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. Consigliato in PLA , anche con piatto PEI texturizzato , per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e dall’aspetto più professionale. La faccia anteriore del modello è pensata per essere stampata a contatto con il piatto texturizzato, così da ottenere una superficie frontale elegante e uniforme. This is a fully 3D-printable 2x2 FTO (Face-Turning Octahedron) twisty puzzle. You do not need an AMS or any additional hardware (like screws or springs) for printing and assembly. Mechanically, it can be described as a Skewb with moving tips attached to the centers. You can choose between three versions: monocolor, stickerless, or tiled . For each version, you can also choose if you want a standard puzzle or a keychain variant with a hole (designed for a 25mm diameter keyring). This puzzle was designed for the BONBON Capsules Design Contest hosted by @Pipin.World - 皮皮世界 . The standard FTO was added as an official WCA (World Cube Association) event this year (2026). This 2x2 version is a simpler, more approachable variant. Just as the 2x2 Rubik's Cube is a simplified version of the standard 3x3, this 2x2 FTO is the simpler counterpart to the standard FTO. Print Settings: ( Using the provided print profile is recommended ) Material: PLA is recomended (for caps you can also use PETG) Layer Height: 0.12mm Infill: 15% (Gyroid) Supports: NO (for stickerless version), YES (for monocolor [ center_fixed ] and tiled version [ center_fixed , center_movable ]) Brim: Recommended for small parts (center_bonds, core_bonds, tip_bonds) Wall Loops (Perimeters): 3 for the small parts (center_bonds, core_bonds, tip_bonds) Performance Notes: The puzzle turns smoothly. While it may feel a little loose, it does not pop. Assembly & Post-Processing Tips: Brims and supports: Clean the parts thoroughly after 3D printing. Make sure no leftover brim or support material is sticking out, as this can negatively affect the movement of the puzzle. Lubrication: For smoother turning, you can apply lubricant to the internal mechanism (this step is optional). Assembly instructions: Step 1: Insert the smaller end of the tip_bond into the edge . Step 2: Place a tip on top of the inserted tip_bond . Repeat Steps 1 and 2 six times Step 3: Pass the smaller end of the center_bond through the center_fixed . Repeat this step four times. Step 4: Slide the center_bond (attached to the center ) into the core . Step 5: Slide the second center_bond (attached to the center ) into the core. Step 6: Secure the core using a core_plug . Repeat Steps 4 through 6 two times. Step 7: Insert the core_bond into the core containing the centers and the other core_bond . Step 8: Attach the second core (with its centers and core_bond ) onto the first core_bond , rotating it by 90°. Step 9: Slide three edges into the assembled skeleton, ensuring the longest inner shaft is touching the centers_fixed . Step 10: Slide the three centers_movable between the inserted edges . Step 11: Slide another two edges between the centers_fixed , again ensuring the longer inner shaft is touching the centers_fixed . Step 12: Insert the center_movable between the two previously inserted edges . Step 13: Click the last edge into the remaining free spot, making sure the longer inner shaft is touching the centers_fixed . Step 14: Click the center_cover onto the centers_fixed . Repeat this four times. (If you are building a colored version, make sure to insert them according to the correct color scheme.) Step 15: Apply stickers or colored tiles to the assembled puzzle, making sure you are following the correct color scheme. Disassembly: Turn the puzzle so that two edges with tips are next to each other. Gently pull one edge (along with its tip) away from the second one and slightly upwards. You can use this method when you want to swap a standard edge and tip for an edge and tip with a hole. After inserting the new edge, press the centers together to prevent popping. #Contests #Hostedbycreator #Bonbon

FlexaTerrestrial - Veyerus Springy Fidget (no AMS) The Veyerus is an organic springy fidget from the FlexaTerrestrial Series . KineticSpecies#001 combines springy tentacles , free‑spinning eyeballs , a rotating dual‑body core , and an optional magnetic click‑twist system . Everything is snap‑fit , press‑fit , and fully No AMS — optimized for fast PLA printing and strong tactile feedback. ❤️ Personal Note This design started with a spark a few months ago: I stumbled upon a joystick fidget that interpreted a gear‑shift pattern — and it instantly hooked me. Later, I discovered a virus‑style fidget and was fascinated by its organic playfulness. I didn’t want to create a simple copy, but something new — a completely different, never‑seen‑before play layer. That’s where the idea of free‑spinning eyes was born. While modeling, another idea hit me: rotating body halves . And in the very last moment, I added the magnetic click points . First print — and it was an instant hit (at least for me and my friends). 📦 Included Parts (for one complete Veyerus unit) 2× Body halves (rotating) 12× Tentacles 12× Eyeballs 12× Pupils 1× Rotation pin Magnet slots for 6×2 mm magnets are built into the model (Installing magnets is optional. If you need different magnet sizes, I’m happy to provide alternate versions.) 🔧 Assembly Instructions 1. Insert Pupils into Eyeballs Place the pupil onto the eyeball opening. Press the eyeball down onto a hard surface. Requires force — this is a true press‑fit . After insertion, the pupil sticks out roughly 1-2mm. 2. Insert Eyeballs into Tentacles Push the eyeball into the tentacle socket. Also requires force. Once inserted, the eyeball spins freely inside the tentacle. 3. Optional: Install Magnets (6×2 mm) Press magnets into the slots of both body halves. Requires force; optionally add a drop of glue. Check polarity before inserting. You may fill only three magnet holes per side : → This creates changing engagement levels (1, 2, or 3 magnets) for a dynamic click‑feel. 4. Insert Tentacles into the Body Push each tentacle into its body socket. Requires force. Optional: add a drop of glue for permanent fixation. 5. Insert the Rotation Pin Press the rotation pin into one body half. 6. Attach the Second Body Half Press the second body half onto the rotation pin. The two halves rotate smoothly. With magnets: they click into magnetic positions. Without magnets: free, smooth rotation. Happy printing!

description: Un coloratissimo pappagallo puzzle 3D facile da montare, educativo e perfetto per stimolare creatività, logica e manualità nei bambini. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo semplice e intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il pappagallo si sostiene in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo sia un simpatico elemento decorativo per camerette, scuole, asili o spazi gioco. Il design è pensato per essere adatto ai bambini: forme morbide, becco simpatico, ali incise, coda allungata, due zampe stabili e dettagli del viso integrati nel modello. Funziona bene sia in versione monocolore sia in versione multicolore. Sono disponibili due profili di stampa: Profilo monocolore Pensato per chi vuole una stampa semplice, veloce e pulita. Il pappagallo può essere stampato tutto in un solo colore, con un tempo indicativo di circa 1 ora , a seconda della stampante, del materiale, della velocità, dell’altezza layer e delle impostazioni utilizzate. Profilo multicolore, anche senza AMS Pensato per chi vuole ottenere un effetto più vivace e accattivante. Ogni pezzo può essere stampato con un colore diverso anche senza AMS, semplicemente cambiando colore tra i vari pezzi o stampandoli separatamente. Il tempo di stampa indicativo è inferiore a 2 ore , a seconda delle impostazioni utilizzate. Ogni singolo pezzo può essere stampato con qualsiasi colore a scelta, permettendo di creare combinazioni personalizzate e rendere ogni pappagallo unico. Puoi realizzarlo in colori realistici, in stile arcobaleno oppure con tonalità pastello più delicate. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il pappagallo diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. Consigliato in PLA , anche con piatto PEI texturizzato , per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e dall’aspetto più professionale. La faccia anteriore del modello è pensata per essere stampata a contatto con il piatto texturizzato, così da ottenere una superficie frontale elegante e uniforme. Prima di consegnare il puzzle a un bambino, verificare che la stampa sia resistente, liscia e priva di bordi taglienti o piccole parti fragili.

The Orbital Gear Fidget combines gears and linkage mechanisms to create a unique and satisfying motion. As you rotate the handle, the outer gears orbit around the centre while remaining perfectly synchronized , producing a smooth mechanical movement that's just as enjoyable to watch as it is to use. Before Printing Please clean the build plate. If you are using the STL files, you need to print: 2 small rods 5 C-clips Everything else only needs to be printed once. Assembly In this video I show you how to assemble it (video coming soon). Insert the small wheel into the large wheel from the bottom, as shown in the images below. Insert the handle. The pin has a square profile, so make sure it is correctly aligned before pushing it into place. Insert both small rods as shown below. Use 2 C-clips to hold the rods in place. Insert the large rod. It should pass through the handle and both pins, as shown below. Use the remaining 3 C-clips to secure the large rod. Your fidget is now complete! Troubleshooting If the mechanism doesn't feel smooth, gears may be a few teeth out of alignment. Try repositioning it so that both sides are as evenly spaced as possible. This should greatly improve the smoothness of the mechanism. If you have any problems or suggestions, feel free to leave a comment. Happy Printing!

Hallo! Ich bin deine neue Seilwinde! Ja, genau ich . Ich sehe vielleicht harmlos aus, aber unterschätze mich nicht – ich bin die neue Beförderungsabteilung für jedes Baumhaus, jeden Spielturm und jedes geheime Hauptquartier. Du hast keine Lust mehr, ständig Kuscheltiere, Spielzeug oder den Proviant nach oben zu werfen? Keine Sorge, ich übernehme das! Je nach Drucker und Filament können meine Toleranzen leicht variieren. Sollte ich an einer Stelle etwas locker sein, freue ich mich über einen kleinen Tropfen Kleber. Danach sitze ich wieder geschniegelt und gebügelt. Noch etwas Wichtiges... Ich bin für Kinderspielzeug gemacht – also für Kuscheltiere, Spielzeugautos, geheime Schätze oder den obligatorischen Snacktransport ins Baumhaus. Bitte nicht versuchen, Erwachsene, Fahrräder, Waschmaschinen oder den Familienhund mit mir hochzuziehen. Ich bin gut... aber nicht so gut. Also... worauf wartest du noch? description: Custom Keyboard Clicker Fidgets Create personalized keyboard clicker fidgets using names, words, numbers, icons, or your own custom SVG designs. The files include 2-Slot, 4-Slot, 6-Slot, and 3x3 clicker layouts. Choose from the included A-Z letters, 0-9 numbers, controller, star, and heart keycaps, or use the blank keycap to create your own design. The multicolor keycaps are designed to print face down with an AMS, giving the letters and icons a clean first-layer finish. Switches Each clicker requires Cherry MX-style mechanical keyboard switches. 2-Slot clicker: 2 switches 4-Slot clicker: 4 switches 6-Slot clicker: 6 switches 3x3 clicker: 9 switches My recommended switches are Outemu Gold, Purple, and Red. You can use one switch type for the entire clicker or mix different switches in the same clicker. Keychain Option All versions include an optional keychain attachment hole. To print a version without the hole, delete the generic torus negative part from the model before slicing. I recommend using a lobster claw keychain for better durability and easy removal. Switches and keychain hardware are not included with the printed parts. Parts I Used Keyboard switches: https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005004285423123.html Lobster claw keychains: https://www.amazon.ca/dp/B07SW2HH7L Assembly Print your chosen clicker body and keycaps. Press the Cherry MX-style switches into the body. Press the keycaps onto the switch stems. Attach the optional keychain hardware. How to Add a Custom SVG Image Add the blank keycap to the build plate. Right-click the blank keycap. Select Add Modifier , then select SVG . Find and open the SVG file on your computer. Set the SVG depth to 0.40 mm . Resize the SVG to fit the keycap. Most designs work well between 10 mm and 13 mm , depending on the shape. Position the SVG in the center of the keycap. Make sure the operation is set to Modifier . It will not work correctly if it is set to Join or Cut. Assign the SVG modifier to your desired filament color. Slice the plate and check the preview to make sure the design appears correctly on the first layer. Intro: Hello Makers! Here's a new 4-wing boomerang toy based on my previous Fuma Shuriken from Naruto. It is print-in-place, prints in 1 hour, and works right off the plate. I included a Kids version and an adult version . The kids version is lighter and easier to get a return , while the adult version is a bit heavier, and glides more in the air . Make sure to watch a boomerang-throwing tutorial before using this toy ! It takes a bit of practice, but when you get it, it feels like magic. Also, make sure you print the right-hand model if you're right-handed and vice versa. Lastly, if you can, print in a strong material like PLA tough or PETG for impact resistance. How to Throw: (Reverse directions for left-handed people.) First, hold the boomerang in front of you and tilt it to the right slightly. Curl your wrist back while throwing the boomerang to your right at around a 40-degree angle upwards. Also, you will likely have to step into your throw for extra power, but make sure not to throw too hard. If it's windy, make sure to throw just right of the direction that the wind is blowing. Refer below for troubleshooting. Quick Troubleshooting: Issue 1# If your boomerang is going up, then coming straight down, you are likely throwing with too much of an angle and/or too hard . Refer to a tutorial for the correct angle. Issue 2# If your boomerang is stopping in front of you, try throwing with more force . This should give you the extra returning distance you need. Issue 3# If your boomerang starts returning, then flips and goes forward, try a lower launch angle and/or less power . Around a 40/45 degree angle is good. Refer to the GIFs of me throwing above for a better idea of how to use the boomerang. Outro: Have fun and leave a rating/boost if you liked it!

However, if you're experienced and comfortable with it, PETG is the superior choice for durability and impact resistance. I do not recommend PLA for the gear asssembly (especially the stem/shaft) as it tends to be too stiff and brittle to handle the repeated torque. Be aware, this is a large print. Expect to use around 2.2-2.5 kg of filament over a total of around 3 days of printing. Choose: EITHER Standard Bin: Plate 1: Standard Cap Plate 2: Standard Bin Plate 3: Standard Upper Base OR Big Bin: Plate 5: Big Cap Plate 6: Big Bin Plate 7: Big Upper Base Base Plate 4: Mid Base Plate 8: Carousel (and spacers) Plate 9: Lower Base This is the only one that requires supports. They are pre-painted for you, but you can tweak them if you like (e.g., use a special support material for transition) Plate 10: Bottom This is pre-colored for multi-color printing. The bottom and the ball chute are integrated into a single component. I do NOT recommend printing them separately as this is also the main structural component of the print. The chute ends up somewhat hidden, so if you need to, a single color is probably fine. Final Bits Plate 11: Misc (Crank and Top Nut) This, too, is multi-color, as each number on the clock is intended to have a color distinct from the base. Likewise the handle has a colored arrow on top. I've also included blank versions of these as separate files if you want to print them blank or design your own. Plate 12: Gears As noted, these probably should be printed in PETG or PA or similar tough and slick material. Assembly Insert threaded rod into printed Bottom. The metal rod just screws into the hole in the middle of the chute. This should bottom out at the correct height. Don't overtighten (it's metal on plastic afterall), though if you need extra leverage, you can use two nuts as jam nuts (put both on the end of the rod and hand tighten them together--then tighten the rod by using a wrench to turn the top nut clockwise and loosen by turning the bottom nut counter clockwise). Assemble the gear mechanism. These should all be pretty tight, so use a small hammer or mallet if needed. Add bearings to the slots on both sides of the gear “Case” Place one side of the case on a table with the “fingers" pointing up and insert the gear into the hole in the middle of the bearing. Insert the gear stem into the corresponding hole in the gear. The “short” side goes into the gear and it should seat fully with the raised shoulder. Slide the other half of the gear case onto the gear stem and slide to engage and fully seat the fingers as shown in the figure on the right. Insert gear case into lower case. Slide gear case through the bottom so that the stem extends through the crank hole. Slide the gear lock panel into the lower case to secure the gear case in place as shown in the figure on the right. Attach printed bottom and lower base. The lower base should slide easily over the chute on the bottom, with the lower base's gate being aligned with the bottom's chute exit. Fully seat the lower base into the associated slots on the bottom; it should be a snug friction fit. Add crank face and handle. Slide printed face onto the gear stem. This may be a tight fit so use a little force if needed, but be careful not to bend or break the stem. Fully seat the face onto the lower base; it will pass through the gear stem hole in the lower base and align vertically using two alignment nibs. Slide the crank handle onto the end of the gear stem. Secure the handle by screwing an m3 x 5mm (up to 8mm) screw into the side of the handle. It will self-tap threads into the hole in the stem. Turn the handle and ensure that the gear turns easily and smoothly. Attach mid base (carousel housing) to lower base. Slide the printed mid base onto the threaded rod. This will be snug, but the rod should “sand” the opening enough to slide down easily from the top. Align the gear slot with the gear and fully seat the mid base into the appropriate slots in the lower base. Attach and align the carousel. First insert a bearing into the cutout in the middle of the bottom of the carousel. Slide the carousel onto the threaded rod; the rod will go through the middle of the bearing. Slide the smaller “inner” carousel bearing spacer onto the threaded rod and down into the cavity in the middle of the carousel. Slide the final bearing onto the threaded rod and seat it fully into the cutout at the top of the carousel. At this point you will be able to lift and lower the carousel assembly onto the gear teeth. While holding the crank handle with the arrow facing up, align the carousel such that the ratchet flaps (pawls) are in the middle of one of the areas empty of any ratchet teeth. The crank should be able to spin freely from 11 to 1 before engaging with any of the ratchet teeth. This is how you know your carousel is properly aligned. Add the final two carousel bearing spacers to the threaded rod so that the “bulb” is at the top near the end of the threaded rod. Attach the upper base so that the hole cover is at the front-left of the machine, covering the chute entrance. Add the bin, aligning the tabs as required to seat the bin in the slots in the upper base and the part of the bin without holes is at the rear. Add the cap. Assemble and secure the top nut. Insert a single M8 hex nut into the slot in the top nut. Slide the top nut insert into the slot to lock the hex nut into place. Screw the top nut into place to secure the cap. Enjoy!! model_name: Noodle Nexus 2: Modular AMS Stacker Drawer
description: Introduction Another one? Yes. Clear up some desk space by stacking your AMS's! This version uses 45mm steel slides to slide out the lower AMS, making a super compact stacker. This is compatible with the original AMS and the AMS 2 Pro. The top AMS is positioned forward to ensure that the lid can open fully. Even so, with 350mm slide travel, the AMS lid will open enough to stay open without falling closed. The dimensions are: Height including an AMS 2 Pro on top: 475 mm Width: 443 mm Depth excluding handle and optional counterweight basket: 355 mm Handle adds 32mm of depth Counterweight basket adds 45mm of depth If this isn't exactly for you, check out this collection for alternatives. Modules Feet extensions to put this on top of your H-series printer 3rd/4th AMS Extension (link coming very soon!) Upcoming: AMS HT adapter Upcoming: Various Storage attachments, perhaps a tool drawer? Difficulty This project is designed for beginners . It is easy because: All parts print with minimal supports and all overhangs are easy to print. There is minimal post-processing required. There is only one type (and length!) of fastener needed with no heat-set inserts, no glue and no other specialty fasteners. You don't need "advanced" materials such as ABS. The challenging aspects are: Large parts, even PLA and PETG parts, can warp and your build plates need to be clean. You may even consider using some glue if you have had issues with your particular material and plate. You need to be able to print TPU, and to do this cleanly, you will need a filament dryer. Filament I recommend: PETG for the frame PETG or PLA for the drawer (if you plan on putting this on top of a printer though, do not use PLA) TPU 90A or similar for the feet If you use ABS or ASA, you must consider shrinkage compensation as the parts are large and the overall dimension can be affected by 2-3mm. Please feel free to post your print profile. Add lots of pictures and a detailed description please! It will help other people decide which one to use. Hardware for Assembly Only one type and length of screw is needed: BT3x14 BHCS Self Tapping Screw (AA223). This is a 3mm diameter, 14mm long screw designed for plastic with coarse deep threads that cut into and grip well onto holes in plastic. They are not expensive extremely easy to use as you don't need to embed heat set inserts or seat little M3 nuts. They also make the printed parts simpler and use far less material than using printed fasteners or bowtie joints. Alternatives: If you have 12mm screws or the socket head style of BT3 screws, they will be perfectly fine too. If Bambu doesn't ship to your country, the key words to search are “3mm self-tapping screw hex socket”. Try to get some without a pointy tip as they have a slightly longer usable thread length and a head height of 2mm or less. I found some products on AliExpress ( Listing 1 , Listing 2 , Listing 3 ) which look promising, but I have not tried them. Do NOT use countersunk screws as most holes in the design are parallel to the print bed plane and the screws can split your layers if you're not careful with tightening. You will need: 43 for the frame assembly 10 for the drawer assembly 16 to attach the steel slides to the frame and drawer assemblies 8 to attach the AMS's Optional: 4 to attach the counterweight basket 81 screws total (if I counted correctly…). If you ever wanted an excuse to buy an electric pencil screwdriver, here it is! In the bill of materials, I have put 5 packets of 20 screws but I suggest ordering extra if you are interested in making the future modules. You will also need 350mm or 14-inch nominal length, 45mm nominal width (can be a little wider as there is nothing below the slides), 12.7mm thick full extension slides. Here in Germany, I got Stahlia branded slides direct from their website , also available on Amazon.de . You do not need to get exactly the same one. I took specs from several different brands and accommodated for them all in the design and you just need 3-4 holes that line up. Worst case, you might need to make some new holes but I think that's unlikely as slide manufacturers just copy each other. IMPORTANT : If you are using soft-close slides, check that they are truly full extension and extend 400mm. Many 3-section slides that are labelled “full extension” are not really full extension, particularly some of the soft-close ones. Slide designers, when taking their regular slide and making a soft-close version, need to decide whether to reduce the load rating of their slide or reduce the extension to try to fit the extra mechanisms into the design. Some brands have lowered weight ratings (say, 35kg down from 45kg), some reduce their travel. Parts for Installation You will need a longer PTFE tube than typically supplied with printers (or a coupler to connect two shorter ones) as the AMS travels forward and back. The length needed depends on your particular setup. If the tube is brand new and tightly-wound for shipping, they will need to be relaxed to form gentle curves. Don't get the "star shaped" tubes, that's a gimmick. If you use a coupler, note that there is an entry side (tapered inlet) and an exit side (not tapered). You may also need longer 6-pin AMS connectors depending on your printer and AMS arrangement. Print Settings General Tips Flow rate calibration is highly recommended for every spool you use! Many clearances in the design are 0.1mm. For proper fit, the parts should not be under or over-extruded. Dry your filament (even PLA) to minimise risks with dimensional accuracy. Aux fan OFF if you've had issues with part warping. Don't worry, all of the overhangs are super easy. Specific Settings These are all set in the print profile. However, if you download it on PC and change the printer, some of these may get overwritten so I will list them here. These are the settings I use and are quite conservative and a little slow for a clean print with sharp corners, it's a balance between Bambu's “High Quality” and “Standard" profiles. Feel free to deviate as you see fit. Speeds Outer wall: 70 mm/s Inner wall: 150 mm/s Top Surface: 120 mm/s Everything else: default for your favourite profile Accelerations Normal printing: 4000 mm/s² Outer wall: 2000 mm/s² Inner wall: 0 (same as Normal) Top surface: 2000 mm/s² Sparse infill: 8000 mm/s² Everything else: default for your favourite profile Strength Parts are designed for a 0.4mm nozzle printing 0.2mm layer heights. Wall loops Top/bottom shell layers Infill Frame Parts 3 7/5 10-15%, your choice of pattern Slider Parts 3 7/5 10-15%, your choice of pattern TPU feet 6 5/3 Your choice All other parts 2 5/3 10-15%, your choice of pattern Bonus tip If you want the perfect 🧑🍳👌🏼fit between parts, make sure your beds are trammed! They're not always trammed out-of-factory; 3 of the printers I got in 2026 were not trammed. Manual Bed Leveling / Manual Bed Tramming | Bambu Lab Wiki P2S & X2D Heatbed Manual Bed Leveling | Bambu Lab Wiki Assembly and Installation As all screws are the same, this is quite straight forward. Just one thing to note: screws can get hot while tightening; tighten them most of the way and give them a minute before final tightening. Frame Assembly Assemble each half first. Use the screws to attach the 5 pieces of one side together. Insert the TPU feet - they are press-fit and should stay-in firmly without glue. Remove the inner part of the slide and attach to the frame using at least 3 screws. When tightening, push the slides up to the flat parts on the frame - this ensures that the left and right slides are parallel and level. Repeat for the other side and put the two halves together with more screws. Attach the top AMS with 4 screws. This will stiffen up the frame assembly considerably. For some versions of the original AMS, there are some small pieces of plastic that need to be trimmed. This is not necessary for the AMS 2 Pro and some original AMS variants. Drawer Assembly Assemble the drawer assembly with more screws. Attach the inner slides using at least 3 screws on each side. When tightening, try to get the two inner slides parallel. You can look at the unused holes to determine the positioning. If the holes are too big, you can use some washers (mine is OK without, this is just for illustration). Now slide this into the frame. Attach the lower AMS Put some filament inside the top AMS to provide some counterweight. Pull out the drawer and place the second AMS. Use 4 more screws to secure it in-place. And finally, post a picture here! Counterweight Options As you can guess, the whole assembly can tip forward when the drawer is opened fully. I have 3 options to reduce this risk. You can use one or more of the methods at the same time. Option 1 - Counterweight Basket Attach the counterweight basket using 4 screws (same screws as above!). The file for this is in a separate print profile, on this page. Fill an empty filament box with heavy stuff - try to get at least 2kg in there (a bag of sand, depleted uranium, a brick, whatever you have around the house). Put the box into the basket. You can make the box smaller too. Option 2 - Feet extensions These extensions extend the front by 95mm - if you have the table space these work great. Option 3 - Add another AMS Coming soon™! Support If you make one, please share a pic on social media! Facebook, Reddit, Twitter, whatever! It really helps me out. And of course: Changelog 25/06/2026 Original release

## Device Description Circle Bambu Monitor is a compact desktop display for monitoring Bambu Lab 3D printer status in real time. It is built around an ESP32-C3 SuperMini development board and a 1.28 inch round TFT display with a GC9A01 driver . The electronics are housed in a snap-fit 3D printed enclosure designed for a clean front view and easy rear access. The device connects to Wi-Fi and reads printer data from Home Assistant entities. It does not connect directly to the printer. Instead, it uses Home Assistant as the data source, which makes it flexible and easy to adapt to different Bambu Lab printer setups. ## Main Components - TENSTAR ESP32-C3 SuperMini development board - 1.28 inch round 240x240 TFT LCD display - GC9A01 display driver - 7-wire for display connection - 3D printed main body - 3D printed rear cover - USB-C power supply - Home Assistant with Bambu Lab integrations ## What It Does Circle Bambu Monitor shows the current status of a Bambu Lab printer on a small round display. It can display print progress, printer state, current print phase, temperatures, filament information, layer progress, print weight, estimated finish time, and a clock when the printer is idle. The device also includes a built-in web configuration interface. On first startup it creates its own Wi-Fi setup network. After connecting to it, the user can configure Wi-Fi, Home Assistant URL, access token, timezone, and the Home Assistant entities used for printer data. Firmware updates can be installed through the browser using the web installer, so users do not need to use the Arduino IDE. ## Data Source The device uses Home Assistant as its data source. It reads configured Home Assistant entities for: - Print phase - Print status - Print progress - Active filament slot - Estimated finish time - Nozzle temperature - Bed temperature - Current layer - Total layers - Filament weight ## Installation and Setup Guide Connect the display to the ESP32-C3 using the wiring diagram from the project documentation . The display uses SPI communication. Make sure all wires are connected correctly before powering the device. Open the web installer in a supported browser, such as Chrome or Edge. 1. Connect the ESP32-C3 to your computer using USB-C. 2. Click `Connect`. 3. Select the ESP32-C3 serial device. 4. Click `Install`. 5. Wait until flashing is complete. 6. Disconnect and reconnect the device if needed. After flashing, power on the device. If the device is not configured yet, it will start in setup mode and create its own Wi-Fi network. The display will show: - Wi-Fi network name - Setup password - Setup IP address Connect your phone or computer to the setup Wi-Fi network shown on the display. Then open the displayed IP address in your browser. In the web configuration page, enter: - Your Wi-Fi network - Wi-Fi password - Home Assistant URL (example http://192.168.1.100:8123) - Long-lived Home Assistant token After saving, the device will restart and connect to your Wi-Fi network. After restart, the device will no longer use the setup Wi-Fi network. Find the new IP address in your router, DHCP client list, or network device list. Open the device IP address in your browser to continue configuration. After the device connects to Home Assistant, the configuration page allows you to select the required entities. Configure entities for: - Print phase - Print status - Print progress - Active filament slot - Estimated finish time - Nozzle temperature - Bed temperature - Current layer - Total layers - Filament weight You can use the searchable entity fields to find matching Home Assistant entities. For example, typing “nozzle”, will show matching nozzle temperature entities. Entity names depend on your Home Assistant setup and integration. Configure Timezone - Select your timezone in the configuration page. This is used for Idle clock screen and estimated finish time display. Choose the timezone that matches your location.

model_name: BambuPlot Free Pen Plotter G-code Generator
description: Turn your Bambu Lab 3D printer into a pen plotter completely free, no subscriptions, no accounts, no uploads. Everything runs locally in your browser. The included test file uses the boat drawing shown in the preview image a detailed line-art illustration that works great as a first plot to verify your setup. When using the tool please consider using the included print profile test model. This helps me out and helps supporting this project with since i could not upload the Bambuplot file directly on Makerworld. ⚠ Read this first this is a tinkerer's project This tool is made for people who enjoy experimenting, troubleshooting, and figuring things out. It is not a plug-and-play product. It will probably not work perfectly on the first try , and that is completely normal. Getting a pen plotter working on a 3D printer requires patience: dialing in the Z height, finding the right pen, getting the paper flat, tuning the feed rates, and sometimes just accepting that the first few attempts are learning runs. I do not cover any damages to your printer, pen holder, bed, or any other part of your setup. Using this tool is entirely at your own risk. Sending custom G-code to a 3D printer always carries a risk of unexpected movement, crashes, or damage if settings are wrong. Always supervise the printer, always do a dry run first with the Z height raised so the pen cannot touch anything, and never leave it running unattended especially not on a first test. If you are not comfortable with that, this project is probably not for you yet but if you enjoy the process of making something work from scratch, welcome aboard. What is BambuPlot? BambuPlot is a single HTML file you download and open in your browser. It lets you design drawings and convert them into G-code that your Bambu Lab printer can execute with a pen instead of a nozzle. No internet connection is required after download — it runs 100% on your computer. Supported printers all current Bambu Lab models: Printer Bed size Notes A1 mini 180 × 180 mm A1 256 × 256 mm ✅ Tested P1P 256 × 256 mm P1S 256 × 256 mm P2S 256 × 256 mm X1 carbon 256 × 256 mm X2D 256 × 256 mm ✅ Tested A2L 330 × 320 mm H2D 325 × 320 mm H2S 340 × 320 mm A custom bed size option is also available for any other setup. What you can draw: Text three modes: single-stroke plotter font (looks like real handwriting), your own custom handwriting (draw each letter yourself, up to 5 versions per letter for variety so repeating letters never look identical), or filled outline using any of 13 fonts Shapes square, circle, triangle, star, line, with optional hatch fill Freehand draw directly on the bed preview with your mouse or stylus Images drop any photo or logo, adjust the threshold and line density, and convert it to plotted lines 3MF import drop a Bambu Lab .3mf file and BambuPlot extracts the 3D geometry and renders the top-down footprint as plottable paths, in either vector outline or hatch-fill mode What you need A Bambu Lab printer or anything else that takes gcode A pen holder that mounts on your toolhead (search MakerWorld or Printables for your specific model many different designs exist.) (I used this one: https://makerworld.com/models/2886015?appSharePlatform=copy ) A ballpoint pen that fits your holder Paper to draw on, attached to the bed (see bed preparation below) A way to get pure gcode on your printer (USB stick/microsd) Bed preparation protecting your print surface This is important. The pen tip will press directly down onto whatever is on your bed. Printing on bare paper placed directly on a softer printing bed can cause damage, especially with a stiff pen or too much Z pressure. My recommendation: place an old flat PEI sheet (Like mine from my old ender 3 v2), a thin sheet of plastic such as a folder cover or binder sheet, or any similarly flat, smooth piece of thin plastic underneath the paper. This gives the paper a firm, even surface to rest on and takes any wear from the pen instead of your actual print bed. An old or scratched PEI sheet you no longer use for printing is perfect for this. Attaching the paper: I use small magnets placed along the edges to hold the paper flat and in position they are quick to place, leave no residue, and hold very reliably. Other options that work fine include masking tape or binder clips on the edges. Whatever you use, make sure the paper is completely flat with no bubbles or lifted corners, as any unevenness will cause the pen pressure to vary across the drawing. How to download and open BambuPlot Go to : https://joep648.github.io/BambuPlot/bambuplot-v1.0.1.html to use it online. or Download the bambuplot.html file from: https://github.com/Joep648/BambuPlot/tree/main Open it with any modern browser (Firefox recommended for best performance Chrome and Edge work fine too, but Firefox handles large designs more smoothly) That is it no installation, no internet needed after that Step-by-step: from design to plot Step 1 Select your printer In the top bar, choose your printer model from the dropdown. The bed preview updates to the correct size. This ensures your G-code coordinates match your actual print surface. Step 2 Add content to the bed Use the tabs on the left panel: Text tab type your text, choose a style (single-stroke is best for plotting), adjust letter spacing and line spacing, then click Add text to bed Shapes tab pick a shape and click Add shape to bed . Enable Filled to get hatch-fill lines inside the shape Image tab click the drop zone or drag an image in. Adjust the threshold slider until the preview looks like clean black lines on white, then click Convert & add to bed . High-contrast line art like the included boat image gives the best results 3MF tab drag a .3mf file onto the drop zone. Choose Vector outline for a clean single-stroke contour of the model, or Top-down silhouette for a hatch-filled footprint Freehand in the Shapes tab, click Draw directly on bed and sketch with your mouse Step 3 Position and size your content Once an item appears on the bed preview: Drag the body of the item to move it Drag a corner handle to scale it the line density automatically recalculates to stay consistent at the new size Drag the white circle above the item to rotate it Use the Layers tab to show/hide, duplicate, or delete items Step 4 Configure pen settings Go to the Pen tab and set: Setting What it does Suggested starting value Z draw How far down the pen tip presses 0.5 mm Z lift How high the pen lifts between strokes 8 mm Draw feed Speed while drawing 1500 mm/min Travel feed Speed while moving between strokes 6000 mm/min Z move feed Speed of Z moves 600 mm/min Pen settle time Dwell after each Z move to prevent stray marks 120 ms These values are starting points every pen holder and pen combination is different. Adjust Z draw until the pen just barely touches the paper with light pressure. Step 5 Generate and download the G-code Click Generate G-code in the right panel. The code appears in the preview (large designs only show the first few thousand lines the full file is always in the download). Click the ⭳ button to download the .gcode file. Step 6 Send to the printer and plot My personal workflow: Home the printer manually via the touchscreen or Bambu Studio After homing, clip the pen holder onto the toolhead with the pen inserted Place your protective plastic sheet on the bed, lay the paper on top, and secure it with magnets, tape, or clips Start the file with in bambuplot Home all axes (G28) at start option turned off Always do a dry run first: temporarily raise the Z draw value by 5–10 mm so the pen stays off the paper, and watch the full motion to confirm the design lands in the right place before doing a real plot Alternative workflow using the dwell option: The Dwell after homing checkbox in the Pen tab inserts a G4 S30 command (a timed pause) after the G28 home command, giving you time to clip the pen on before plotting starts. This feature is experimental and untested I have not personally used it this way. Bambu printers do not support the standard M0 unconditional pause command, so a timed dwell is used as a workaround. If you try it, set the duration long enough to comfortably attach the pen holder (60 seconds or more). Tips for best results Use the right paper smooth, slightly heavier paper works best. Thin paper can wrinkle from pen pressure Ballpoint pens are the most reliable. Felt-tips can bleed on paper and dry out if the pen sits in one spot for too long Start with a short test plot a small shape first to calibrate your Z height before committing to a full design Line density matters lower density (higher number on the slider) = fewer lines = faster plot and less ink bleed. Higher density looks more solid but takes much longer to plot The settle time setting (default 120 ms) adds a brief pause after every pen up/down move. This is the main fix for random stray lines on the paper if you see faint marks between strokes, increase it to 150–250 ms Mirror X or Y if your plot comes out flipped Saving your settings In the Pen tab, click Save profile + handwriting to file to save all your pen settings, printer choice, and your custom drawn handwriting alphabet to a single .json file. Load it again any time even on a different device with the load button. Questions, problems, and ideas for future versions If something does not work, you have a question about the setup, or you just want to share your results feel free to leave a comment on this MakerWorld page or send me a message directly through MakerWorld. I am happy to help where I can, though keep in mind this is a hobby project and responses may not always be instant. If you have ideas for features you would like to see in a future version, I would love to hear them. BambuPlot is actively being worked on and new features get added regularly. Things on the radar include better SVG import, more letter styles, and improved multi-layer support. If there is something specific you need for your use case, suggest it in the comments the best ideas from the community are what shape where this goes next. BambuPlot is a fan-made tool and is not affiliated with Bambu Lab. Pen holder designs are not included search MakerWorld or Printables for a mount that fits your specific printer model. Always run a dry pass before plotting on good paper. Use at your own risk.

model_name: True Spring Filament Clip ⧸ Tangle Free Storage
description: A filament clip that solves the three most common problems of traditional filament clips. Plastic Fatigue Most filament clips rely on a printed flex geometry to generate clamping force. Repeated use and elevated drying temperatures gradually reduce the clamping force as the plastic permanently deforms. True Spring Solution The clamping force is generated by a real steel compression spring. The printed parts only guide the movement. No Plastic Fatigue. Constant tension. Filament Stress Many filament clips bend the filament sharply by securing it through spool holes or around the spool rim. Brittle materials may break after long term storage. True Spring Solution The filament is secured close to the spool core with a large bending radius, minimizing unnecessary stress while keeping the filament securely retained. Tangle Risk Some clips secure the filament directly to the wound filament. This can increase the risk of accidental tangles when the spool is handled carelessly. True Spring Solution The filament is retained independently of the wound filament. Nothing is attached to the filament winding itself. Hardware The clip uses two inexpensive compression springs. You can either use a compatible spring from the BOM or simply try the spring from an old ballpoint pen. Many common pen springs fit perfectly. No screws. No glue. No tools. Everything simply snaps together. Printer Tolerance Test Every printer and every filament behaves slightly differently. Since this model relies on precisely fitting moving parts, I strongly recommend printing the Printer Tolerance Test first. The test consists of one plunger and six labeled test sockets with clearances of 0.05 mm , 0.10 mm , 0.15 mm , 0.20 mm , 0.25 mm and 0.30 mm . The correct fit should move smoothly with minimal friction while having as little play as possible. Don't feel like running the calibration? Simply print Print Plate 1 (0.15 mm clearance) . It provides a good fit for most printers and materials. Temperature Testing Successfully tested after 24 hours of continuous filament drying: PETG - 45 °C ASA - 65 °C ASA - 80 °C PC - 85 °C For comparison, I tested a popular Flexi Filament Clip under identical print settings, using the same material and identical drying conditions. After 24 hours at the respective drying temperatures, the flex geometry had permanently deformed and the remaining clamping force was no longer sufficient for reliable reuse. If you have ever dried filament while using this type of clip, you probably know exactly what I mean. Recommended Materials PETG works perfectly for everyday use. For frequent filament drying or elevated temperatures I recommend ASA or PC . Assembly Printed parts and two compression springs. Insert the filament clamps. Insert the springs. Insert the Double Plunger and press firmly. Finished, enjoy.

So funny story. I love printing things. Therefore I have a lot of plastic waste from poop to supports etc…. A while ago my husband says “your going to need a dumpster for all that plastic”. Then my neighbor noticed the several bags of plastic “poop” I have and said the exact thing. And only when my nephew comes over and says the same thing once again I thought to myself, I need to make a little dumpster to catch all the poop my printer makes. I pictured the Home Alone 2 movie where the house Kevin rigs up has a chute outside the window going into a dumpster. So that's where the idea for project came from. There are tons of “poop” bins and baskets for the other printers but I wanted to make one for my new Bambu Lab A2L printer. She's a beast. Very detailed and prints well. I love it. It does shake the house though being a large sized bed slinger. I have been printing on silent mode to calm it down in most cases. This took me a week to create. A little longer than usual but I needed to get the tolerances perfecta. My main goal was to make it easy and reliable to print. That was the challenge. I tried several ways to get the chute to print as one piece but it never worked out. So clip or bracket that connects to the printer is separate and has to be glued to the chute. I did make a connection socket so the two fit together perfectly so all is needed is a drop of cyanoacrylate glue (Super Glue) or something similar on each edge of the connection opening and hold it in place for the appropriate time (depending on your glue). I have printed 19 sets of the chute and bracket and glued them together successfully with no problem. Supports were absolutely necessary to accomplish my goal. I tried to keep the settings simple but tweaked the settings like the top and bottom Z distance, speed etc… to get dumpster and chute to come out clean. Just be sure to keep my settings. You can add to them if you please but it wont be necessary as you can tell by my photos. I have had several people that don't have a printer me to print them one just because they wanted the cute little bin. I have even been changing the sizes per their requests. The dumpster itself is scalable and you can make a smaller or larger one depending on your needs. I am sure it will have many uses. This is the A2L model version. I created this first due to the need for a way to control the filament purge waste or “Poo” . Upon request I made a clip portion that fits the A1 and A1 Mini printers. All the A1 series poo cute parts are now on the same page. You can find them here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/3073625-poo-chute-dumpster-for-all-a-series Thank you ahead of time and please enjoy. Have a nice day.

Durch die verschiedenen Überhänge, Aussparungen, Brücken und Kontaktflächen eignet sich der Test hervorragend, um die Druckqualität unterschiedlicher Materialkombinationen zu vergleichen und optimale Einstellungen für saubere Support-Oberflächen zu finden. Was wird getestet? Oberflächenqualität über Supportstrukturen Maßhaltigkeit kritischer Geometrien Qualität von Überhängen und Brücken Trennbarkeit der Supports Einfluss verschiedener Interface-Materialien Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch Vorteile von Multi-Material Supports Durch die Verwendung eines separaten Support-Interface-Materials lassen sich deutlich sauberere Unterseiten und Kontaktflächen erzielen als mit Supports aus dem gleichen Material. Besonders bei anspruchsvollen Überhängen können dadurch: glattere Oberflächen bessere Maßhaltigkeit weniger Nacharbeit einfachere Supportentfernung erreicht werden. Empfohlene Druckvarianten Variante 1 – Nur Support-Interface in anderem Material (empfohlen) Hier wird das Modell und die eigentlichen Supportstrukturen mit dem Hauptmaterial gedruckt. Lediglich die Support-Schnittstellen (Support Interface Layers) werden mit einem zweiten Material erzeugt. Beispiel: Modell: PETG Supports: PETG Support Interface: PLA Diese Methode bietet in der Regel das beste Verhältnis aus Druckqualität, Materialverbrauch und Druckzeit. Variante 2 – Komplette Supports in anderem Material Alternativ können sowohl die Supportstrukturen als auch die Support-Schnittstellen vollständig aus einem zweiten Material gedruckt werden. Beispiel: Modell: PETG Supports + Interface: PLA Diese Variante kann die Trennbarkeit weiter verbessern, erhöht jedoch den Materialwechsel erheblich. Wichtig: Durch die vielen Werkzeugwechsel zwischen den Materialien verlängert sich die Druckzeit deutlich und es entsteht zusätzlicher Materialabfall durch Spülvorgänge. description: AMS HT mount X2D/P2S - Standalone and AMS Flipper - V2 This is my brand new and completely (re)built and revamped mount for the AMS HT for X2D/P2S printer frames that can now be used either standalone with the printer by attaching it directly to the printer frame on the back, or with an AMS Flipper from @ Jakob_K_Design attached to the back and integrating with the AMS Flipper handle. The model has been built from the ground up, taking prior experience and designing a fully modular, easy to print frame of the mount that is almost support free for printing, and assembled together using standard hardware forming a strong base for the AMS HT that sits even horizontally with the top of the printer to be side by side with an AMS Pro 2 on top of the printer. The mount can also be extended with the new Filament Track Switch to allow dynamic inputs for the extruders. Core features of the mount The AMS HT mount conveniently sits on the side, flush with the top of the printer, allowing installation of an AMS Pro 2 or other Risers on top of the printer without interference. You can choose between installing the mount directly to the printer frame, or if you are using an AMS Flipper, to the Flipper handle, using the provided compatible bracket. AMS HT mount allowing full view of the side window with minimal obstruction Some highlights of the model: Strong triangular brackets, balancing strength and material use to mount the AMS HT to the side of the X2D/P2S printer frame Full view of the side window below the AMS HT with minimal obstruction Side bracket provides extra strength and vibration dampening from the printer for the front side of the mount Easy to print flat on the bed with no supports needed for the frame and only minimal supports required for the interfacing slots for precision Easy assembly by slotting the four (4) parts of the mount together using standard hardware of M3 screws and square nuts for a strong hold Can either be used: Directly with the printer using the Standalone main bracket or using the AMS Flipper compatible main bracket which slots around the AMS Flipper handle The mount allows access to the l inear rail belt tensioning ports for maintenance The model print profile has been fine tuned for strength, optimizing extrusion settings to maximize strength and limit support interface swaps and harnessing the power of the X2D dual nozzle system. The print profile is optimized to be printed using the X2D using PETG for the frame, with PLA as support interface support layer for crisp results and easy support removal. Note: As the printer frame is shared between the X2D and the P2S, if printing using the P2S, you will have a few nozzle swaps for the interface layers, but they are minimized to just a few, so it shouldn't affect print time dramatically. NOTE: Please be careful with resetting settings, they have been carefully set to have repeatable successful prints and hold to the print bed. Optional Add-on : Designed to be compatible with my X2D Filament Track Switch mount by having a cutout reserved for the mount and utilizing triangles for chord organization. Optional Add-on: Cable organizer using the triangle brackets. Upon request by another user, I designed another add-on to make the cable organization of the 6-pin cable even neater using a figure-8 cable organizer loop that snap-fits into one of the triangle brackets and can be mounted either vertically or horizontally depending on your preference. Hardware required for assembly and installation You will need a few types of M3 Socket Head Screws and thin M3 square nuts: 7x Socket Head Screw M3x30mm (DIN 912) - Bambu Lab store part AA042 x2 3x Socket Head Screw M3x30mm for the mount assembly 4x Socket Head Screw M3x30mm for the installation to the X2D/P2S printer frame 2x Socket Head Screw M3x20mm (DIN 912) - Bambu Lab store part AA040 x1 5x Socket Head Screw M3x10mm (DIN 912) - Bambu Lab store part AA159 x1 10x thin M3 square nuts (DIN 562, ≤2mm height) - Bambu Lab store part AB015 x1 Optional: If you plan to install the Cable organizer you will also need 4x size 8x3mm round magnets (Bambu Lab store part CA008 x1) for the mount in the frame (and another 4x for the organizer itself ) Assembly The assembly is fairly simple and requires just a few standard hardware M3 screws and square nuts, providing a strong hold. You can follow the below step by step instructions, or follow the annotated images for location of screws, nuts and (optional) magnets. As the mount sits right next to the printer frame, for durability the model should be printed using PETG - so dry your filament prior to use! - you want to avoid stringing, warping or lifting off the bed. Print the four (4) parts - To help avoid any warping, you may want to reduce the Aux Fan speed to avoid spot cooling, which can contribute to lifting of large prints, or consider installing an Aux Fan deflector . Print the Main Bracket Pick either the Standalone Main Bracket if you want to install the mount directly to the printer frame or pick the AMS Flipper compatible Main Bracket if you are using the Flipper to mount the bracket to the Flipper Handle Print the Side Bracket for strong support of the mount and provide dampening to limit vibrations from the printer Print the Top Front Mount Bracket that holds the AMS HT and interfaces with the back and side brackets Print the Top Back Mount Bracket that holds the AMS HT and interfaces with the front and main brackets Print optional add-ons as desired: (Optional): Print the Filament Track Switch add-on to mount the Filament Track Switch to the frame over the AMS Flipper Handle and into the AMS HT side mount frame (Optional): Print the Cable Organizer add-on for extra neat organization of the 6-pin cable connecting to the AMS HT Annotated location of mounting hardware: Step by Step instructions: Connect the Top Front and Back brackets through their connecting interface Install two (2) thin M3 square nuts into the inside slots on both left and right side of the top arms Screw two (2 ) socket head screws M3x10mm length from the outside through each of the two arms to connect to the nuts to lock the front and back brackets together Slot the assembled Top Bracket into the Main Bracket through the four trapezoid interface arms note this is a precise interface with 0.15mm tolerances, so check that your printer printed the interfacing arms without any blobs or give them a light sand on the edges as needed Make sure the interface arms are aligned straight and push down using the back of your palm until the top and main brackets are flush - if things are tight and get stuck, a light sideways wiggle can help to loosen things Slot the Side Bracket into the Main Bracket through the two trapezoid interface arms using the same technique Install thin square nuts M3 in all remaining slots, sliding them to their embedded depths: One (1) - Inside of the Top Back bracket One (1) - Upper side of the Top Front bracket Two (2) - Inside of the Side bracket Two (2) - Sunk into the two slots on the back of the Main bracket - use a thin long screwdriver or pliers to push them into place Screw one (1) M3x10mm socket head screw from the bottom of the side bracket through the front bracket , watching until the screw surfaces through the square nut and locks the two parts together Screw two (2) M3x20mm socket head screws from the top of the Main Bracket through the interface arms, meeting the sunk square nuts Screw three (3) M3x30mm socket head screws from the back of the Main Bracket into the remaining holes connecting the Main and Top bracket with one (1) and the Main and Side bracket with two (2) screws (Optional) Install four (4) size 8x3mm round magnets into the holes on the back of the Main Bracket if you plan on installing the optional Cable Organizer. Installation Directly to the printer Remove the four (4) screws from the left backside of the X2D/P2S printer frame Remove the external spool holder mount if it is currently installed at the top and move it tothe bottom of the printer Attach two (2) M3x30mm socket head screws to the top of the mount and two to the bottom of the mounting holes aligning them with the four holes from which you removed the screws Using AMS Flipper Lift the left side (from the back) AMS Flipper Handle up and clip the mount into the handle - this should sit evenly almost flush on both sides -the mount will minimally protrude prior to tightening of the screws to create a counter clamping force to the AMS Flipper Handle to ensure a strong tight fit, but it will still allow the Flipper Handle to sit flush against the printer frame once aligned correctly as pictured below. Lower the Handle onto the printer and align the top and bottom evenly. A small gap before tightening the screws is ok but it should only be 1-2mm and be even between the top and bottom of the handle. If mount was correctly clicked into the handle and the handle sits even as shown above, screw the four (4) M3x30mm socket head screws onto the printer frame. I recommend starting with one of the bottom screws, but without fully tightening it, and then moving to the top and then finishing the rest of the screws and tightening things into place. Check that the flush fit hasn't shifted in case you tightened one screw before alignment was locked into place. The AMS HT mount and the top and bottom of the AMS Flipper handle should sit basically flush with the printer if the AMS HT side mount was clicked into place together correctly once everything is tightened as shown below: If things don't sit flush correctly, repeat Step 1-3, check the fit and try again until the mount is properly set in the center of the handle, resulting in a flush fit. If this is your initial installation of the AMS Flipper, follow the rest of the AMS Flipper installation instructions to finish installation of your AMS Flipper. Install optional add-ons Optional: Install the Filament Track Switch mount . Utilize the triangle cutout in the frame or use the cable organizer to store and tuck away the cords of the AMS HT: If you installed the External Spool holder on the bottom of the printer frame, you could route the power chord of the AMS HT through the triangle frame and down and using a cable tie (ideally a good quality Velcro one) attach the chord to the external spool holder for a clean installation. Optional: Install the Cable Organizer for AMS HT side-mount to organize the 6-pin cable using a neat figure-8 loop Done, enjoy easy access to your AMS HT on your X2D/P2S printer. Print Settings Supports: yes, with top interface layer enabled for smooth finish on supported portions Only the interface arms and the cutout for the linear rail adjustment screws require supports Brim: no Layer Height: 0.20mm Infill: 25 % cubic for strength Walls: 2 Print orientation: Flat on the bed Material: Parts: Dry PETG for strength and temperature resistance due to the close proximity to the printer. Loaded into Primary (left) nozzle Support Interface: PLA or specific support material to make removal easy (PLA won't bond strongly with PETG, so removal is easy, but the bond is strong enough for print support and using just interface layer reduces nozzle swaps). Loaded into Aux (right) nozzle if printed on X2D

description: This is a remixed model originally created by the very talented morph91 . Original model link: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2749412-bc-250-gaming-pc-case-mk-ultra-uno . I'm naming this model the MK Ultra Uno Plus : ) Case Highlights: Can be printed in only 3 plates with less than 600g of filament Tool-less design (no screws required) Fits the FSP500-30AS, Apevia ITX flex, and Metalfish flex PSUs Customizable front plates Ability to fit 40 & 50 mm fans on rear Internal clips to attach both halves of case together securely & internal psu lock to securely hold psu in place without external latch Heatsink mod (stick on heatsinks) to help improve thermals Important Considerations: There are two different versions of the fan shroud. One is the exact same as the original, the other is a modified version that allows active airflow to flow to stick on heatsinks that I personally made for my build. You can reference the assembly instructions for photos. Please make sure you only print the plate relevant for your build! Both the apevia and metalfish variants of the back case contain one less internal clip/latch due to space constraints. So these variants may be slightly less rigid when the two case halves are put together The internal psu lock was created specfically for the FSP500-30AS variant. It might fit the apevia variant, but will most likely not fit the metalfish variant. If someone prints either version, I'm more than happy to create a working psu lock for these versions. I just need accurate measurements and someone to test any prototypes. If you're interested then leave a comment/DM me : ) If anyone ends up printing the apevia or metalfish variants, please let me know if anything needs to be adjusted (besides the internal psu lock)! I used morph91 's measurements for the metalfish variant and also lolheyaj 's measurements for the apevia variant, since I do not personally own either of those psus. Also, as a temporary solution for the internal psu lock issue - you could probably use glue to keep the psu secure in the case as a temporary measure. If you have a different flex psu, and can take some accurate measurements for me - I am more than willing to create new versions to suit your psu (as long as dimensions fit the case)! : ) Expected Thermals: Thermals may vary slightly, given differences in thermal paste and depending whether you use the stick on heatsinks like I did. Also depending on 24CU vs 40CU, fan curves, overclock, undervolts, etc. For reference here's my configuration: GPU: 40CU 2000MHz @940mV (+16CU and +500 MHz from stock) CPU: 3800MHz @1060mV (+300MHz from stock) And here are some max temps from a couple games @1080p: My Part List: BC250 PSU (fsp500-30as, apevia itx flex, or metalfish flex) https://a.co/d/0gOMs9rW black petg https://a.co/d/04eTZ6sm for the two brown pla's from this bundle for my fake wood texture front panels makerworld.com/en/models/2527214-bc-250-scooper fin scooper to straighten fins https://a.co/d/0hZ28ifs for 12mm latching button (you may need a wire stripper, wire crimper, and dupont connectors if you copy me 1:1) https://a.co/d/0jdT5jNV arctic p12 pro pst https://a.co/d/0iLAR7Ty arctic mx-4 thermal paste (optional) https://a.co/d/063cMg66 noctua NF-A4x20 (optional) https://a.co/d/00RnzoEo stick on heatsinks, I bought 2 of these kits and used 3 out of the 4 heatsinks (optional) This looks to be a cheaper alternative: https://a.co/d/038s6cPO - it would be the same size as what I used, but as one large piece instead. Based on reviews, it looks like a thermal pad of some sort is already preapplied. If you end up buying this one, let me know how it fits! (optional) https://a.co/d/066uYDJ8 rubber anti vibration screws used to mount noctua 40mm fan Print Instructions: Print the main case components in PETG, and dry filament for 8 hours before printing (reduces stringing). Make sure to print only one of the fan shroud plates. For more information read the important considerations at the top. If you want to make your front panel have the fake wood texture like mine, then use this as a modifier: https://makerworld.com/en/models/1492898-wood-grain-modifier-add-wood-grain-to-any-models?from=search#profileId-1560821 . You can print the front panels in PLA. I recommend using a 0.2mm nozzle if you're doing the wood texture like I did. If you are downloading the model to modify or use with a different slicer (and not bambu studio), then make sure to paint a straight line seam on the bottom part of back half of the case. This helps reduce VFAs: Assembly Instructions: Take off the IO shield and the small bracket next to cmos battery Use the fin scooper to straighten the fins underneath where the fan shroud is gonna go. After straightening the fins, use an air duster to make sure any debris is blown off. Also if you haven't already, repaste the chip! Attach fan (recommend arctic p12 pro pst) with pins to fan shroud. Then attach fan shroud to pcb. Make sure the two small latches are pushed as far up as possible (in pic below you can see the one latch is in the corner of the pcb). Optionally here, if you have the stick on heatsinks (120x40x20mm), you can stick them right next to the fan slit. Doing this mod helped my ingame temps by 3-7C. VERY IMPORTANT NOTE: If you do not have/don't plan to use stick on heatsinks print the plate with the original fan shroud instead! Put PSU into back half of case: Add psu lock on left side (currently only known compatible for fsp500-30as): Mount any 40mm fans now (both screws or rubber mounts work): Slide bc250 on alu backplate onto the back half of case. Plug in exhaust fan to the Y splitter of main fan. Plug in the 8 pin power cable: (optional) Place any lower custom front panels on now before you install your 12mm button (This step is for FSP500-30AS psu, idk what pins to short for apevia/metalfish psus but you can probably find out on reddit) Plug in latching button to PS_ON and GND. I crimped the wires into two male dupont connectors and put them in a 2pin housing. I slightly have to bend the metal pins to fit into the psu which creates enough friction where the pins don't fall out. There's probably a better solution for this… Attach front half of case, and slide until both halves attach together. Enjoy!
