description: The faint hum of the short dagger vibrates through the cave, mixing with the low roar of alien wind that howls through the rock cracks 🪨. Koren, a veteran smuggler who has wandered the outer galactic rim for 12 years, never thought he would encounter something that cannot be explained by any existing astrophysics data 📡. His navigation system was struck by a sudden solar storm 72 hours ago, forcing him to crash land on this unmarked planet that does not appear in any galaxy public or black market star map. His three crew members all got wrapped by the growing root-like rock tissue when they tried to touch the glowing cave wall, turning into part of the cave in less than ten minutes. He ran all the way to this core cave, only to find this dagger half embedded in the central stone, with a dreamy pink-blue gradient, twisted branch handle wrapping a tiny round star core 🌟. When he got close, he could feel the tiny gravitational pull from the dagger, dragging his consciousness to connect with the remnant information left in the core. He saw the war that broke out a million years ago: the native civilization of this planet fought against the machine legion that came to plunder the planet's core energy, they chose to seal the dying star core into the dagger made of their own life tissue, dragged the whole legion into this cave, and buried everything here to stop the legion from spreading to other star systems 🛸. Now this dagger wakes up because of the new outsider, waiting for a new carrier to take the core out, or join the guardian of this cave forever. Koren tries to pull his hand back from the blade, but his boots have been firmly held by the growing branch, the same pink blue light is slowly climbing up his leg 🔹. The whispers of his old crew can be heard behind him, he cannot tell whether he is the chosen messenger or just the next prey for this ancient guardian. He tightens his grip on the dagger, waiting for what will happen next ✨.

description: 一、模型设计概述 本模型基于《我的世界》游戏内二维像素剑造型进行3D重构。区别于仅做平面拉伸的同类模型，该设计利用高低落差的阶梯式结构，塑造出三维立体的体素浮雕质感。在无需多色打印的条件下，依然可通过光影呈现丰富的层次感。 剑柄部分针对握持的人体工学进行了重新设计。参考游戏内官方3D化逻辑，将原二维扁平剑柄进行90度旋转并合并重组，消除冗余块面，使握把具备真实的立体体积和圆润的握持手感。剑柄底部设计有贯穿的镂空结构，可穿入挂绳，用于悬挂或作为背包挂饰。 二、打印与组装参数 文件拆分 ：剑身与剑柄已完成分体处理，默认分布在1-2两盘，可分开独立打印。 公差与组装 ：经多重精度测试，公差控制精准。装配预期为无胶水拼装（摩擦力卡合结构），无需额外使用粘合剂。 打印设置测试 ：内部已进行多组打印参数实测，以保障最佳打印质量。 三、耗材适配与操作提示 多色与单色适配 ：模型未预设固定配色，任何基础色彩耗材均可直接打印。纯色打印即可凸显像素浮雕质感；若配备多色打印系统（如AMS），或具备后期手涂上色能力，由于全模型皆为方块构造，表面涂装和分色操作非常简便，可根据游戏原作色彩自行调配。 耗材翘边预警 ：模型默认未在剑身部分添加辅助裙边（Brim）。若使用PETG或ABS等收缩率较高的材料，打印时 必须 在切片软件中手动开启裙边功能，否则极易发生翘边；若使用PLA材料，则无需额外处理。 打印尺寸限制 ：针对A1 mini 等较小打印平台的机器，无法直接打印原比例尺寸模型，可通过切片软件等比缩小后输出缩小版本。 四、文件开源与兼容性说明 本模型同步提供 STEP 格式开源文件，可在网页端下载。用户可将其导入任意CAD软件中进行结构修改，用于创作个人二次开发版本。 注意 ：此STEP文件暂无法在 Bambu Studio 切片软件中直接打开。如需在常见切片软件中预览和打印，请直接下载模型提供的 STL 格式文件。

description: This spearhead model is inspired by the famous Spear of King Fuchai of Wu (吴王夫差矛) . If you're interested in the history behind the original artifact, you can read about it on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spear_of_Fuchai The spearhead is modeled at approximately the same size as the original artifact and is just over 300 mm long. Since it exceeds the printable height of many printers, it is split into two pieces that are joined with the included connector. I recommend printing one spearhead piece per build plate, even though it may be tempting to place both pieces on the same plate. There are two reasons for this: Print stability – The spearhead is very thin and tall. When both pieces are printed side by side, the nozzle may strike one of them while traveling between parts, causing a print failure. (I learned this the hard way.) If you decide to print both at once, place them end-to-end (like - -) rather than side-by-side (like =) to reduce the chance of collisions. Surface finish – I found that the surface texture is noticeably smoother when only a single part is printed on the build plate. Printing multiple parts at once produced a slightly different finish. This may depend on your filament or printer, but for the best-looking result, I recommend printing the pieces individually. The spearhead shown in the photos was printed using ERYONE Gold Silk PLA at a 0.16 mm layer height. The gold color is intentional —newly cast bronze weapons had a golden appearance.The greenish appearance of the surviving artifact is due to the patina formed during more than two thousand years of corrosion. The pole is designed as 25 mm in diameter and is divided into 150 mm (approximately 6 in) sections. Each section uses M20 × 1.5 threads, allowing you to print as many sections as needed and screw them together to create a spear of your desired length. I printed the pole sections with Fuzzy Skin enabled to create a nice visual contrast with the smooth, polished spearhead. The pommel completes the assembly. To avoid support, a threaded connector was included and the pommel can be threaded onto the end of the pole using that connector. Printing Notes Supports is required for the lower spearhead section only. The upper spearhead section, pole sections, connector, and pommel print without supports. For maximum strength, glue the two spearhead halves together after inserting the connector. Note: The cover image was created using AI.

description: Cosplay Caine the Ring Master from The Amazing Digital Circus (TADC) Printed in white PETG, with 2 walls, 2% lightning infill (basically hollow) to make it was light as possible. These files are for printing the teeth/jaws. They're split into 3 segments for each jaw; front, left, and right. And should fit on an Ender 3, or any 220 printbed or larger. The segments dovetail together, but I still recommend glue or plastic welding for the strongest attachment possible. It is designed to clip onto the brim of a baseball cap, and the aliceband isn't meant to sit it normally would on your head, but add better stability to the brim, because the center of gravity is farther forward than you would expect. I ultimately glued some nickels to the back to bring the center of gravity farther back for balance. However, if I were to do it again, I would add strategic infill to the farthest back section (in the slicer) for counterweight and to reinforce the clip connector holes, which I broke. I also recommend adding springs to the back of the jaws to space them apart, and keep them from hitting each other. I played around with various 3D printed springs, which I included. However, I ultimately broke the connectors while switching them, and just 3D printed a straight, flat rectangle piece that I plastic welded to them. Really, anything will work, as long as you attach something to them to keep them apart. I also recommend connecting the front of the jaws using fishing line. I included some small holes where fishing line may be attached, however they came out too small in my print, perhaps do to my printer settings in the slicer. I ultimately tied the fishing line around the seems where the segments meet, where it would be completely hidden. I would also recommend using a touch of hot glue on the knots, to absolutely make sure they stay. And of course you can adjust the length to choose how open the mouth hangs open, just make sure both lines are the same length. I choose to space them so that the bottom jaw doesn't rest on my shoulders, so it all turns with my head, but it also closes if I shrug my shoulders. For my cosplay, I used contact cement to glue a large stripe of red craft foam around the "gums" for texture and to hide the seams, and then I sealed it with Mod Podge for toughness and luster. A hair dryer can also be used to help shrink wrap the foam to the print, but be careful not to let the plastic get too hot or it could warp. I just painted the inside gums red, since they're less visible, and I was very concerned about weight since I was going to be wear it for long hours.
